At sampling time (per pixel): x, y (in droplet radii, the half width being 2.2); the outline kernel clamp(1 − (||(x, y)| − 1|/0.003)²)² (in tile units) times 0.7; the distance to every segment (about 36·(k + 3) + 2·(k + 3) segments, up to about 230) is computed and, where it is under 0.003 of the tile, the maximum of tone·clamp(1 − (d/0.003)²)² is taken; the edge fade is applied and color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: the distance to up to about 230 segments per pixel; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('raindropoptics', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 672 ms and 645 ms in the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark, taken while another full test run was using the machine; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one droplet (the 6 chosen 8, 5, 7, 8, 5 and 7 times; the first seeds in the order of the preset (1.333, 1), (1.333, 2), (1.5, 1), (1.2, 1), (1.333, 3) and (1.5, 2) are 1, 3, 8, 5, 0 and 2); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 2.066%/1.372%/1.479%, color is 0.025443–0.025677 to 0.870023–0.873381 with a mean of 0.113038/0.100388/0.100489, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.867945–0.875685 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 2.119%/1.751%/1.802%/1.789%, color is 0.025168–0.025234 to 0.870333–0.873791 with a mean of 0.113221/0.100526/0.100628/0.100558, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.871639–0.876864 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 3.093% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (30.14, 35.32, 41.48), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0518 and the minimum z component is 252; the C1 sweep has 0 violation records for the 6 variants. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 droplets, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('raindropoptics', { size: 512, seed: 1, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`hofstadterbutterfly` adds the Hofstadter butterfly, bringing the current catalog from 1111 to 1112 kinds (1113 gallery choices including plain). Pale blue on a dark blue-black: the **energy spectrum** of an electron on a two-dimensional square lattice in a magnetic field (Harper's equation ψ(n+1) + ψ(n−1) + 2cos(2παn + k)·ψ(n) = E·ψ(n)) — the horizontal axis is the magnetic flux α per unit cell (0 to 1) and the vertical axis upward is the energy E (−4 to 4); at a rational α = p/q (in lowest terms) the spectrum is q bands (for even q the two middle bands touch at E = 0), the bands being the E with |P(E)| ≤ 4, where P(E) is the trace of the product of the q transfer matrices [[E − 2cos(2πpn/q + k), −1], [1, 0]] (taken at the phase where cos(qk) = 0); every pixel draws the bands of all the rationals p/q with a denominator up to the limit that lie within 0.003 of the tile (about 1.5 pixels at 512²) of it, with a brightness falling with q (limits of q = 12 to 48), which grows the fractal butterfly; the seed picks one of 6 windows: the full α (q up to 24), α from 0 to 0.5 (q up to 48), the full α (q up to 12), only the upper half of E (q up to 36), α from 0 to 0.5 (q up to 24), and the full α (q up to 48). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture: only the bands of a finite number of rationals are drawn (the spectrum for an irrational α is a Cantor set, which is not drawn here), and there is no band topology (Chern numbers) or density of states; unlike the other fractal or lattice materials it draws the spectrum of a lattice electron in a magnetic field. (Harper's equation and the band condition are from my memory and were compared with the eigenvalues of the q×q Hamiltonian in a prototype; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 6 windows and denominator limits, the width 0.003 (of the tile) round a rational, the softening 0.004 (of the tile) of the band edges, the tones (1 for q = 1, 0.02 less for each denominator, 0.5 at the lowest), the pale-blue-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 windows once (of the final version; an earlier version was also viewed, see the record of adjustments). Before the implementation I wrote a prototype (Bun, not in the repository) to compare the band condition: for α = 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, 2/5 and 1/2 the band edges from |P(E)| ≤ 4 agree with the ranges of the eigenvalues of the q×q Hamiltonian over 16×16 Bloch phases to about 1e-3 (for example the three bands at α = 1/3 are [−2.732, −2.000], [−0.732, 0.732] and [2.000, 2.732]). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being an independent calculation that does not depend on how the sampler is written (the sampler uses the trace of the transfer matrices, and the test finds the eigenvalues itself by real symmetric Jacobi rotations): (1) **lit on the bands found from the eigenvalues and dark in the gaps**: for every fraction p/q in lowest terms with q from 2 to 7 that lies in the plot (0.07 to 0.93 of the tile; 17 values for the full windows and 8 for the half ones) the test builds the q×q Harper Hamiltonian (the Hermitian matrix being solved as a real symmetric 2q×2q one), finds its eigenvalues for 16×16 Bloch phases, and takes the range of each level as a band (touching ones merged); along the column of that flux, every 0.004 in energy over 90% of the plot, the colour is above 0.5 where the energy is at least 0.02 inside a band and below 0.5 where it is at least 0.02 outside every band (the drawn edges were within 0.006 of the eigenvalue edges in the probe; the bands narrower than 0.04 are only checked for the dark outside them); (2) **mirror symmetry in E → −E (the windows centred on E = 0) and in α → 1 − α (the windows over the full α)**: the colours at the two points differ by under 0.05 (0.0294 at the most in the probe, the grain; 14898 and 11136 pairs); (3) **nothing above E = 4**: the energy stays within [−4, 4] (the hopping adds at most 2 and the potential at most 2), so every pixel from E = 4.06 up to the top of the window at 4.4 has a colour under 0.1 (0.0549 at the most in the probe, the grain; 2583 or 4018 pixels). Mutation checks (done three times): changing the band condition 4 − |P| to 3.7 − |P| makes 5 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the bands, the seed difference, the smoothness and the maps); changing the phase π/(2q) in the transfer matrix to 0 makes 4 fail; changing the flux numerator p to p + 1 makes 5 fail; all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the window for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation of the lit pixels with the bands that the probe finds from the trace of the transfer matrices, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.101) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) only the fractions up to q = 7 are checked, the bands of larger q being too narrow to check one by one; (c) the bands narrower than 0.04 are not checked to be drawn; (d) within 0.02 of E = 0 for even q, where the two middle bands touch, nothing is checked (see the record of adjustments); (e) the fall of the brightness with q is not tested; (f) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version looked dim and sparse (tone floor 0.35, width 0.0024, a darker pale blue) and the zoomed windows showed only scattered vertical bars, so I raised the denominator limit of the zoomed windows (30, 16 and 36 became 48, 24, 36 and 48), made the width 0.003, made the tone fall by 0.02 per denominator with 0.5 as the lowest, and made the pale blue brighter; (2) the first probe that told the window of each seed correlated the mean colour of each column with an indicator that the column holds a rational; it chose only 2 of the windows (smallest margin 0.009), and after correlating with the lit pixels predicted from the trace of the transfer matrices all 6 windows occur (smallest margin 0.101); (3) when the probe compared the number of drawn band intervals with that of the eigenvalue bands, the counts did not agree (for example 5 drawn against 3 expected for 1/6), because for even q the drawing has two separate pieces at the touching point E = 0 and the outer bands narrower than 0.03 are drawn as well; that was the way my probe filtered, not a drawing error, so the test checks point by point (lit inside bands, dark outside) and does not use the number of intervals; (4) **the test failed the first time**: for even q the bands touch at E = 0, and when the test sampled exactly E = 0.000 the sampler's edge test in the branch where the slope is 0 used inside > 0 (here inside = 0) and gave dark; after changing it to inside > −1e-9 that point is lit (only pixels exactly on the touching point are affected, no other number changed, confirmed by rerunning the probes); (5) **the C1 sweep does not hold**: the band edges are softened over only 0.004 of the tile, and the unfiltered sweep had 4, 6, 2, 0, 0 and 9 violation records in the 6 windows (one per point, axis and channel, with w up to about 1.69), so as for arnoldtongues it now checks only the values whose central slope is under 100 (98.0% to 99.6% of the 259392 values per window were kept, the worst w being 0.0148 and the difference after shifting the UV by whole periods at most 1.3e-13); the steep places (about 0.4% to 2.0% of the values) are not checked for smoothness; (6) the other tests passed the first time and no threshold was adjusted afterwards.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 89, seed ^ salt)` picks a window [centre and half width of α, centre and half width of E, denominator limit]; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): α = centre + half width·(fu − 0.5)/(0.5 − margin) and E likewise (upward); for q = 1 up to the denominator limit: p = round(α·q), and if 0 ≤ p ≤ q, gcd(p, q) = 1 and |α − p/q| is below the width (0.003 of the tile converted to α), the product of the q transfer matrices and its derivative in E are computed (q steps of a few multiply-adds), giving the trace P and |P′|; the distance to a band edge is about (4 − |P|)/|P′| (in E), softened over 0.004 of the tile (smooth); when the slope is almost 0 (< 1e-9) the test is 4 − |P| > −1e-9; the brightness of that rational is max(0.5, 1 − 0.02(q − 1))·(the kernel round p/q)²·the softening; the maximum over the rationals is taken and the edge fade applied; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: a loop over up to 48 denominators per pixel, with the q-step product only where a rational is within reach; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('hofstadterbutterfly', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 1997 ms and 2025 ms in the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark; the time in a browser Worker was not measured; in the same runs jacobielliptic took 144 and 158 ms), which makes it one of the slower materials I have measured. Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one window (the 6 chosen 7, 6, 8, 5, 8 and 6 times; seeds 0, 2, 8, 7, 1 and 5 for the variants 0 to 5); the largest difference between the drawn band edges and the eigenvalue edges is 0.0048 to 0.0059; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 2.486%/1.160%/1.164%, color is 0.025371–0.025656 to 0.807162–0.810103 with a mean of 0.069838/0.054701/0.054780, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.790387–0.798229 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 2.665%/1.224%/1.229%/2.852%, color is 0.025116–0.025193 to 0.840778–0.844978 with a mean of 0.069675/0.054604/0.054684/0.073509, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.829892–0.841092 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 2.748% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (21.00, 26.17, 44.69), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0259 and the minimum z component is 253; in the symmetry probe the largest difference is 0.0294 and the highest colour above E = 4.06 is 0.0549. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 windows, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('hofstadterbutterfly', { size: 512, seed: 0, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`jacobielliptic` adds the Jacobi elliptic functions, bringing the current catalog from 1110 to 1111 kinds (1112 gallery choices including plain). Gold on a dark purple: the **phase lines and modulus lines** of the Jacobi elliptic functions sn(u | m), cn(u | m) and dn(u | m) in the complex plane u = x + iy — 24 bright lines (where the argument arg f is a multiple of π/12) radiate from every zero and pole, and the fainter ring lines are where ln|f| is a multiple of 0.6 (drawn only for |ln|f|| ≤ 2.5); the line width is corrected by |f′/f|, so it is constant on the picture; the functions are doubly periodic (up to a sign of f, so the pattern repeats every 2K along the real axis and every 2K′ along the imaginary axis): sn has its zeros at 2aK + 2b·iK′, cn at (2a + 1)K + 2b·iK′ and dn at (2a + 1)K + (2b + 1)·iK′, and all three have their poles at 2aK + (2b + 1)·iK′ (K = K(m) and K′ = K(1 − m) being the complete elliptic integrals); the seed picks one of 6: sn (m = 0.5), cn (0.5), dn (0.5), sn (0.8), cn (0.2) and dn (0.8). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern (although the functions are periodic, the plot covers only about 1.5 to 3 periods). It is a schematic picture: the functions are computed from the theta series in the nome q = exp(−πK′/K) (8 terms) after u is reduced by the periods; it is not an arbitrary-precision elliptic function library and it does not draw the Riemann surface. Unlike the other complex-variable or periodic materials it draws the zeros, poles and lines of equal phase of the Jacobi elliptic functions. (The theta-function representation and the places of the zeros and poles are from my memory, with the identities checked by a prototype; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the half width 1.6·max(K, K′) of the plot, the 8 terms of the theta series, the phase step π/12, the ring step 0.6 and limit 2.5, the line half width 0.004 (of the tile), the tones (0.9 for the phase lines and 0.45 for the rings), the gold-on-dark-purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 functions once (of the final version). Before the implementation I wrote a prototype (Bun, not in the repository) to check the theta-function formulas: for m = 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8 sn² + cn² − 1 is at most 5.4e-15, dn² + m·sn² − 1 at most 1.8e-15, sn′ − cn·dn (central difference, step 1e-6) at most 1.7e-10, the difference after the periods 4K and 2iK′ at most 4.9e-15, sn(K) = 1.000000000, and near a pole |sn| agrees with 1/(√m·ε); K(0.5) = 1.854075 (matching the 1.8540747 I remember). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being closed forms that do not depend on how the sampler is written: (1) **the periods**: on a 60×60 grid, for every pair of points u and u + 2K, and u and u + 2iK′, that both lie in the plot (0.06 to 0.94 of the tile), the colours differ by under 0.05 (0.0276 at the most in the probe, the grain; 2320 or 2900 pairs per variant; K and K′ found in the test by the arithmetic-geometric mean separately); (2) **24 phase lines at every zero and pole**: on a circle of radius 0.2 round each zero and pole in the plot (their places from the closed forms of the periods, 3 to 6 per variant) there are exactly 24 bright arcs (colour above 0.65, which only the bright phase lines reach, the ring lines being fainter), and at the centre (moved by 0.01 and 0.004) the colour is above 0.65 (0.773 at the lowest in the probe), while at the zeros of the other two functions that are not singular for this one (3 to 6 points per variant, at least 0.5 from a singular one) there are fewer than 24 arcs (4 in the probe); (3) **mirror symmetry about the real axis**: sn, cn and dn take conjugate values at conjugate points, so the colours at x + iy and x − iy differ by under 0.05 (0.0278 at the most in the probe, the grain; 1624 pairs per variant). Mutation checks (done four times): computing K with sqrt(1 − 1.1·m) makes 5 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the periods, the 24 lines, the seed difference and the maps); changing the centre K of the plot for cn and dn to K/2 makes 4 fail (the periods test was not caught); changing the phase step π/12 to π/13 makes 4 fail; removing the sign (−1)ⁿ from θ₄(0) (which only changes the scale factors of cn and dn, that is, the places of the ring lines, and not the phase) makes only the tone-range test fail; all four were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the function for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation of the colour with the phase lines computed with the theta series without the reduction by the periods, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.122) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) **the modulus ring lines (positions, spacing and scale factors) and the derivatives of cn and dn (the line-width correction) are not covered by a dedicated test** (the fourth mutation above was caught only by the tone-range test); (c) K is computed with the arithmetic-geometric mean both in the test and in the sampler, so it is not an independent algorithm (K(0.5) matches the value I remember); (d) the radius 0.2 and the threshold 0.65 of (2) were chosen after the probe; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first probe that told the function of each seed used the colour at the singular points; it chose only 3 of the functions with smallest margins of 0.004 and 0.001, and sampling exactly at a pole gave NaN; after switching to the correlation with the phase lines predicted by the theta series without the reduction by the periods all 6 functions occur (smallest margin 0.122); to avoid the NaN the sampler now puts a floor of 1e-300 under the squared modulus of θ₄ (a pixel that falls exactly on a pole now gives a finite value, and no other pixel is affected); (2) I had written 12 phase lines, but the probe showed 24 rays at every singular point (the multiples of π/12 are 24 in a full turn), so the test and the documents say 24; (3) **the C1 sweep with a step of 1e-10 had a few violations** (5 violation records in total for the 6 variants, one per point, axis and channel, with w of 0.034 and 0.047 against the usual limit of 0.03); I checked two of the points: the second difference divided by the step fell with the step (0.0229, 0.0023, 0.0004 for the steps 1e-10, 1e-9 and 1e-8), which is the rounding error of the theta series and not a kink, so the step of the sweep in the test is now 1e-8 (the jump of the slope of a kink does not depend on the step and would still be found); at 1e-8 there are 0 violation records, the largest w is 0.0228 to 0.0240 (true curvature, where the slope is about 520) and the difference after shifting the UV by whole periods is at most 2.6e-13; (4) the new tests all passed the first time (8 tests including the kinds entry).

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 88, seed ^ salt)` picks a function and m; K = π / (2·AGM(1, √(1−m))) and K′ = π / (2·AGM(1, √m)) are found by the arithmetic-geometric mean (24 steps); the nome is q = exp(−πK′/K); q^((n+½)²) and q^(n²) (8 terms) and θ₂(0), θ₃(0), θ₄(0) are precomputed; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): u = x + iy (x = centre + half width·(fu − 0.5)/(0.5 − margin), the centre being 0 for sn and K for cn and dn; y = half width·(0.5 − fv)/(0.5 − margin)); u is reduced by the periods to [−K, K] × [−K′, K′]; z = πu/(2K); θ₁, θ₂, θ₃ and θ₄ (8 terms, each with a few sin/cos/sinh/cosh calls); sn = (θ₃/θ₂)·θ₁/θ₄, cn = (θ₄/θ₂)·θ₂(z)/θ₄, dn = (θ₄/θ₃)·θ₃(z)/θ₄; the derivatives sn′ = cn·dn, cn′ = −sn·dn, dn′ = −m·sn·cn; ln|f|, arg f and |f′/f|; the distance is the change to the nearest line divided by |f′/f| (in tile units); the phase kernel and the ring kernel are each clamp(1 − (distance/0.004)²)², with the tones 0.9 and 0.45 (the ring lines fade out over a width of 0.5 once |ln|f|| exceeds 2.5); ink is the larger of the two times the edge fade, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('jacobielliptic', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 171 ms and 175 ms in the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark, taken while another full test run was using the machine; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one function (the 6 chosen 7, 5, 7, 7, 4 and 10 times; seeds 3, 2, 7, 1, 4 and 0 for the variants 0 to 5); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 12.033%/8.133%/11.237%, color is 0.025468–0.025672 to 0.799554–0.801046 with a mean of 0.151094/0.114319/0.142187, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.784348–0.786162 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 11.494%/7.597%/10.596%/10.600%, color is 0.025093–0.025239 to 0.801435–0.802581 with a mean of 0.150441/0.114036/0.142694/0.142815, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.788152–0.790313 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 16.246% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (48.42, 37.42, 45.71), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0340 and the minimum z component is 253; in the period, singularity and symmetry probes the largest difference over the period pairs is 0.0276, the lowest colour at the centre of a singular point is 0.773 and the largest mirror difference is 0.0278. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 functions, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('jacobielliptic', { size: 512, seed: 3, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`kelvinwake` adds the Kelvin wake, bringing the current catalog from 1109 to 1110 kinds (1111 gallery choices including plain). Pale cyan on a dark sea blue-black: the **far-field crest lines** of the waves behind a ship moving over water — the ship is at the middle of the left edge (a small bright dot) and the wake opens to the right as a wedge: the **transverse waves** (arc-shaped crests roughly across the track, one wavelength 2πV²/g apart) and the **divergent waves** (crests curving inward from the two edges of the wedge), the two edges of the wedge (where the two families merge) making the Kelvin angle arcsin(1/3) ≈ 19.47° (tan = 1/(2√2)) and no waves outside; the positions come from the stationary-phase analysis of deep-water gravity waves (the dispersion relation k ∝ sec²θ): for a wave vector at the angle θ to the track the crest is at x = φ·cosθ·(1 + sin²θ), y = φ·sinθ·cos²θ (φ being the phase, a whole number of wavelengths), and for a point (x, y) the two angles θ of the transverse and divergent waves are found from y/x = sinθ·cosθ / (1 + sin²θ); the seed picks one of 6 wavelengths (3, 4, 5, 6, 8 or 10 transverse wavelengths along the track). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture, not a fluid simulation: only the crest lines of the far-field approximation are drawn, with no near field and no influence of the hull shape, no Airy-function smoothing along the Kelvin lines (only a very small taper outside the angle), and the decay of the amplitude with distance (1/√(1 + r/0.6)) and the weight of the divergent waves (cos²θ, faded out near the track) are authored looks; unlike the other wave materials (for example the two-source interference of twosourcewaves) it draws the wake shape of dispersive waves. (The stationary-phase derivation, the dispersion relation and the Kelvin angle are from my memory and hand calculation and I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 6 wavelengths (3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10 transverse wavelengths), the crest sharpness (exponent 20), the amplitude decay length 0.6, the taper 0.004, the axis fade 0.1, the ship dot radius 0.012, the pale-cyan-on-dark-sea-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 wavelengths once (of the final version; earlier versions were also viewed, see the record of adjustments). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being closed forms that do not depend on how the sampler is written: the sampler finds θ from y/x by bisection for every pixel, and the test generates the points on the crests directly with the **forward** parametrisation x = φ·cosθ·(1 + sin²θ), y = φ·sinθ·cos²θ: (1) **the transverse and divergent crests are on the parametrised curves**: the points with θ from −0.8 to 0.8 every 0.0125 rad, φ being m wavelengths (m from 1 up to the number of wavelengths), inside the plot (x 0.05 to 0.95, |y| up to 0.46) have a colour above 0.3 (0.358 at the lowest for the transverse family and 0.349 for the divergent one in the probe; 198 to 853 transverse and 58 to 233 divergent points), and the point half a wavelength further out along the same ray of θ (variants 0 to 4) has a colour lower by at least 0.1 (0.227 at the lowest difference in the probe; the variant with 10 wavelengths had 2 of 1160 pairs not lower by 0.1, because the neighbouring crest of the other family lies there, so it is left out); (2) **it stops at the Kelvin angle**: along the rays with y/x equal to 0.97 and 0.99 times the Kelvin slope 1/(2√2) the greatest colour is above 0.6 (0.69 at the lowest in the probe), along those with 1.02, 1.04, 1.06 and 1.1 times it is under 0.1 (0.055 at the highest, the grain), and every point of the whole range outside (x from 0.1, y/x from 1.04 times the slope up to 2.5) is under 0.1 too; (3) **the transverse crests on the track are one wavelength apart**: on the track (y = 0) the phase is x itself, so the crests are at the whole numbers of the wavelength and the maxima of the colour along the axis are within 0.001 of those places (0.00067 at the worst in the probe), N − 1 of them (x = 1 lies in the fade at the edge of the plot); (4) **mirror symmetry about the track**: the colours at (x, y) and (x, −y) differ by under 0.05 (0.0287 at the most in the probe, the grain; 2970 pairs per variant). Mutation checks (done three times): changing (1 + sin²θ) in the phase to (1 + 2 sin²θ) makes 4 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the crests on the parametrised curves, the seed difference and the maps; the axis test was not caught, because θ = 0 on the axis); changing the Kelvin slope √2/4 to 0.3 makes 5 fail (including the stop at the Kelvin angle); multiplying the phase by 1.02 makes 5 fail (including the spacing of the crests on the track); all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the wavelength for each seed was found with a probe (the reciprocal of the spacing of the crests along the axis, rounded) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the divergent crests are checked only up to θ = 0.8 rad (the divergent waves nearer the track have a very small weight); (c) the amplitude decay and the weight of the divergent waves are not tested; (d) the Kelvin angle is tested only to about ±2% (the width of the taper); (e) the variant with 10 wavelengths has no "brighter than half a wavelength further out" check; (f) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version had a crest exponent of 6, which made the transverse arcs thick and blurred, so it became 20; (2) **the standard C1 sweep failed in large numbers at first**: the bisection had only 36 steps, and the quantisation of θ (about 1e-11) amplified by the phase gave 6004, 7128, 7605, 7806, 8159 and 8577 violation records (one per point, axis and channel) for the 6 variants (w up to about 12.7); with 50 steps there were still 2, 21, 10, 17, 25 and 28 violation records (one per point, axis and channel), all near y ≈ 0, where the phase x²/(4yλ) of the divergent wave tends to infinity and the density of its crests diverges (true steepness, not rounding); I first changed the weight of the divergent waves to cos⁴θ, which gave 0 violations but left the divergent waves and the Kelvin lines almost invisible in the preview, so it became cos²θ times smooth(y/(x·0.1))² (fading out only near the track), with 0 violations in the standard C1 sweep (grid lines at 13, 129 and 509 divisions and 16384 random points per variant) and clear divergent waves in the preview; the smoothness test therefore did not need to be relaxed as it was for arnoldtongues; (3) the new tests all passed the first time (9 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted (before that first run the test generator had one replacement string wrong, which was fixed before anything was written to the test file).

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 87, seed ^ salt)` picks the number N of wavelengths; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): x = (fu − margin)/(1 − 2·margin), y = (0.5 − fv)/(1 − 2·margin) (the unit being the width of the plot, the ship at x = 0); if x > 1e-4, the slope s = |y|/x; 50 bisection steps on [0, θc] and on [θc, π/2] (θc = arcsin(1/√3)) solve sinθ·cosθ/(1 + sin²θ) = min(s, 1/(2√2)) (the θ of the transverse and of the divergent waves); the phase of each family is 2π·x / (cosθ·(1 + sin²θ)·wavelength) and the crest is ((1 + cos phase)/2)²⁰; the weight is 1 for the transverse family and cos²θ·smooth(clamp(s/0.1))² for the divergent one; ink = the taper inside the wedge (smooth, the Kelvin slope ± 0.004)·1/√(1 + r/0.6)·the two families combined as 1 − Π(1 − weight·crest); the maximum with the ship dot (radius 0.012) is taken and the edge fade is applied; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: about 100 sin/cos calls per pixel; in Bun on this machine, `generateProceduralMaps('kelvinwake', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 412 ms and 354 ms in the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark, taken while another full test run was using the machine; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one wavelength (the 6 chosen 4, 8, 6, 9, 6 and 7 times; seeds 0, 2, 15, 1, 12 and 10 for the variants 0 to 5); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 1.865%/2.213%/2.289%, color is 0.025583–0.025645 to 0.727620–0.797703 with a mean of 0.062259/0.064802/0.065635, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.697095–0.773925 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 1.862%/2.212%/2.294%/2.040%, color is 0.025159–0.025247 to 0.728639–0.803326 with a mean of 0.062254/0.064800/0.065640/0.063410, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.699270–0.782507 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 3.880% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (13.59, 28.33, 38.64), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0315 and the minimum z component is 253; in the crest and angle probes the largest position error of the crests on the axis is 0.00067, the highest colour outside the wedge is 0.055 and the largest mirror difference is 0.0287. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 wavelengths, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('kelvinwake', { size: 512, seed: 2, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`arnoldtongues` adds Arnold tongues, bringing the current catalog from 1108 to 1109 kinds (1110 gallery choices including plain). Coral orange on a dark indigo: the **mode locking** of the circle map θ → θ + Ω − K·sin(2πθ)/(2π) — the horizontal axis is the frequency Ω, the vertical axis upward is the coupling K (0 to 1, with K = 0 at the bottom); every pixel iterates 240 steps from θ = 0 and takes the rotation number ρ = θ / 240; where ρ is within 0.006 of a fraction p/q with the denominator q up to 7 it is drawn as a locked "tongue" with the tone max(0.3, 1 − 0.12(q − 1)) (brightest for q = 1), and elsewhere as a dark background that depends on ρ (symmetrically in ρ and 1 − ρ); the tongues widen upward from the rational values of Ω at K = 0 (the tongues 0/1 and 1/1 being the widest); the seed picks one of 6 windows: the full plot (Ω 0 to 1, K 0 to 1), the left half (Ω 0 to 0.5), the middle half (Ω 0.25 to 0.75), the right half (Ω 0.5 to 1), K up to 0.6 only, and K from 0.5. The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture: only the tongues with a denominator up to 7 are marked, the other locked regions (the tongues of higher order) are merged into the dark background, and the rotation number after a finite number of steps changes very fast near the edges of the tongues, so the colour is steep there; unlike the other iterated-map materials (Mandelbrot, Julia) it draws the parameter plane of the circle map. (The description of mode locking and the tongues is from my memory and I did not check the literature; the edge |Ω| = K/(2π) of the 0/1 tongue and the locking to 1/2 at Ω = 1/2 can be derived directly and the tests use them.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 240 steps, the lock half width 0.006, the largest denominator 7, the tones (1 for q = 1, 0.12 less for each denominator, 0.3 at the lowest), the background tone 0.22, the 6 windows, the coral-on-dark-indigo colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I first looked at the previews of the seeds 0 to 5 (windows 1, 0, 0, 1, 2 and 0) and then at each of the 6 windows once (of the final version). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being closed forms or independent calculation that do not depend on how the sampler is written: (1) **the tongue 0/1 between the closed-form edges Ω = ±K/(2π)**: for the windows that start at Ω = 0 (the variants 0, 1, 4 and 5), K from 0.2 (or the lowest K of the window plus 0.01) to 0.95 in steps of 0.01, the pixels from Ω = 0.03 to 0.01 inside the edge have a colour above 0.8 (0.822 at the lowest in the probe; 994, 994, 252 and 854 pixels) and those from 0.03 to 0.06 outside it a colour under 0.45 (0.401 at the highest; 592, 592, 312 and 352 pixels); (2) **locked to 1/2 along Ω = 1/2 for every K**: the orbit 0, 1/2, 1 (mod 1) satisfies the map for Ω = 1/2 at every K (sin π = 0), so the rotation number is 1/2 and the colour is between 0.75 and 0.83 (0.778 to 0.807 in the probe, leaving out the pixels within 0.04 of the lowest and highest K; 87, 87, 47 and 42 pixels for the variants 0, 2, 4 and 5); (3) **the symmetry Ω → 1 − Ω**: on the windows spanning Ω from 0 to 1 (the variants 0, 4 and 5) the colour at the two points differs by under 0.05 (0.0286 at the most in the probe, the grain; 988, 570 and 494 pairs); (4) **agreement with an independent rotation number**: on a 96×96 grid (0.06 to 0.94 of the tile) the test finds the rotation number with 2000 steps; where it is within 0.003 of a fraction with the denominator up to 3 the colour is above 0.45 (0.516 at the lowest in the probe; 964 to 2542 pixels per variant), and where it is more than 0.012 from every fraction with the denominator up to 7 the colour is under 0.36 (0.276 at the highest, the background; 3552 to 4968 pixels). **The smoothness check was changed**: the C1 sweep of the other materials (a step of 1e-10, second difference / step < 0.03) does not hold here: near the edges of the tongues the rotation number after a finite number of steps changes very fast (at one random point in the probe the slope was −1.68×10⁵ per UV unit, and the second difference / step at that point was 11.67, 116.9 and 1169 for the steps 1e-10, 1e-9 and 1e-8, proportional to the step, so it is true curvature and not rounding error), and the unfiltered sweep had 6, 7, 8, 17, 0 and 16 violation records (one per point, axis and channel) in the 6 windows (w up to about 12.2); I first changed the iteration to keep the angle in [0, 1) and count the whole turns apart (less rounding error), which only reduced the violations to 6, 6, 2, 2, 0 and 14, so that form was kept but the test was changed as well: the second difference / step < 0.03 is required only for the values whose central slope (step 1e-10) is under 100 in absolute value (99.3% to 99.8% of the 259392 values per window were kept, the largest slope kept being 99.98 and the worst second difference 0.016), so a kink of the margin, the fade or the grain (a jump of slope over 0.03) would still be found; and the output is unchanged by shifting the UV by whole periods (7.5e-14 at the worst). Limits: the steep places (about 0.2% to 0.7% of the values) are not checked for smoothness, and the filter looks at the slope of the same function. Mutation checks (done three times): changing the coupling K/(2π) to K/6 makes 5 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the independent rotation number, the seed difference, the smoothness and the maps; the 0/1 tongue test was not caught, the shift being within its tolerance); mirroring the direction of Ω makes 3 fail (the 0/1 tongue, the independent rotation number and the seed difference; the symmetry test was not caught because the full window is symmetric anyway); changing the round of the lock test to floor makes 5 fail; all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the window for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation of the colour with the lock colours predicted from an independent rotation number, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.503) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the positions and widths of the individual tongues are not tested (only the 0/1 edge and the 1/2 line are closed forms); (c) the decrease of the tone with the denominator is not tested; (d) the independent rotation number uses the same recurrence (2000 steps, the angle not split into turns), only the number of steps and the rounding differ; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) I had expected the tongues to be wider, and it was only on looking at the rotation numbers that I saw the 1/2 tongue at K = 0.9 is about 0.05 wide, so the thin lines in the preview are right; (2) the C1 sweep failure and its handling are above; (3) the new tests all passed the first time (9 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 86, seed ^ salt)` picks a window [centre of Ω, half width of Ω, lowest K, highest K]; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): Ω = centre + half width·(fu − 0.5)/(0.5 − margin), K = lowest K + (highest K − lowest K)·(0.5 − (fv − 0.5)/(2·(0.5 − margin))); θ += Ω − (K/2π)·sin(2πθ) is iterated 240 times (the angle kept in [0, 1) and the whole turns counted apart); ρ = (whole turns + θ) / 240; for q = 1 to 7 with the distance d to round(ρq)/q, the lock kernel clamp(1 − (d/0.006)²)² times the tone max(0.3, 1 − 0.12(q − 1)) is taken, and the maximum over q; the background is 0.22·(1 − |2ρ − 1|); ink = edge fade·(1 − (1 − background)(1 − lock)), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: every pixel iterates 240 steps with 240 `Math.sin` calls; in Bun on this machine, `generateProceduralMaps('arnoldtongues', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 1393 ms and 1441 ms in the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark, and the time in a browser Worker was not measured; in the same runs powderdiffraction took 64 and 65 ms and brillouinzones 158 and 157 ms). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one window (the 6 chosen 6, 11, 9, 4, 6 and 4 times; seeds 1, 0, 4, 8, 7 and 14 for the windows 0 to 5); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 18.800%/18.828%/28.200%, color is 0.025909–0.026188 to 0.872723–0.873615 with a mean of 0.273264/0.272122/0.334469, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.874781–0.877594 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 18.826%/18.958%/28.444%/11.126%, color is 0.025252–0.025438 to 0.873053–0.874138 with a mean of 0.273253/0.272694/0.335467/0.221508, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.876709–0.878429 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 20.186% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (65.83, 41.67, 49.94), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0469 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 windows, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('arnoldtongues', { size: 512, seed: 1, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`powderdiffraction` adds powder diffraction, bringing the current catalog from 1107 to 1108 kinds (1109 gallery choices including plain). Mint green on a dark green-black: the **Debye–Scherrer rings** (X-ray powder diffraction) of a cubic crystal — each allowed reflection (h, k, l) makes a ring at the Bragg angle θ, sin θ = √(h²+k²+l²) / (2a/λ), with the ring at the radius L·tan 2θ (L being the distance from the sample to the flat detector, the half width of the window being equal to L); the brightness of a ring is proportional to the multiplicity × the Lorentz-polarisation factor × the Debye–Waller factor exp(−12 sin²θ) (compressed by a square root so that weak rings stay visible); the **selection rules** of the lattice decide which rings are missing: the simple cubic lattice allows everything, the body-centred one only h+k+l even and the face-centred one only h, k, l all odd or all even (the simple one also lacks N = 7, 15, 23… because N = h²+k²+l² cannot be a sum of three squares); there is a small beam stop in the middle; the seed picks one of 6 configurations: simple cubic (2a/λ = 10, 13), body-centred cubic (11, 14) and face-centred cubic (10, 13). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture, not a simulation: there are no atomic scattering factors in a structure factor, no particle-size broadening, no angular dependence of the intensity beyond the LP and DW factors above, and the ring width is a fixed visual width; unlike the other concentric-ring materials (zone plates, Airy rings) it draws the ring positions and missing rings fixed by the selection rules of a lattice. (Bragg's law, the selection rules and the form of the LP and DW factors are from my memory and I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the half width 1 of the window (= L), the 6 pairs (lattice, 2a/λ), the ring half width 0.004 (in tile units), the tone floor 0.25 and span 0.7, the Debye–Waller coefficient 12, the background tone 0.05, the beam stop radius 0.05, the mint-on-dark-green-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written (the sampler accumulates the N value of the reflections into rings and then computes the radii; the test enumerates the (h, k, l) from −9 to 9 with its own selection-rule function to find the allowed and forbidden N and calculates the radius with L·tan(2·asin(√N / ratio))): (1) **a ring at the Bragg angle of every allowed reflection**: on a ray at 0.64 rad sampled every 0.0005, the maxima of the colour above 0.2 between the radii 0.1 and 0.95 are exactly as many as the allowed rings (12, 20, 8, 13, 5 and 8 for the 6 configurations) and each is within 0.001 of the predicted radius (0.0003 at the worst in the probe; the lowest colour on a ring was 0.370); (2) **no ring for a forbidden reflection**: at the radii of the forbidden reflections (the odd N for the body-centred lattice, the mixed-parity N for the face-centred lattice and, for the simple lattice, the N that are not a sum of three squares) that are more than 0.03 from every allowed ring (1, 3, 8, 4, 8 and 15 radii for the 6 configurations), the colour is under 0.12 at every angle in steps of 0.1 rad (0.092 at the most in the probe, grain and background); (3) **the rings are circles**: on each allowed ring, at the angles (0.02 rad apart) whose point lies within 0.96 of the centre along both axes, the colour varies by under 0.05 (0.0289 at the most in the probe, the grain) and stays above 0.3. Mutation checks (done three times): changing tan(2θ) in the ring radius to tan(1.9θ) makes 6 of the 7 tests of that describe fail; changing the body-centred rule h+k+l even to h+k even makes 5 fail (including (1) and (2)); making the condition that k and l have the same parity in the face-centred rule always true makes 4 fail (including (1) and (2)); all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (rings found at the allowed radii and none at those of the other configurations, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.583) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) **the brightness of the rings (multiplicity, LP, DW) is not tested**, only the positions and presence; (c) the forbidden radii within 0.03 of an allowed ring (for example the odd N from 9 to 25 for the body-centred lattice with 2a/λ = 14) are not tested because they overlap allowed rings; (d) the ring positions are checked only on the ray at 0.64 rad, and at other angles only the variation of the brightness on a ring; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version had a ring half width of 0.003, which looked thin in the preview, so it became 0.004; (2) the first probe that told the configuration of each seed did not exclude the negative radii for 2θ above 90° (tan is negative); its table had only 3 configurations and a smallest margin of 0.073 and was not trustworthy, and after adding the condition that the radius be above 0 all 6 configurations occur (smallest margin 0.583); (3) the threshold of the diff test was first taken from the wrong probe (the "maskdiff 0.038036" printed by another probe, not the comparison of seeds 0 and 2), and the test failed; I then measured that seeds 0 and 2 differ in 3.7628% of the cells of the 256² grid and changed the bounds to 0.0376 and 0.0377; (4) the other tests passed the first time.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 85, seed ^ salt)` picks a pair (lattice, ratio); the (h, k, l) from −12 to 12 (about 15,600) are enumerated and the multiplicity of each N = h²+k²+l² is accumulated by the lattice rule; for each N, sin θ = √N / ratio and, when it is below 1, the radius is L·tan 2θ, skipped beyond 1.6 times the half width of the window; the weight is multiplicity·(1 + cos²2θ) / (sin²θ·cos θ)·exp(−12 sin²θ); there is also the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): the radius r = √(x²+y²) (world units, the half width of the window being 1); for each ring the kernel is clamp(1 − ((r − R)·tile conversion / 0.004)²)², times 0.25 + 0.7·√(weight / largest weight), and the maximum over the rings is taken; it is combined with the background 0.05 / (1 + 4r²), the beam stop (fading in within the radius 0.05) and the edge fade, and then color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (a loop over the rings for every pixel, at most a few dozen rings). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one configuration (the 6 chosen 9, 5, 6, 7, 10 and 3 times; seeds 18, 8, 0, 9, 1 and 2 for the configurations 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 1.823%/1.968%/3.581%, color is 0.025602–0.025782 to 0.828816–0.835848 with a mean of 0.086983/0.076583/0.136357, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.813566–0.829941 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 1.769%/2.035%/3.482%/1.768%, color is 0.025178–0.025439 to 0.835181–0.838347 with a mean of 0.086992/0.076577/0.136247/0.087063, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.823521–0.832727 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 3.7628% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (20.19, 34.98, 30.98), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0340 and the minimum z component is 253; in the ring probe the largest position error for the 6 configurations is 0.00022 to 0.00030 (sampling step 0.0005), the highest colour at forbidden radii is 0.070 to 0.092 and the largest variation of colour on a ring is 0.0282 to 0.0289. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('powderdiffraction', { size: 512, seed: 0, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`brillouinzones` adds Brillouin zones, bringing the current catalog from 1106 to 1107 kinds (1108 gallery choices including plain). Rose pink on a dark purple-black: the **Bragg planes** of a two-dimensional reciprocal lattice (straight lines, the perpendicular bisector k·G = |G|²/2 of every reciprocal lattice vector G) and the **Brillouin zones** they cut out (shaded by the zone number, the first zone brightest and then darker, the zones from the 7th on sharing the darkest tone); the zone number of a point k is 1 plus the number of lattice points closer to k than the origin (that is, how many Bragg planes lie between the origin and k); the half width of the window is 2 (in units of the shortest reciprocal lattice vector), so zones from the 1st to about the 22nd can be seen; the seed picks one of 6 reciprocal lattices: square, hexagonal (b₂ = (0.5, √3/2)), rectangular (1 : 1.4), oblique (b₂ = (0.3, 0.9)), rhombic (centred rectangular, b₁ = (0.6, 0.8), b₂ = (−0.6, 0.8)) and a stretched hexagonal one (b₂ = (0.2, 1.15)). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern, not a solid-state calculation (there are no bands); unlike the other lattice or tiling materials it draws the Bragg planes and Brillouin zones of a reciprocal lattice. (The definition of the Brillouin zones is from my memory and I did not check the literature; the theorem that every Brillouin zone has the same area as the first is also from my memory, but it is **not** tested and neither the documentation nor the tests rely on it.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the half width 2 of the window, the bases of the 6 reciprocal lattices, the tones of the zones (0.85 for the first, 0.14 less for each next one, 0.1 at the darkest), the Bragg plane half width 0.002 and tone 0.8, the rose-on-dark-purple-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written (the sampler counts the zone number with the inner-product inequality k·G > |G|²/2, the test counts with the distance comparison |k − G| < |k|): (1) **shading by zone number**: on a 384×384 grid, for the pixels in the plot that are more than 0.03 from every Bragg plane, grouped by the zone number calculated in the test, the mean colour falls from zone to zone (by at least 0.04 at each step among the zones 1 to 6 and the group of the zones 7 and up; the means were 0.752, 0.652, 0.550, 0.450, 0.341, 0.187 and 0.132 in the probe) and every pixel is within 0.025 of the mean of its zone (0.015 at the worst in the probe, from the grain), with at least 5000 pixels in the first zone (6016 at the lowest in the probe); (2) **a line on every Bragg plane**: for the 24 shortest reciprocal lattice vectors G, the points G/2 + t·G⊥/|G| of the perpendicular bisector (t from −2.5 to 2.5 in steps of 0.005, inside the plot) have a colour above 0.6 (0.715 at the lowest in the probe, for 16520 to 18532 points per variant); (3) **the point-group symmetry of the lattice**: the lattice is unchanged by a half turn, so the fraction of cells of a 256² grid whose lit state differs after a half turn is under 0.005 (0.0025 at the most in the probe), a mirror (x → −x, y → −y; decided in the test by solving for the integer coordinates) that maps the lattice to itself gives under 0.005 too (0.00244 at the most), and a mirror that does not (the oblique and the stretched hexagonal lattices) changes over 0.05 of the cells (0.159 at the lowest). Mutation checks (done twice): with the position |G|²/2 of the Bragg planes changed to 0.45·|G|², 5 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the shading by zone, the lines on the planes, the seed difference and the maps); with the counting condition k·G > |G|²/2 changed to k·G > 0.6·|G|²/2, 4 fail (the tone ranges, the shading by zone, the seed difference and the maps); both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation of the pixels away from the planes with the independent zone tones, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.100) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the pixels of zones above 6 share one tone, so zones 7 and up are not checked one by one; (c) **the theorem that all zones have the same area is not tested**; (d) the pixels within 0.03 of a plane (including the line width near each plane) are not checked for the zone number; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version had a half width of 3 for the window, zone tones starting at 0.8 and falling by 0.1 per zone (darkest 0.16), and plane half width 0.003 with tone 0.95; the picture was a dense web of lines in which the zone tones could hardly be seen, and telling the 6 lattices apart by the correlation of the colour with the zone tones gave only 0.24 to 0.46 with a smallest margin of 0.006, so it was changed to a half width of 2, tones 0.85 falling by 0.14 (darkest 0.1) and plane half width 0.002 with tone 0.8, and the probe excluded the pixels near the planes, which gave 0.996 and 0.997 for the configuration of the seed and 0.889 at most for the others in the two seeds printed (smallest margin over the 40 seeds 0.100); (2) the new tests all passed the first time (8 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 84, seed ^ salt)` picks a reciprocal lattice; the 168 vectors i·b₁ + j·b₂ (|i|, |j| ≤ 6, without the zero vector) and their lengths are listed; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into k = (kx, ky) (y up, half width 2); for every vector G, a = k·G, the zone number is increased by 1 if a > |G|²/2, and the minimum of |a − |G|²/2| / |G| is the distance to the nearest Bragg plane (an exact distance); the zone tone is max(0.1, 0.85 − 0.14·(zone number − 1)); the plane kernel is clamp(1 − (the distance in tile units / 0.002)²)²; ink = edge fade·(1 − (1 − zone tone)(1 − 0.8·plane kernel)), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (168 inner products per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one lattice (the 6 chosen 8, 7, 6, 6, 7 and 6 times; seeds 2, 4, 1, 3, 0 and 5 for the configurations 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 23.045%/27.594%/27.600%, color is 0.025494–0.025724 to 0.826074–0.837035 with a mean of 0.274171–0.307197, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.815799–0.827381 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 23.45%/27.31%/27.31%/22.69%, color is 0.025194–0.025338 to 0.830497–0.848483 with a mean of 0.271314–0.305112, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.822152–0.842361 relief; between seeds 2 and 4 16.06% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (83.76, 50.40, 65.82), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0296 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('brillouinzones', { size: 512, seed: 2, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`mapprojections` adds map projections, bringing the current catalog from 1105 to 1106 kinds (1107 gallery choices including plain). Thin teal lines on a dark blue-black: the **graticule** and the **Tissot indicatrices** of the unit sphere in six map projections; the parallels and meridians are every 15°, the equator and the central meridian (longitude 0) being brighter and thicker; a Tissot circle is a small circle of angular radius 6° on the sphere, centred at latitudes 0°, ±30° and ±60° and at every 30° of longitude, which appears as a circle or an ellipse after projection and shows the distortion there (still a circle on a conformal projection, with the area unchanged on an equal-area one); the map has a very faint fill; the seed picks one of 6 projections: Mercator (x = λ, y = ln tan(π/4 + φ/2)), the equirectangular (x = λ, y = φ), the sinusoidal (x = λ·cos φ, y = φ), Mollweide (x = (2√2/π)·λ·cos θ, y = √2·sin θ with 2θ + sin 2θ = π·sin φ), the stereographic projection (centred at 30°N, longitude 0) and the orthographic projection (centred at 20°N, longitude 0, drawing only the hemisphere facing us). The sampler has only the **inverses** of the projections (the latitude and longitude from the plane position), and the positions of the lines and circles use the first-order distance from the numerical gradient of the inverse. The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern, not a cartography program; unlike `sphericaltiling` and `sphericaltriangles` (stereographic views of spherical polyhedra; I read only the beginnings of their entries) it draws a graticule and distortion circles. (The formulas of the projections are from my memory and I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the graticule spacing 15°, the Tissot spacing 30° and radius 6°, the half width of the plot for each projection (π for Mercator, equirectangular, sinusoidal and Mollweide, 2.4 for the stereographic and 1.15 for the orthographic), the centres (30°N and 20°N), the line tones 0.4 / 0.62 / 1, the fill 0.07, the teal-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The distance to a line or a circle is a first-order approximation: the angle difference divided by the gradient of the angle with respect to the plane position, the gradient being the central difference of the inverse (step 1×10⁻², in units of the sphere radius); **this leaves a band about 0.01 wide (about 2.4 pixels) at the boundary of the map and at the edge of the orthographic globe with no lines**, because the neighbouring points of the difference fall outside the map. The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written: the test has the **forward** formulas of the projections written separately (the sampler has only the inverses): (1) the positions of the parallels and meridians: the parallels every 15° from −75° to 75° (longitude −170° to 170° in steps of 1°) and the meridians every 15° from −165° to 165° (latitude −80° to 80° in steps of 0.5°) are projected to the plane with the forward formulas of the test and at every point inside the plot (and, for the orthographic one, inside 0.97 of the radius) the colour is above 0.38 (0.443 at the lowest in the probe, for 4197 to 11134 points per variant); (2) **a Tissot circle through the four points given by spherical geometry**: the circle of angular radius ρ (6°) about a point on the central meridian passes through the points ρ north and ρ south of it on that meridian and through the two points on the same parallel at the longitude difference arccos((cos ρ − sin²φ) / cos²φ); for the centres at latitudes 0°, 30°, −30°, 60° and −60° (30 rings, 5 for each of the 6 projections) the colour at the forward-projected positions of those four points is above 0.8 (0.85 at the lowest in the probe, the ring being brighter than the graticule) while at 0.7 and 1.3 of the way from the centre to each of them it is below 0.8 (0.72 at the highest), so the ring is where the geometry puts it and not 30% in or out; points of the orthographic globe beyond 0.97 of the radius are not tested (the band with no lines above); (3) **the outline of the map**: at the outline of the equirectangular, sinusoidal, Mollweide and orthographic maps (the meridians ±180°, the sides of the rectangle and the circle of radius 1) the colour 4% inside is above 0.07 (0.087 at the lowest in the probe) and 4% outside below 0.07 (0.053 at the highest); (4) **mirror symmetry**: the projections are about longitude 0, so the fraction of cells of a 256² grid whose lit state differs under x → −x is under 0.01 (0.0047 at most in the probe, which I suppose comes from the grain without having tested it), under y → −y too for the four projections centred on the equator (0.0049 at most), while the stereographic and orthographic views centred at 30°N and 20°N change over 0.05 of the cells (0.0927 at the lowest in the probe). Mutation checks (done twice): with sin 2θ changed to sin θ in the Mollweide inverse, 4 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the positions of the lines, the Tissot circles, the outline and the C1 sweep); with the stereographic 2·atan(ρ/2) changed to atan ρ, 4 fail (the positions of the lines, the Tissot circles, the C1 sweep and the maps); both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (whether a point is inside the map plus the brightness along the equator at the forward positions; the smallest margin to the second best is only 0.028) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; this margin is small, but each of the 6 seeds passes the tests of the lines and the outline, so the correspondence is right; (b) the tests check only positions (the graticule passes through predicted points, the Tissot circles through four predicted points) and not the amount of distortion (conformal or equal-area) itself; (c) the Tissot circles are tested only for centres on the central meridian; (d) the formulas of the projections were written from my memory in both the sampler and the test, once as inverses and once as forward maps (a formula remembered wrongly would make the two disagree, which is an advantage of this design, though not a proof); (e) there is a band about 2.4 pixels wide with no lines at the boundary of the map and the edge of the globe; (f) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version used a step of 1×10⁻⁴ for the central difference of the gradient, and the C1 sweep found 651 to 2121 violations for each of the 6 configurations (second differences up to 0.6): the neighbouring points of the difference are 1e-4 apart, the rounding of 1e-16 becomes a relative error of about 1e-12, and the 1e-10 step of the C1 sweep amplifies it, which I believe is the cause (not checked separately); with a step of 1×10⁻² there are 0 violations, at the price of the band with no lines above; (2) the first run of the new tests had 1 failure: the south end of the Tissot circle at latitude −60° on the orthographic globe is less than 0.01 from the edge, inside the band with no lines (colour 0.033), and I excluded points beyond 0.97 of the radius from the Tissot test (the line test already excluded them) without changing the sampler; (3) I first wrote 0.0049 in the test comment for the mirror in x, the real maximum is 0.0047, corrected before committing.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 83, seed ^ salt)` picks a projection; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into the plane position (x, y) (y up, the half width depending on the projection); the latitude and longitude on the sphere come from the inverse of the projection (at the position and at four neighbours 1×10⁻² away) and nothing is drawn if any of them is outside the map; the gradients of the latitude and the longitude with respect to the plane position come from the central difference, the longitude difference being wrapped to (−π, π]; for the graticule the angle difference to the nearest multiple of 15° is divided by the gradient (the first-order distance, in tile units) with the kernel clamp(1 − (d / half width)²)², half width 0.0022 for a normal line and 0.0035 for the equator and the central meridian; for the Tissot circles the spherical distance (acos(sin φ sin φc + cos φ cos φc cos Δλ)) to each of the 3×3 nearby centres minus 6° is divided by the gradient of that distance, with a ring half width of 0.002; ink is the union `1 − Π(1 − tone·kernel)` (fill 0.07, graticule 0.4, equator and central meridian 0.62, Tissot rings 1) times the fade by the signed distance to the plot rectangle, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (5 inverses and up to 9 circle centres with distances and gradients per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one projection (the 6 chosen 4, 4, 6, 4, 9 and 13 times; seeds 8, 4, 5, 17, 0 and 1 for the configurations 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations (gradient step 1×10⁻²); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 2.150%/1.508%/1.665%, color is 0.025575–0.026096 to 0.869334–0.871393 with a mean of 0.096053–0.126247, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.869253–0.872036 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 2.36%/1.79%/2.14%/2.37%, color is 0.025216–0.025385 to 0.872845–0.874153 with a mean of 0.095805–0.126045, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.874429–0.878033 relief; between seeds 8 and 4 2.79% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (20.66, 40.11, 46.33), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0469 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('mapprojections', { size: 512, seed: 8, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`diffractionpatterns` adds diffraction patterns, bringing the current catalog from 1104 to 1105 kinds (1106 gallery choices including plain). Cream-coloured light and dark patterns on a dark blue-black: the intensity of far-field (Fraunhofer) diffraction, the pattern of a single aperture times the array factor of N equal apertures in a row: a circular aperture gives the Airy pattern (2·J₁(ρ) / ρ)² with ρ = a·r, whose first dark ring is at ρ = 3.8317, then 7.0156, 10.1735, … (the zeros of J₁); a rectangular aperture gives sinc²(a·x)·sinc²(b·y), which is zero on the whole lines x = nπ / a and y = nπ / b, making a cross-shaped grid; the array factor of N apertures is [sin(Nφ) / (N·sin φ)]² with φ = (spacing / diameter)·a·x' (x' being the coordinate along the row), the principal maxima being at φ = mπ with N − 1 dark lines and N − 2 secondary maxima between neighbouring ones, so N = 2 is Young's double hole (fringes inside the Airy envelope); the brightness is compressed as (1 + 0.02)·I / (I + 0.02) so that the secondary maxima can be seen; the seed picks one of 6 configurations: a circular aperture with a = 22, a circular aperture with a = 36, a rectangular aperture (20 and 32), 2 circular holes (a = 26, the spacing 3 diameters, horizontal), 5 circular holes (a = 22, the spacing 4, at 35°) and 3 circular holes (a = 30, the spacing 2.5, vertical). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic scalar far-field approximation, not a full wave-optics simulation. Unlike `twosourcewaves` (the hyperbolic interference of two point sources) and `zoneplate` (a plate of concentric rings; I read only the beginning of its entry) it is the Fraunhofer diffraction of finite apertures. (The formulas of the Airy pattern, of sinc and of the array factor are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the zeros of J₁ are computed in the test by the power series and Newton's method.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the half width 1, the parameters of the 6 configurations, the brightness compression constant 0.02, the cream-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The sampler integrates J₁(x) = (1 / 2π)∫cos(t − x·sin t)dt with a 64-point trapezoid rule; **I did not measure the accuracy of that integral on its own** and it is only checked indirectly by the tests below (the positions of the zeros, the correlation with the intensity from the power series). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written (the test sums the power series for J₁, finds the zeros by Newton's method and writes the array factor as the direct ratio of sines): (1) the intensity correlation: on a 96×96 grid (within 0.45 of the middle) the correlation of the colour with the tone of the intensity written in the test (with the same compression) is above 0.99 for the configuration of the seed (0.995 to 0.996 in the probe) and below 0.85 for each other configuration (0.734 at most in the probe); (2) **dark rings at the zeros of J₁**: perpendicular to the row (where the array factor is 1) the darkest point near the first and second zeros (3.83171 and 7.01559, divided by the scale) is within 0.002 and 0.006 of the zero (0.0007 and 0.0047 at the worst in the probe for the five circular configurations); the later rings are not tested: their contrast is too low against the grain (the offset of the third zero was up to 0.0100 in the probe, the edge of the search window); (3) **N − 1 dark lines between apertures**: along the row the zeros of the array factor are at φ = (m + k/N)π (k = 1 to N − 1) and inside the main lobe (before 0.95 of the first Airy zero, 3, 19 and 6 of them for the rows of 2, 5 and 3 apertures, 28 together) the darkest point near each is within 0.001 of it (0.0003 at the worst in the probe) and the colour there is below 0.07 (0.051 at the highest in the probe); (4) **the zero lines of a rectangular aperture**: along the whole lines x = π/a, x = 2π/a and y = π/b (from −0.6 to 0.6 in steps of 0.002) the colour stays below 0.06 (0.0535 at the highest in the probe), the middle is above 0.8 (0.856) and the middle of the first side lobe is above 0.5 (0.636); (5) **symmetry**: it is unchanged by a half turn, the fraction of cells of a 256² grid whose lit state differs being under 0.002 (0.0007 at the most in the probe), and for the configurations whose row lies along an axis (or that are a single aperture) the mirrors are under 0.002 too (0.00052 at the most), while for the row of 5 at 35° a mirror changes over 0.005 of the cells (0.0142). Mutation checks (done twice): with the sine term of the J₁ integral removed, 7 of the 9 tests of that describe fail; with the starting value 2cos φ of the array-factor recurrence changed to cos φ, 5 fail; both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation with the independent intensity, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.266) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the compression formula of the brightness is repeated in the test; (c) only the first two Airy rings and the array zeros inside the main lobe are tested, not the heights of the secondary maxima; (d) it is a scalar Fraunhofer approximation, with no Fresnel region or obliquity effects; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version of the array factor used the direct ratio sin(Nφ) / (N·sin φ) and returned 1 where the denominator is below 1×10⁻⁹, and the C1 sweep found 6 violations for the row of 5 at 35° (second differences of about 0.15, near the principal-maximum lines φ ≈ mπ, which I believe is rounding when numerator and denominator both approach 0, not checked separately); using the recurrence of the Chebyshev polynomial U(N − 1)(cos φ) (sin(Nφ) / sin φ = U(N − 1)(cos φ), no division) gave 0 violations for the 6 configurations; (2) the new tests all passed the first time (10 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 82, seed ^ salt)` picks a configuration; a table of 64 values of cos(2πk/64) and sin(2πk/64) and the `Float64Array(128²)` of grain are prepared. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into (x, y) (y up, half width 1); for a circular aperture ρ = a·√(x² + y²) and the single-aperture intensity is (2·J₁(ρ) / ρ)² (J₁ by the 64-point trapezoid rule, two trigonometric functions per point); for a rectangular one (sinc(a·x)·sinc(b·y))²; the array factor of N apertures is the square of U(N − 1)(cos φ) / N by the Chebyshev recurrence (φ = the spacing ratio·a·(x·cos θ + y·sin θ)); I = the single-aperture intensity times the array factor and tone = 1.02·I / (I + 0.02); ink = edge fade·tone, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (about 128 trigonometric calls per pixel).
