Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one configuration (the 6 chosen 5, 10, 8, 10, 4 and 3 times; seeds 7, 12, 1, 0, 10 and 2 for the configurations 0 to 5); the first four zeros of J₁ (in the test, by the power series and Newton's method) are 3.83171, 7.01559, 10.17347 and 13.32369; the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 0.768%/1.474%/0.774%, color is 0.025413–0.025752 to 0.860830–0.871120 with a mean of 0.056670–0.062489, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.850796–0.872328 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 0.797%/1.472%/0.794%/1.481%, color is 0.025122–0.025232 to 0.861966–0.873948 with a mean of 0.056686–0.078087, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.854847–0.877750 relief; between seeds 7 and 12 0.911% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (25.44, 26.11, 37.74), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0020 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('diffractionpatterns', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`errordiffusion` adds error-diffusion dithering, bringing the current catalog from 1103 to 1104 kinds (1105 gallery choices including plain). Pale round dots on a dark blue-black: a black-and-white dithered image of 96×96 cells, each cell being lit (a pale dot) or dark (a very faint small dot); a grey-level source image is turned into black and white by error diffusion: the cells are processed in raster order (left to right, top to bottom), the value of a cell is the grey level of the source plus the error diffused to it from the cells already processed, a value ≥ 0.5 is lit, and the error = value − output (0 or 1) is shared with the cells not yet processed according to the kernel (what falls outside the grid is dropped); the seed picks one of 6 configurations (kernel × source image): Floyd–Steinberg (7, 3, 5, 1 over 16) on a horizontal ramp, Atkinson (six cells of 1 over 8, sending on only 3/4 of the error) on a horizontal ramp, Jarvis–Judice–Ninke (over 48) on 8 steps, Stucki (over 42) on a radial ramp, Burkes (over 32) on a diagonal ramp and Sierra Lite (2, 1, 1 over 4) on 8 steps. The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.03), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern; unlike ordered dithering such as `bayerdither` (I read only the beginning of its entry), the pattern comes from the error being passed on cell by cell. (The weights of the kernels and Atkinson's 3/4 are from my memory; I checked the sums of the weights with a small program: 16/16, 6/8, 48/48, 42/42, 32/32 and 4/4; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 96 cells, the margin 0.03, the 8 steps, the 6 configurations (the pairing of kernel and image), the lit tone 0.92 with a dot radius of 0.47 cell, the dark tone 0.1 with a radius of 0.12 cell, the pale-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being: (1) **cell by cell agreement**: the lit/dark state read back at the centres of the 96×96 cells equals the error diffusion written in the test as a **pull** (the error arriving in a cell is the sum of the shares of the errors of the cells already processed, where the sampler pushes the error to the cells to come) in every cell (0 cells differ in the probe, the test allows 0.001 for ties in the floating-point sums), while the dither of each of the other 5 configurations differs from the read-back for over 0.2 of the cells (0.2998 at the lowest in the probe); (2) **the mean grey level is kept**: the kernels whose weights add up to 1 send the whole error on, so the number of lit cells equals the sum of the grey levels of the source image (the error can only fall off the edges): the difference is under 0.01 of the cells (0.0053 at the most in the probe, for all six), and on strips of 12 columns the lit fraction differs from the mean grey level by under 0.03 for the five kernels that keep the error (0.026 at the most in the probe), while Atkinson (which sends on only 3/4 of the error) goes over 0.05 (0.0853), with a negative sign in the darkest strip and a positive one in the lightest (−0.058 and 0.058 in the probe). Mutation checks (done twice): with one weight of Floyd–Steinberg changed from 5 to 4, 2 of the 6 tests of that describe fail (the cell-by-cell agreement and the seed difference) and the mean-grey-level test does **not** notice (the weights then add up to 15/16 and the difference stays under 0.01); with the lit/dark threshold changed from 0.5 to 0.6, 3 of the 6 fail (the tone ranges, the cell-by-cell agreement and the mean grey level); both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the agreement with the dither, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.300) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the weights of the kernels were written from my memory in both the sampler and the test, so (1) cannot find a weight that I remembered wrongly in the same way twice; I checked the sums with a small program but did not compare with the literature; (c) the pull and the push are two ways of writing the same algorithm, not two algorithms, with a different order of the floating-point sums; (d) the local density of 8×8 blocks deviates more (0.04 to 0.12 at the most in the probe), so the tests use only the whole picture and the strips of 12 columns; (e) only the raster order is used, no serpentine scan. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version mapped the cells to the plot area treating the half width as the full width, so the picture took only about a quarter of the middle of the tile, which I noticed in the preview; it was changed to (fu − 0.5) / (2·half width) + 0.5 and measured again; (2) the new tests all passed the first time (7 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 81, seed ^ salt)` picks a configuration; the 96×96 lit/dark cells are computed by error diffusion in raster order (the grey level of the source image: the horizontal ramp column / 95, the 8 steps (⌊8·column / 96⌋ + 0.5) / 8, the radial one 1 − the distance to the centre / (√2·the distance of the centre), the diagonal ramp (column + row) / 190), using a `Uint8Array(9216)` and a `Float64Array(9216)` (about 82 KB together) and the 128² grain cache; at sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into cell coordinates, the lit or dark state of the cell is taken, with the dot kernel clamp(1 − r² / R²) (R = 0.47 cell for a lit cell, 0.12 cell for a dark one); ink = edge fade·tone (lit 0.92, dark 0.1)·kernel², color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time** (the construction is 96×96 cells with at most 12 diffusion targets each). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one configuration (the 6 chosen 6, 5, 8, 4, 3 and 14 times; seeds 5, 8, 0, 9, 4 and 1 for the configurations 0 to 5) and the read-back of every seed equals the push-form dither exactly; the colour at the centre of a lit cell is at least 0.447 and that of a dark cell at most 0.147; the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 8.086%/8.018%/8.047%, color is 0.025608–0.025695 to 0.812210–0.814435 with a mean of 0.124061–0.124657, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.795836–0.802129 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 7.65%/7.64%/7.69%/7.67%, color is 0.025224–0.025290 to 0.813773–0.815387 with a mean of 0.124593–0.125205, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.79985–0.804088 relief; between seeds 5 and 8 4.99% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (34.62, 42.87, 51.12), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0241 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('errordiffusion', { size: 512, seed: 5, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`keplerorbits` adds Kepler orbits, bringing the current catalog from 1102 to 1103 kinds (1104 gallery choices including plain). Light violet on a dark purple-black: a star in the middle (the focus shared by all the orbits) and four elliptical orbits (thin lines) around it, with a bright dot at every **equal time step** along each orbit and a faint spoke from the star to each dot, so that the sectors between the spokes have equal areas (Kepler's second law: the dots are far apart near the perihelion and crowded near the aphelion); the positions of the dots come from Kepler's equation M = E − e·sin E (solved by Newton's method), E being the eccentric anomaly; the semi-major axis of each orbit follows from the third law, a^(3/2) proportional to the period (that is, to the number N of equal time steps in a period, so a ∝ N^(2/3)), scaled so that the largest aphelion is 0.85 (the half width of the picture being 1); the seed picks one of 6 configurations of 4 orbits, each with [dots per period, eccentricity, direction of the perihelion in degrees, the phase of the first dot], for example configuration 0 is [8, 0.55, 20°, 0], [14, 0.3, 140°, 0.4], [22, 0.5, 250°, 0.7] and [32, 0.2, 80°, 0.2] (the other 5 are in the preset). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern, not an ephemeris: only two-body Kepler motion without perturbations. Unlike `ellipsebilliard` (the path of a ball in an elliptical table) and `confocalconics` (a grid of confocal conics) (I read only the beginnings of their README entries), it draws Kepler's laws. (The form of Kepler's equation and of the second and third laws is from my memory and I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the largest aphelion 0.85, the 4 orbits, the dots per period, eccentricity, direction and phase of each orbit, the orbit half width 0.0035, the spoke half width 0.0016, the dot radius 0.016, the star radius 0.024 (tile units), the violet-on-dark-purple-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version, seeds 7, 13, 1, 2, 9 and 0); in the composition the orbits all lie to one side of the star (which is in the middle of the tile) and I did not change that. The curve distance is a first-order approximation: the implicit function of the ellipse divided by its gradient. The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written (the test solves Kepler's equation by its own Newton iteration and uses the implicit function of the ellipse and the area integral of a conic): (1) the orbits, time steps and star: of the pixels with a colour above 0.45 inside the plot (7605 to 9872 per configuration), the fraction lying within 0.8 of the half width of an ellipse of the configuration (the semi-major axes being calculated in the test from the third law a ∝ N^(2/3)), or within 1.1 dot radii of any equal-time-step dot solved in the test, or within 1.1 star radii of the star, is above 0.99 for the configuration of the seed (1.0000 in the probe) and below 0.4 for each other configuration (0.2659 at most in the probe); (2) **a bright dot at every equal time step**: at the 72 to 92 dot positions calculated in the test (for all 6 configurations) the colour is above 0.8 (0.846 at the lowest in the probe), and so it is at the star; this checks Kepler's equation (sampling the eccentric anomaly uniformly would misplace the dots on the orbits of high eccentricity) and the third law together (a wrong orbit size makes (1) and (2) fail); (3) **the second law**: for the dots at least 0.05 from the star and 0.045 from every other time step (tile units), the centre of the bright disc is read back (the weighted centroid of the colour above 0.8 within 0.025, in steps of 0.001), and for consecutive dots on one orbit that can both be read, the area swept between them, the integral of r²/2 over the angle along the conic r = a(1 − e²) / (1 + e·cos(θ − ω)), is within 4% of the area of the ellipse divided by the number of steps (5 to 41 pairs per configuration and 0.0156 at the worst in the probe). Mutation checks (done twice): with the number of Newton iterations changed to 0, 4 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the fit of the orbits and dots, the dot positions and the second law); with the exponent 2/3 of the semi-major axis changed to 0.5, 6 of the 7 fail; both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the brightness at the independent dot positions, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.848) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) **the third law was not measured independently from the picture**: the geometry of the test is calculated with a ∝ N^(2/3), so (1) and (2) only show that the picture matches that geometry; I tried to estimate a from the perihelion and aphelion distances measured along a ray in the direction of the perihelion, the error was up to 3.5% (from crossings with the lines of other orbits), the deviation from the third law came to 3.7%, which was not stable enough and I abandoned that check; (c) the second law is checked only for isolated pairs of dots (5 to 41 pairs per configuration); dots of different orbits that are too close merge into one bright spot on the picture: the number of connected pieces with a colour above 0.8 is smaller than the number of dots plus the star for configurations 1, 3, 4 and 5 (83 against 85, 92 against 93, 72 against 73 and 88 against 89), so there is no test of the number of connected dot pieces; (d) the positions of the orbit lines and the spokes are only checked through the first-order half width in (1), the spokes are not checked on their own; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version of the isolation rule for the second-law test used 0.06 and left 0 to 13 pairs, so it was relaxed to 0.05 and 0.045, leaving 5 to 41 pairs; (2) the new tests all passed the first time (8 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 80, seed ^ salt)` picks a configuration; for each orbit a = scale·N^(2/3) (the scale making the largest a(1 + e) 0.85) and b = a·√(1 − e²); for every equal time step j, M = 2π(j + phase) / N, Kepler's equation E − e·sin E = M is solved by Newton's method (12 steps) and the position (a(cos E − e), b·sin E) is rotated by the direction of the perihelion, giving about 72 to 92 points; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain and these points. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into (x, y) (y up, half width 1); for every orbit the first-order distance (the implicit function ((x' + a·e) / a)² + (y' / b)² − 1 divided by its gradient) with the kernel clamp(1 − d² / 0.0035²); for every dot the distance to the point (kernel radius 0.016) and to the segment from the star to it (kernel half width 0.0016); the star is a disc of radius 0.024; ink is the union `1 − Π(1 − tone·kernel²)` (orbits 0.6, spokes 0.2, dots and star 1) times the fade by the signed distance to the plot rectangle, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (two distances per dot per pixel, at most 92 dots). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one configuration (the 6 chosen 8, 7, 8, 5, 5 and 7 times; seeds 7, 13, 1, 2, 9 and 0 for the configurations 0 to 5); the total numbers of dots for the configurations 0 to 5 are 76, 84, 78, 92, 72 and 88; the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 3.055%/2.692%/2.904%, color is 0.025513–0.025618 to 0.869168–0.871102 with a mean of 0.069059–0.072856, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.866479–0.869988 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 3.02%/2.68%/2.89%/2.90%, color is 0.025125–0.025184 to 0.870660–0.872834 with a mean of 0.069079–0.072836, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.869252–0.875079 relief; between seeds 7 and 13 5.35% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (27.11, 19.36, 42.63), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0177 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('keplerorbits', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`zerovelocitycurves` adds zero-velocity curves, bringing the current catalog from 1101 to 1102 kinds (1103 gallery choices including plain). Thin golden lines on a dark teal-black: the contours of the effective potential Ω = (x² + y²)/2 + (1 − μ)/r₁ + μ/r₂ of the circular restricted three-body problem (two primaries of masses 1 − μ and μ moving in circles about their centre of mass, and a third body of negligible mass) in the rotating frame, which are the boundaries of the zero-velocity curves (the Hill regions); the primaries are at (−μ, 0) and (1 − μ, 0), the half width of the picture is 1.8 (in units of the distance between the primaries), each primary being a small disc; the thin lines are about 16 contours above the minimum Ω = 3/2 − μ(1 − μ)/2 at L4 and L5, starting at 0.04 above it with a ratio of 1.45; the brighter and thicker lines are the critical contours: the three through the saddle points L1, L2 and L3 (which decide the topology of the Hill region: the dumbbell, horseshoe and tadpole regions) and the contour of L4 and L5 that shrinks to two points; L1, L2 and L3 are on the x axis at the zeros of the force along the axis (found by bisection when the sampler is built) and L4 and L5 are at (1/2 − μ, ±√3/2); the seed picks one of 6 mass ratios μ: 0.5 (equal masses), 0.3, 0.12, 0.01215 (Earth and Moon), 0.0009537 (Sun and Jupiter) and 0.04. The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern, not an orbit simulation. Unlike `cylinderflow` and `fieldlines` (contours of a potential flow and of an electric field) it is the potential of a rotating frame with a centrifugal term. (The potential of the circular restricted three-body problem, the positions of the Lagrange points and the formula for the minimum at L4 and L5 are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests use a potential, a bisection and closed forms written separately in the test.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the half width 1.8, the start 0.04 and the ratio 1.45 of the levels, the line half widths 0.0035 (regular) and 0.006 (critical) (tile units), the primary disc radius 0.06 + 0.08·mass, the 6 mass ratios, the gold-on-dark-teal-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The line distance is a first-order approximation: the potential difference divided by the strength of the force; 1×10⁻³ (it was 1×10⁻⁴) is added to the squared force to avoid dividing by zero at a saddle point. The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written: (1) the fit: of the pixels with a colour above 0.45 (16298 to 19392 per configuration) more than 0.3 from both primaries, the fraction lying within 0.8 of the critical half width of a drawn level (regular and critical) of the potential calculated in the test is above 0.97 for the mass ratio of the seed (0.985 to 1.000 in the probe) and below 0.9 for each other mass ratio (0.836 at most in the probe, for the neighbouring ratios 0.01215 and 0.0009537); (2) **a bright critical contour through each Lagrange point**: L1, L2 and L3 are the zeros of the force along the axis found by bisection in the test, and L4 and L5 are at (1/2 − μ, ±√3/2), where the test also checks that the potential equals the minimum 3/2 − μ(1 − μ)/2 to within 1×10⁻¹²; the colour at all five points is above 0.75 (0.814 at the lowest in the probe); (3) **the number of contours across the axis**: on the axis between the primaries (starting 0.15 plus a mass-dependent part from each primary) the number of runs with a colour above 0.45 is exactly the number of roots, found in the test by sign changes and bisection, of the potential at each drawn level, plus 1 (the critical level of L1 only touches the axis there, with no sign change): 7, 7, 7, 10 and 8 for the mass ratios 0.5, 0.3, 0.12, 0.01215 and 0.04; the ratio 0.0009537 is not tested: its two closest lines are only 0.0364 apart (0.0093 in tile units, less than the sum of their half widths) and merge into one run, 11 runs against 12 roots in the probe; (4) **mirror symmetry**: the potential does not depend on the sign of y, so the fraction of cells of a 256² grid whose lit state differs is under 0.006 (0.0038 at most in the probe), and for the equal masses (μ = 0.5) the mirror about x = 0 is as well (0.0027), while for the other mass ratios it changes over 0.02 of the cells (0.0286 at the lowest in the probe). Mutation checks (done twice): with the critical level of L2 removed, 4 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the Lagrange points, the seed difference and the maps) but the fit and the number of contours across the axis do **not** notice (L2 lies outside the primaries and one line fewer does not change the fit fraction of the others); with the potential term of the second primary multiplied by 1.1, 7 of the 8 fail; both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the fit of the bright pixels to the independent contours, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.183; the table was measured with the squared force regularised by 1×10⁻⁴, the choice of the mass ratio for a seed does not depend on the regularisation, and the fit fractions of each mass ratio were measured again with 1×10⁻³) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the levels of the regular contours (start, ratio, upper limit) are repeated in the test from the preset, so (1) and (3) do not check the choice of the levels; (c) the distance is a first-order approximation and is not exact near the saddle points; (d) the mass ratio 0.0009537 has no check of the contours across the axis; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first probe used a fit threshold that was too loose (the largest margin was only 0.013), and using the colour at the centres of the primaries to tell the mass ratios apart tied for 0.01215 and 0.0009537 (their second primaries are less than 0.0012 apart); the tight fit fraction with the critical levels included separates them; (2) the probe found one more run on the axis than there are sign-change roots, because the critical contour of L1 is tangent to the axis, and adding that one makes them agree; (3) with 1×10⁻⁴ the C1 sweep had 1 violation each for the mass ratios 0.01215 and 0.0009537 (second differences of the occlusion of 0.0348 and 0.0307, just over 0.03, near u ≈ 0.25 and 0.49), which I believe is rounding noise amplified by large derivatives near a saddle point (not checked separately), so the regularisation was changed to 1×10⁻³ and with that the 6 configurations have 0 violations; this makes the lines a little wider near the saddle points; (4) the new tests all passed the first time (9 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 79, seed ^ salt)` picks a mass ratio μ; L1, L2 and L3 (the zeros of the force along the axis) and their potentials are found by bisection, and with the minimum 3/2 − μ(1 − μ)/2 these give 4 critical levels; the regular levels are minimum + 0.04·1.45^k while Ω < 14 (about 16); there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into (x, y) (y up, half width 1.8); Ω = (x² + y²)/2 + (1 − μ)/r₁ + μ/r₂ and the gradient is (x − (1 − μ)(x + μ)/r₁³ − μ(x − 1 + μ)/r₂³, y − (1 − μ)y/r₁³ − μy/r₂³), the strength being √(|∇Ω|² + 10⁻³) in tile units; the minimum of |Ω − level| over the regular levels and over the 4 critical levels is taken, with the kernel clamp(1 − (difference / strength)² / half width²); the primary discs have the kernel clamp(1 − r² / R²) with R = 0.06 + 0.08·mass; ink is the union `1 − Π(1 − tone·kernel²)` (regular 0.6, critical 0.95, primaries 1) times the fade by the signed distance to the plot rectangle, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (about 20 level comparisons per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one mass ratio (the 6 chosen 9, 6, 5, 5, 8 and 7 times; seeds 4, 1, 2, 11, 7 and 0 for the configurations 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations (regularisation 1×10⁻³); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 12.111%/11.732%/12.276%, color is 0.025414–0.025835 to 0.857597–0.864972 with a mean of 0.141510–0.150688, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.841255–0.854378 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 12.11%/11.86%/12.27%/11.73%, color is 0.025176–0.025246 to 0.857812–0.868178 with a mean of 0.141622–0.150589 (0.149346 for seed 7), AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.840009–0.862430 relief; between seeds 4 and 1 19.41% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (39.78, 45.51, 36.02), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0300 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('zerovelocitycurves', { size: 512, seed: 4, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`escapefractals` adds escape-time fractals, bringing the current catalog from 1100 to 1101 kinds (1102 gallery choices including plain). Glowing light-blue fractals on a dark blue-black: for each parameter c in the plane the escape-time iteration z → F(z) + c (z₀ = 0) is run for at most 150 steps and counts as escaped when |z|² exceeds 4096; a parameter that never escapes is inside the set (dark), and an escaped one gets a tone 0.2 + 0.7·(0.5 + 0.5·cos(2πν / 6)) from the smooth iteration count ν = n + 1 − ln(ln|z| / ln 64) / ln d, which gives a glowing gradient and contour bands around the set; the seed picks one of 6 configurations: the Burning Ship (F(z) = (|Re z| + i|Im z|)², centre (−0.45, −0.5), half width 1.8, the imaginary part growing downward), a zoom near the antenna of the Burning Ship (centre (−1.762, −0.028), half width 0.06), the tricorn (F(z) = z̄², centre (−0.3, 0), half width 1.8) and the multibrot sets of power 3, 4 and 5 (F(z) = z^d, centre (0, 0), half widths 1.5, 1.5 and 1.4). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. Unlike `mandelbrottiles` and `juliatiles` (a 64×64 table of rounded tiles of escape counts) it is a continuously sampled high-resolution picture and shows different sets. It is a schematic pattern, not a numerically exact boundary of the sets. (The definitions of the Burning Ship, the tricorn and the multibrot sets and their symmetries are from my memory and I did not check the literature; before writing the tests I measured the symmetries with a separate small program, see below.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 150 iterations at most, the escape radius 64, the tone band period 6, the inside tone 0.05 and the outside tones 0.2 to 0.9, the centre and half width of each of the 6 configurations, the light-blue-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version, seeds 7, 0, 6, 18, 2 and 1). **It is not C1**: the boundary of the set is a fractal, the tone jumps across it and the contour lines of the escape count have kinks everywhere near it, so the C1 sweep of the other materials does not apply here (I measured it first with the usual sweep: the 6 configurations had 2408, 11072, 363, 663, 564 and 627 violations); the test instead checks that the colour is smooth far from the set (at most 6 iterations to escape, 8 for the zoom of variant 1). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written (the test rewrites the iteration with complex numbers as objects and with the power by repeated multiplication): (1) the independent escape-time iteration: on a 128×128 grid whether a pixel is dark (inside the set) agrees completely with the test's own iteration (0 pixels disagree in the probe, the test allows under 0.002), the inside takes 0.0773 to 0.3579 of the grid (the test requires above 0.05), and for the escaped pixels the correlation of the colour with the tone calculated in the test from the smooth iteration count is above 0.99 (0.9972 to 0.9983 in the probe; the tone formula is repeated in the test, so this checks the iteration and the smooth count and not the choice of the tone); (2) **the extent of the set on the real axis**: the orbit of a real parameter stays real, so on the real axis the Burning Ship and the tricorn are inside from −2 to 1/4 (as for z² + c), and the multibrot z^d + c from −2^(1/(d−1)) (even power) or −(d − 1)·d^(−d/(d−1)) (odd power) to (d − 1)·d^(−d/(d−1)); scanning in steps of 0.0005, the first and last inside points are within 0.001 of these closed forms (the probe found 0.25, −1.99999 and 0.25, ±0.385, −1.2595 and 0.4725, and ±0.535); the left end of the Burning Ship is not tested, because the rounding of the imaginary part, about 1e-16, is amplified by the orbit near −2 and the probe found −1.9855, which I believe is the cause but did not check separately; (3) **symmetry**: the tricorn and the multibrots are symmetric under conjugation, the tricorn has 3-fold and the multibrot of power d (d − 1)-fold rotational symmetry, and on 4000 points the inside/outside state of the mirrored or rotated parameter differs for under 0.002 of them (none in the probe); I also measured with a separate program that does not use the sampler that the Burning Ship is not symmetric under conjugation (about 33.6% of the points differ), so its symmetry is not tested; (4) **smooth far from the set and periodic**: at points that escape in at most 6 iterations (8 for variant 1) the second difference over a step of 1e-10 divided by the step is under 0.03 (7.05×10⁻⁴ at the worst in the probe, 20000 points per configuration), and shifting the UV by whole periods gives the same output (1.6×10⁻¹⁴ at the worst in the probe). Mutation checks (done twice): with the absolute value of the imaginary part removed from the Burning Ship, 4 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the independent iteration, the seed difference and the maps) while the real-axis test does not notice (the imaginary part is 0 on the real axis, so the change does not affect it); with the conjugation sign of the tricorn changed (making it the Mandelbrot set), 3 of the 7 fail (the independent iteration, the symmetry and the smoothness); both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the agreement of the inside/outside classification with the independent iteration on a 40×40 grid, taking the best one, without printing the agreement fraction of each seed) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) being inside is decided by a colour below 0.12, so an outside pixel with a very dark tone (if any) would count as inside — the probe and the test verify against the independent iteration, with 0 disagreeing; (c) nothing checks the tone close to the boundary of the set; (d) membership uses only addition, subtraction, multiplication and absolute values, which should be identical in Node and Bun, but I measured it only in those two environments and did not verify it in a browser GPU or another engine; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments and discarded attempts**: (1) before this I had implemented 'the points of an elliptic curve over a finite field' (`ellipticcurvedots`) and rendered previews: the dots were sparse, the tone differences (the rank of the group order) were hardly visible and most of the picture was empty, so I abandoned and reverted it without committing; (2) I measured the symmetries and the real-axis extents with a separate small program before writing the tests: the Burning Ship is not symmetric under conjugation (I had expected it to be, and only the measurement showed it is not), so I made no such claim; (3) the new tests all passed the first time (7 tests of the describe plus the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 78, seed ^ salt)` picks a configuration; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into the parameter c = centre + ((u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46)·half width; starting from z = 0, at most 150 times: the Burning Ship z ← (|Re z| + i|Im z|)² + c, the tricorn z ← z̄² + c, the multibrot z ← z^d + c (by repeated multiplication, not Math.pow); it escapes when |z|² > 4096; the inside has ink 0.05 and an escaped parameter has ink = 0.2 + 0.7·(0.5 + 0.5·cos(2πν / 6)), multiplied by the fade by the signed distance to the plot rectangle; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time**; in the worst case each pixel takes 150 iterations (d − 1 complex multiplications each for the multibrot) and every pixel inside the set runs all of them; I did not time the probes. Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one configuration (the 6 chosen 4, 5, 7, 6, 7 and 11 times; seeds 7, 0, 6, 18, 2 and 1 for the configurations 0 to 5); the inside takes 0.1828, 0.0803, 0.0773, 0.2642, 0.2932 and 0.3579 of the probe grid for the configurations 0 to 5; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 30.714%/6.033%/31.032%, color is 0.025664–0.026413 to 0.80142–0.80190 with a mean of 0.222210–0.379806, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.787233–0.788659 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 30.60%/6.09%/31.09%/29.09%, color is 0.025097–0.025494 to 0.80180–0.80253 with a mean of 0.222685–0.379820, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.78817–0.79019 relief; between seeds 7 and 0 27.52% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (45.51, 90.51, 106.65), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0377 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('escapefractals', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`fourierseries` adds Fourier-series partial sums, bringing the current catalog from 1099 to 1100 kinds (1101 gallery choices including plain). Orange curves on a dark brown-black: the tile is divided into 4 rows, each drawing one period of the Fourier **partial sum** of a waveform, with the number of terms growing from the top row to the bottom — a square wave (4/π)·Σ sin((2j + 1)x) / (2j + 1), a sawtooth (2/π)·Σ (−1)^(k+1) sin(kx) / k, or a triangle wave (8/π²)·Σ cos((2j + 1)x) / (2j + 1)²; each row has dim thin horizontal lines at 0 and ±1 (the amplitude is 0.085); the seed picks one of 6 configurations (the waveform and the number of terms of the 4 rows): a square wave with 1, 2, 4 and 10 terms; a square wave with 2, 3, 6 and 16; a sawtooth with 1, 2, 4 and 10; a triangle wave with 1, 2, 3 and 6; a sawtooth with 2, 4, 8 and 20; and a square wave with 3, 5, 8 and 20. The square wave and the sawtooth show the Gibbs phenomenon at their jumps: however many terms are summed, the first peak overshoots by about 9% of the jump and only gets narrower; the triangle wave has no jump and so no overshoot. The tile has exactly one period horizontally and the 4 rows repeat vertically, so it is a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern; the curve is a first-order distance approximation, so its steep parts at the jumps are drawn as a straight stroke. Unlike the other materials this one draws the graphs of functions, not a two-dimensional pattern. (The coefficients of the series and the Gibbs constant (2/π)·Si(π) ≈ 1.179 are from my memory; the test computes that constant by numerical integration; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 4 rows, the amplitude 0.085, the curve half width 0.005 and the half width 0.0022 of the horizontal lines (tile units), the tones 0.92 / 0.16 / 0.1 of the curve and the lines, the 6 configurations, the orange-on-dark-brown-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version; seeds 0 to 5 happen to cover all 6). The distance to the curve is a first-order approximation: the height difference divided by √(1 + slope²). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on the recurrence of the sampler (the test sums the terms one by one): (1) the fit: the fraction of the pixels with a colour above 0.5 (5682 to 7404 per variant) lying within 0.8 of the half width of the curve of the partial sum calculated in the test is above 0.99 for the configuration of the seed (1.0000 in the probe) and below 0.6 for each other configuration (0.454 at most in the probe); (2) **the Gibbs overshoot**: in the rows of the square waves with at least 8 terms (4 rows with 10, 16, 8 and 20 terms) the centre of the stroke at the first peak x = π / (2m) (the slope of the partial sum is proportional to sin(2mx) / sin(x)) is within 0.004 of the direct sum in the test (0.0009 at the most in the probe) and its excess over 1 is a fraction of the jump of 2 that is within 0.003 of the Gibbs constant (2/π·Si(π) − 1) / 2 = 0.08949 (0.0892 to 0.0901 in the probe), the integral being computed in the test by the midpoint rule; (3) **the plateaus flatten**: on the plateau of a square wave (x from π/4 to 3π/4, at 65 columns) the largest distance of the stroke centre from 1 is within 0.004 of that of the direct sum (0.0014 at the most in the probe) and gets smaller from each row to the next (0.2728, 0.2005, 0.1088 and 0.0435 for configuration 0 in the probe); (4) **the symmetry of the waveform**: the square wave and the sawtooth are odd (unchanged by a half turn about the middle of each row), the triangle wave is even (unchanged by a left-right mirror), and the square wave is also mirror symmetric about x = π/2; the fraction of lit pixels that differ is under 0.03 for the symmetries that hold (0.0178 at the most in the probe) and over 1 for the ones that do not (1.4247 at the lowest in the probe). Mutation checks (done twice): with the signs of the sawtooth all made positive only 1 of the 8 tests of that describe fails (the fit); with the square-wave coefficient 4/π changed to 1.2, 4 of the 8 fail (the fit, the Gibbs overshoot, the plateaus and the seed difference); both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the fit fraction, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.545) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the Gibbs and plateau checks cover only the square wave; the sawtooth and the triangle wave have only the fit (1) and the symmetry (4), and the symmetry check cannot tell the sign pattern of the sawtooth (the mutation check above confirmed this); (c) the series formulas in the test and in the sampler were both written from my memory, so (1) cannot find a coefficient I remembered wrongly; the 4/π and 1/k structure of the square wave is indirectly supported by the independent integral constant in (2), while the sawtooth and the triangle wave have no such independent check; (d) the curve is a first-order approximation and the steep parts at the jumps are not exact; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version had horizontal-line tones 0.3 and 0.18 and a curve half width of 0.004 and looked like ruled paper, so they were changed to 0.16, 0.1 and 0.005; (2) the first draft of the sampler text had a mistake in the operator precedence of the loop bound and a leftover temporary expression in the ink formula, which I found on re-reading and corrected before it was generated into the repository; (3) the new tests all passed the first time, without any threshold being adjusted, the numbers having been measured with a probe before being written into the tests.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 76, seed ^ salt)` picks a configuration; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): row = floor(4·v), y = (0.5 − position within the row) / 4 (up, 0 on the centre of the row); x = 2π(u − 0.5); sin(kx) and cos(kx) are obtained term by term with the rotation recurrence from sin x and cos x (at most 39 terms), accumulating the partial sum and its slope in x; value = 0.085·coefficient·sum and slope = 0.085·coefficient·slope sum·2π (in u); the curve distance = |y − value| / √(1 + slope²) and the curve kernel is clamp(1 − d² / 0.005²); the horizontal lines (y = 0 and |y| = 0.085) have a kernel half width of 0.0022; ink = 1 − (1 − 0.92·curve²)(1 − 0.16·level²)(1 − 0.1·zero line²), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. The tile is periodic in both u and v. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time**. Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one configuration (the 6 chosen 10, 5, 7, 5, 7 and 6 times; seeds 0, 2, 5, 4, 1 and 3 for the configurations 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 2.565%/2.351%/2.280%, color is 0.025449–0.025727 to 0.814705–0.819251 with a mean of 0.061657–0.064263, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.801947–0.807114 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 2.575%/2.315%/2.242%/2.240%, color is 0.025089–0.025267 to 0.819307–0.823439 with a mean of 0.063496–0.066318, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.807195–0.812316 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 4.106% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (36.81, 17.02, 7.57), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0297 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('fourierseries', { size: 512, seed: 0, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`twosourcewaves` adds two-source interference, bringing the current catalog from 1098 to 1099 kinds (1100 gallery choices including plain). Light green bands on a dark green-black: two point sources in phase send out waves of the same wavelength, and the brightness is the time-averaged intensity cos²(π(r₁ − r₂) / wavelength) — a bright band where the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths (constructive) and a dark line where it is a half-integer number; the dark lines are hyperbolas with the two sources as foci, and the perpendicular bisector (path difference 0) is always bright; the two sources are small bright dots (the distance function has a cusp at a source, so the intensity is faded to 0.5 within a radius of 0.01 + 0.012); the seed picks one of 6 configurations (the spacing of the sources in wavelengths, the wavelength in tile units, the angle of the line through them): (2.25, 0.08, 0°), (3.75, 0.06, 30°), (5.3, 0.05, 90°), (7.1, 0.04, 0°), (9.2, 0.035, 60°) and (11.2, 0.04, 15°). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern with no decay of the waves, polarisation or time dependence; unlike `raindropripples` (8×8 drops with random amplitudes and phases), `quasicrystal` (a periodic sum of plane waves) and `moirefringes` (two gratings multiplied), it has only two sources and a closed form for the path difference, so the number and the positions of the dark lines can be calculated directly. (The formula for the interference of two sources is from my memory and I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the source dot radius 0.01 and its blend 0.012, the wave tone 0.85, the 6 configurations, the light-green-on-dark-green-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler writes its formula: (1) the Pearson correlation between the intensity cos²(π(r₁ − r₂) / wavelength) written in the test and the colour on a 64×64 grid (0.1 to 0.9, more than 0.05 from a source) is above 0.99 for the configuration of the seed (0.9954 at the lowest in the probe) and below 0.3 in size for each other configuration (0.214 at most in the probe); (2) **the number of dark lines**: the dark lines are the hyperbolas where the path difference is (m + ½) wavelengths for m = 0, 1, … below the spacing in wavelengths, M = ⌈spacing − ½⌉ of them on each side (calculated in the test, M = 2, 4, 5, 7, 9 and 11), and a circle larger than the spacing of the sources (radius 0.3 and 0.4) crosses each branch exactly twice, so the circle has exactly 4M dark runs (colour below 0.3; 8, 16, 20, 28, 36 and 44 in the probe), a count that does not depend on the shape of the lines; (3) **the positions of the dark lines**: on the line through the sources the path difference is −2s, so the dark lines are at s = ±(m + ½)·wavelength / 2; scanning in steps of 0.0002 (stopping 0.03 short of each source), the middle of every dark run lying wholly inside the scan is within 0.001 of such a position and every position whose dark band (0.15 wavelength to each side) lies wholly inside has a run (0.0002 at the worst in the probe for the configurations where the match was made); (4) **the perpendicular bisector is fully bright**: from −0.38 to 0.38 in steps of 0.002 the colour is above 0.7 (0.737 at the lowest in the probe); (5) **symmetry**: swapping the two sources (a half turn about the middle) leaves cos² unchanged, so the fraction of cells of a 256² grid whose lit state differs is under 0.015 (0.0089 at most in the probe, which I suppose comes from the fine grain without having tested it), and for the configurations whose line of sources runs along an axis (0, 2 and 3) the left-right and top-bottom mirrors are under 0.015 as well (0.0094 at most), while for the others the mirrors change over 0.2 of the cells (0.3895 at the lowest). Mutation checks (done twice): with the weight of r₂ changed to 0.9, several tests of that describe fail (only the first 8 lines of the output were read, so I did not read the total); with the wavelength multiplied by 1.03, 6 of the 9 tests of that describe fail (tone ranges, the fit, the number of dark lines, their positions, the seed difference and the maps), while the bisector, symmetry and C1 tests still pass (they do not depend on the wavelength or are not affected by that change); both were restored. **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation with the independent intensity, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.79) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) within 0.03 of a source the positions and numbers of dark lines are not checked; (c) the tests do not check the shape of the hyperbolas as such, only their number, their positions and the fully bright bisector; (d) I did not check the formula against the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version faded the source dots with radius 0.012 and blend 0.02 and this was changed to 0.01 and 0.012 so that the dark bands near a source are not altered by the blend; (2) the first version of configuration 5 had a spacing of 11.4 wavelengths and the probe found 46 runs on the circle instead of 44: the largest path difference (11.4 wavelengths) reaches into the dark tail of the next dark line (11.5 wavelengths), which adds two dark runs at the ends of the line of sources, so it was changed to 11.2 wavelengths (the fractional parts of the other spacings are far enough from 0.5); (3) in the first probe the comparison of the dark-line positions counted or missed runs cut by the ends of the scan (a probe problem, not the sampler), and the test now counts only runs wholly inside the scan; (4) the first run of the new tests had 1 failure, my own arbitrary guard of 'at least 4 positions' (configuration 0 has only 2), which I changed to at least 2 without touching the sampler.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 75, seed ^ salt)` picks a configuration; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): the two sources are at (0.5, 0.5) ± half the spacing·(cos θ, sin θ); r₁ and r₂ are the distances to them and wave = 0.5 + 0.5·cos(2π(r₁ − r₂) / wavelength); close to a source the wave is blended to 0.5 with smooth(clamp((r − 0.01) / 0.012)); ink = clamp(rectangle fade·(0.85·wave + 1·source dots)), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. What is outside the plot is faded by the signed distance to its rectangle. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (two square roots and a cosine per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one configuration (the 6 chosen 4, 5, 8, 7, 9 and 7 times; seeds 10, 6, 0, 2, 1 and 3 for the configurations 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 37.236%/41.980%/40.077%, color is 0.025589–0.026014 to 0.86074–0.87029 with a mean of 0.364947–0.371966, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.84197–0.86743 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 37.20%/41.98%/40.06%/39.04%, color is 0.025107–0.025462 to 0.86224–0.87049 with a mean of 0.36267–0.37517, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.84597–0.86797 relief; between seeds 10 and 6 39.06% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (55.67, 103.95, 76.56), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0100 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('twosourcewaves', { size: 512, seed: 10, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`fieldlines` adds electric field lines and equipotentials, bringing the current catalog from 1097 to 1098 kinds (1099 gallery choices including plain). Pink lines on a dark purple-black: the field lines and equipotentials of several **line charges** (point charges in two dimensions) in the plane; the potential is φ = Σ q·ln r, the field is E = ∇φ = Σ q·(position − charge) / r², the field lines are contours of Σ q·atan2(…) taken at multiples of 2π / 12 (so each unit charge sends out 12 lines and a charge q sends out 12|q|, which is Gauss's law in two dimensions), and the equipotentials are drawn at multiples of 0.2 of φ as dimmer thinner lines that do not cover the field lines; each charge is a small disc (the lines merge inside it anyway); the seed picks one of 6 configurations of charges (position (x, y) and size q, the half width of the picture being 2.2): a dipole (−0.8, 0, +1) and (0.8, 0, −1); an equal pair (−0.8, 0, +1) and (0.8, 0, +1); 2 : −1 : −1 as (−0.9, 0, +2), (0.7, 0.7, −1) and (0.7, −0.7, −1); a quadrupole at (±0.8, ±0.8) with alternating signs; three equal charges at (0, 0.9) and (±0.8, −0.6); and four alternating charges along a line at x = −1.2, −0.4, 0.4, 1.2 (y = 0). The picture does not show the sign of a charge (the discs are drawn the same). The plot is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.05), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern, not an electromagnetic simulation. (The potential of line charges in two dimensions, the field lines as contours of Σ q θ and the Gauss's-law count are from my memory and I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.05, the half width 2.2, the 12 lines per unit charge, the equipotential spacing 0.2, the line half widths 0.02 and 0.014 (in plane units), the tone 0.4 of the equipotentials, the charge disc radius 0.13, the 6 configurations, the pink-on-dark-purple-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version, seeds 12, 0, 2, 38, 4 and 1, variants 0 to 5 by the probe's table). The distance to a line is a first-order approximation: the difference in angle (or potential) divided by the strength of the field, so the lines are narrower on the tile where the field is strong (close to a charge) and wider where it is weak (near a zero); that is part of the design. 1×10⁻⁴ is added to the squared field strength to avoid dividing by zero at a null point. The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler writes its formulas: (1) with the field and the sum of q·atan2 written in the test, the fraction of the pixels with a colour above 0.5 more than 0.4 from every charge (4559 to 11704 per variant) lying within 0.8 of the first-order half width of a field line is above 0.99 for the configuration of the seed (1.000 in the probe) and below 0.4 for each other configuration (0.22 at most in the probe); (2) **Gauss's law**: on a circle of radius 0.35 around each charge the number of separate runs of pixels with a colour above 0.5 (the field lines; the equipotentials are dimmer and not counted) is exactly 12|q| (12 for q = 1 and 24 for q = 2; all 18 charges of the 6 configurations agree in the probe), a topological count that does not depend on the position of the lines or how the formula is written; (3) **the lines run in the direction of the field**: at every third pixel with a colour above 0.75 (the middle of a line) more than 0.6 from every charge and whose neighbourhood (radius 4 pixels, colour above 0.5) has at least 8 pixels and is clearly elongated, the angle of the line differs from the direction of the field by under 11.5 degrees (|sin| below 0.2) for all of them (108 to 317 pixels per variant, 0.127 at the worst in the probe); (4) **mirror symmetry**: reversing the sign of every charge leaves the set of field lines and equipotentials unchanged, so a mirror image of the charges that differs only by sign leaves the picture unchanged: left to right for variants 0, 1, 3, 4 and 5 (the fraction of pixels whose lit state differs is under 0.003, 0.0011 at most in the probe) and top to bottom for variants 0, 1, 2, 3 and 5, while the other mirrors change over 0.05 of the pixels (0.0998 and 0.1071 in the probe); (5) **a line through the null point**: the field of two equal charges vanishes at the middle point (0, 0) and that of three equal charges at the point of least field strength found by a scan of the plane in steps of 0.01 ((0, 0.09), with a strength of 0.0019), and a line goes through each (a separatrix whose value is, by symmetry, a multiple of the line spacing), the colour being above 0.7 (0.785 and 0.790 in the probe). Mutation check (done once): with q replaced by sign(q) in the angle sum (ignoring the size of a charge), 3 of the 9 tests of that describe fail (the field-line fit, Gauss's law and the direction of the lines) while the others still pass; it has been restored (this change affects only configuration 2, which has a charge of 2, so the tests of the other configurations were not affected, and the mirror and null-point tests did not notice). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the fit to the independent field lines) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 are covered; configuration 3 is chosen by only 2 of 40 seeds); (b) the first-order line width approximation is the same on both sides in (1), so the physical content (the number of lines, their direction, the null points) is checked independently by (2), (3) and (5); (c) the equipotentials are only excluded from the count by being darker than 0.5 and are not checked on their own (orthogonality is not checked directly, only the direction of the field lines); (d) within 0.4 of a charge nothing is checked; (e) I did not check the formulas for charges in two dimensions against the literature. **Record of adjustments**: the first version drew a negative charge as a ring and a positive one as a disc, and after viewing the images I found that the lines merge into a solid within a distance of about 0.136 so the ring could not be seen; it was removed and now charges of both signs are drawn the same.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 74, seed ^ salt)` picks a configuration of charges; there is no large precomputation, only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into plane coordinates (x, y) (y up, half width 2.2); for each charge (cx, cy, q): dx = x − cx, dy = y − cy, r² = dx² + dy², and the sums angle += q·atan2(dy, dx), potential += 0.5·q·ln r², field += q·(dx, dy) / r² are accumulated together with the charge disc kernel clamp(1 − r² / 0.13²); the squared field strength is |E|² + 1×10⁻⁴; for the field lines with k = round(angle / (2π / 12)) the three lines k − 1, k and k + 1 each give t = clamp(1 − (angle − k·2π / 12)² / (squared strength·0.02²)), combined as `1 − t²`; the equipotentials use the potential, a spacing of 0.2 and a half width of 0.014 in the same way; ink = clamp(fade·(0.9·field lines + 0.4·equipotentials·(where there is no field line) + 1·charge discs)), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. What is outside the plot is faded by the signed distance to its rectangle. The angle sum jumps by 2πq across a branch cut, a whole number of line spacings, so the lines on the two sides join. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (an atan2 and a logarithm per charge per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one configuration (the 6 chosen 6, 10, 7, 2, 7 and 8 times; seeds 12, 0, 2, 38, 4 and 1 for the configurations 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 5.063%/4.005%/6.297%, color is 0.025436–0.025811 to 0.87110–0.87340 with a mean of 0.088129–0.119037, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.86960–0.87574 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 3.72%–6.15%, color is 0.025172–0.025256 to 0.87363–0.87423 with a mean of 0.088421–0.125129, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.87634–0.87796 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 8.90% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (44.16, 26.52, 48.65), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0340 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('fieldlines', { size: 512, seed: 12, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`cylinderflow` adds the flow past a cylinder, bringing the current catalog from 1096 to 1097 kinds (1098 gallery choices including plain). Pale-blue streamlines on a dark blue-black: the **ideal (inviscid, incompressible, irrotational) potential flow** of speed U from left to right past a cylinder of radius 1 with circulation Γ = 4π·U·a·g (clockwise for g > 0); the stream function is ψ = y·(1 − 1 / r²) + 2g·ln r (velocity (∂ψ/∂y, −∂ψ/∂x)), the streamlines being drawn at ψ = 0.2·k with an extra thicker **dividing streamline** (the one through the stagnation points); the cylinder itself is drawn as a dark teal disc with a bright rim. For g ≤ 1 the two stagnation points are on the surface of the cylinder (sin θ = −g) and for g > 1 they leave it and lie on the vertical axis at y = −(g + √(g² − 1)), with a closed streamline around the cylinder below. The seed picks one of 6 circulations g = 0, 0.5, 1, 1.25, 1.5 and 0.75; for g = 0 the picture is symmetric top to bottom and left to right and for g > 0 the streamlines above are closer together (a faster flow). The plot is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.05, the half width of the picture being 3.2 radii of the cylinder), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern and not a fluid simulation (no viscosity, wake or separation). (The stream function of potential flow past a cylinder, the stagnation points sin θ = −g and y = −(g + √(g² − 1)) for g > 1 are from my memory and my own derivation and I did not check the literature; the test's velocity formula was written separately by me from the polar components.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.05, the half width 3.2, the streamline spacing 0.2, the line half width 0.02 (in flow units), the half width of the dividing streamline 0.032, the fade into the cylinder 0.04, the rim half width 0.035, the 6 circulations, the pale-blue-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 circulations once (the montage of seeds 0 to 5 had g = 0.75, 0.5, 0.75, 0, 1 and 1.5, and seed 10 was rendered separately for g = 1.25). The distance to a line is a first-order approximation (the difference in ψ divided by the speed), so on the tile the width of a line varies where the flow is very fast (close to the cylinder) or very slow (near a stagnation point); that is part of the design and not the true distance. **C1 and the stagnation points**: the first version used dψ² / speed² directly and the C1 sweep had 14 violations for g = 1 (seed 4, 0.069 at the most) and 2 for g = 1.5 (0.039 and 0.032), all near stagnation points; I scanned the slope near such a point and found no jump along v, so it is not a crease but numerical error amplified by 1 / speed² (g = 1 is the degenerate case where the two stagnation points merge and the speed goes as the square of the distance to the stagnation point; the squared speed at the probe's point was only 7.7×10⁻⁶), and **I did not find out which step the error comes from**; with 1×10⁻⁴ added to the squared speed (which only thickens the lines slightly within 0.01 of a stagnation point) the C1 sweep has 0 violations for all 6 circulations. The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being independent checks: (1) with the stream function written in the test (from the polar form (r − 1 / r) sin θ + 2g ln r and not the sampler's Cartesian form) and the velocity computed just as independently, the fraction of the pixels with a colour above 0.5 outside radius 1.3 (16987 to 25319 per variant) lying within 0.8 of the first-order half width of a level ψ = 0.2k or of the dividing streamline is above 0.99 for the circulation of the seed (1.000 in the probe) and below 0.45 for each other circulation (0.304 at most in the probe); (2) **the lines run in the direction of the velocity**: at every third pixel with a colour above 0.75 (the middle of a line) outside radius 1.5 whose neighbourhood (radius 4 pixels, colour above 0.5) has at least 8 pixels and is clearly elongated (the larger eigenvalue of the covariance at least 3 times the smaller), the angle of the line differs from that of the velocity (from the polar components v_r = (1 − 1 / r²) cos θ and v_θ = −(1 + 1 / r²) sin θ − 2g / r, not from the stream function) by under 11.5 degrees (|sin| below 0.2) for at least 99% (0.9975 at the lowest in the probe; 478 to 801 pixels per variant) and by under 14.5 degrees for all of them (0.218 at the worst); (3) **mirror symmetry**: the stream function is even in x for all g and odd in y only for g = 0: on the 256 by 256 reading the fraction of pixels whose lit state differs from that at the mirror image in x is under 0.003 for every variant (0.0018 at most in the probe), and in y it is under 0.003 for g = 0 (0.0012) and above 0.1 for the others (0.1412 at the least); (4) **the dividing streamline passes through the stagnation points**: for g > 1 the colour at the stagnation point (0, −(g + √(g² − 1))) (−2 for g = 1.25 and −2.618 for g = 1.5) is above 0.7 (0.779 and 0.784 in the probe), and for g = 0 the dividing streamline is the axis y = 0 and the colour along it on both sides of the cylinder from x = 1.25 to 2.95 is above 0.7 (0.773 at the lowest). Mutation check (done once): with the sign of the vortex term in ψ only reversed (the gradient left unchanged, so ψ is inconsistent), 7 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (only the mirror symmetry still passes, as ψ stays even in x); it has been restored. **Limitations**: (a) the circulation for each seed was found with a probe (the fit to the independent stream function) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 are covered); (b) the first-order line width approximation is the same on both sides in (1), so that shows only that the sampler draws contours of this stream function, while the physical content (the stagnation points, the velocity) is checked independently by (2) and (4); (c) only the region outside radius 1.3 and the stagnation points are checked, not the neighbourhood of the cylinder surface or the faded edge; (d) I did not check these potential-flow formulas against the literature.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 73, seed ^ salt)` picks a circulation g; if g > 1 the value of the dividing streamline is ψ_s = −(r_s − 1 / r_s) + 2g ln r_s (r_s = g + √(g² − 1)) and otherwise 0; there is no large precomputation, only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into flow coordinates (x, y) (y up, half width 3.2) and r = √(x² + y²); ψ = y(1 − 1 / r²) + 2g ln r, the gradient is ψ_x = 2xy / r⁴ + 2gx / r² and ψ_y = 1 − 1 / r² + 2y² / r⁴ + 2gy / r², and the squared speed is ψ_x² + ψ_y² + 1×10⁻⁴; with k = floor(ψ / 0.2) the two streamlines k and k + 1 each give t = clamp(1 − (ψ − 0.2k)² / (squared speed·0.02²)), the dividing streamline gives the same with a half width of 0.032, each is combined as `1 − t²` and multiplied by the fade outside the cylinder smooth(clamp((r − 1) / 0.04)); the inside of the cylinder is a solid tone of 0.12, with a bright rim at r = 1 of clamp(1 − (r − 1)² / 0.035²)²; what is outside the plot is faded by the signed distance to its rectangle; ink = clamp(fade·(0.9·streamlines + 0.9·rim + 0.12·cylinder)), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (a logarithm and the kernels of 2 or 3 streamlines per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one circulation (the 6 chosen 12, 4, 9, 4, 7 and 4 times; seeds 3, 1, 4, 10, 5 and 0 for g = 0, 0.5, 1, 1.25, 1.5 and 0.75); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 8.754%/8.252%/8.260%, color is 0.025371–0.025556 to 0.87046–0.87201 with a mean of 0.116742–0.120564, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.86790–0.87203 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 8.33%–8.82%, color is 0.025124–0.025223 to 0.87312–0.87417 with a mean of 0.116767–0.120511, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.87498–0.87778 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 13.78% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (17.54, 36.87, 49.21), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0447 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 circulations). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('cylinderflow', { size: 512, seed: 5, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`sphericalharmonics` adds spherical harmonics, bringing the current catalog from 1095 to 1096 kinds (1097 gallery choices including plain). The tile is divided into 2 columns × 4 rows of 8 rectangular maps, each a longitude-latitude map of a **real spherical harmonic** Y_l^m: longitude φ (0 to 2π) across and colatitude θ (0 to π) down, with the tone 0.5 + 0.5·Y / the largest value of the map (so the nodal lines are the middle grey), Y = P_l^|m|(cos θ) times cos(mφ) (m ≥ 0) or sin(|m|φ) (m < 0); each map has a thin frame and fades to dark outside it; pale green on dark green-black; the seed picks where the 8 maps start (in the order l = 0, 1, 2, … with m = −l … l, the starts being 0, 4, 9, 16, 25 and 36, laid out row by row from the left and the top): start 0 is l = 0, l = 1 and the first 4 of l = 2; start 4 is the 5 of l = 2 and m = −3 to −1 of l = 3; start 9 is the 7 of l = 3 and m = −4 of l = 4; start 16 is the first 8 of l = 4 (m = −4 to 3); start 25 is m = −5 to 2 of l = 5; start 36 is m = −6 to 1 of l = 6. Properties: |m| of the nodal lines are meridians and l − |m| are parallels (the sectoral harmonics of l = |m| have no parallels, the zonal ones of m = 0 no meridians). The tile has a whole number of rectangles, so it is a periodic pattern (the unit being the whole tile, with a margin between maps). Unlike `zernikemodes` (Zernike polynomials on discs, tone (1 + Z) / 2) these are the harmonics of a sphere unrolled as rectangular longitude-latitude maps, with a grid of meridians and parallels for nodal lines and not the rings and sectors of a disc. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The number of zeros of the spherical harmonics, the explicit sum of the Legendre polynomial and the sign conventions are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the sign of a map is the one given by the recurrence and may differ by a sign from the textbook, which I did not compare, only the sign of the independent formula.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin of the maps 0.06 (as a fraction of the side of the cell), the frame half width 0.004, the fade 0.012, the tone 0.5 + 0.5·Y / the largest value, the 6 starts, the pale-green-on-dark-green-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 starts once (the montage of seeds 0 to 5 had starts 9, 9, 4, 16, 25 and 4, and seeds 8 and 9 were rendered separately for starts 0 and 36). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on the sampler's recurrence: (1) the independent real spherical harmonics are computed by **differentiating the explicit sum of the Legendre polynomial m times** (not the sampler's recurrence) and, with 400 points in each map, the Spearman rank correlation between the colour and the independent value over the 8 maps of the start of the seed is above 0.99 (0.998 at the lowest in the probe) and below 0.1 for each other start (0.04 at most in the probe); (2) **the number of nodal lines**: in each map of l ≥ 1, taking the colour at a nodal line as zero (the mean of 9 points along a nodal meridian, or along the parallel of the first root of the Legendre polynomial for m = 0) and ignoring colours within 0.04 of it (the grain), the sign changes along the parallel of the largest |P| (longitude 0.03 to 0.97 of the map) are 2|m| (2|m| − 1 for the sin kind, as its zero at longitude 0 is on the edge) and those down the meridian of the largest |wave| (colatitude 0.03 to 0.97) are l − |m| (all 47 maps in the probe agree); the map of l = 0 is flat to within the grain (a range of 0.0265 in the probe); (3) **the positions of the parallels of the zonal harmonics**: for the maps with m = 0 and l ≥ 2 (6 of them) the zero crossings of the colour (by linear interpolation between pixel centres) down a vertical line in the middle of the map are as many as the roots of the Legendre polynomial (found by a scan and bisection of its explicit sum) and each is within 1.5 pixels of a root (0.999 at worst in the probe). Mutation check (done once): with (l + m − 1) in the sampler's recurrence changed to (l + m), 6 of the 7 tests of that describe fail and only the C1 sweep passes; it has been restored. **Limitations**: (a) the start for each seed was found with a probe (by the rank correlation) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 are covered); (b) the nodal-line check restricts the sampling to 0.03 to 0.97 of the map because the fade at the edge of the map moves the colour away from the zero (my first probe did not restrict it and produced extra sign changes, which I only then fixed), so the nodal lines close to the poles and edges are not checked; (c) amplitude is not checked beyond l = 0 (the correlation looks only at order); (d) my first probe's scan for the roots of the Legendre polynomial missed the root x = 0 which fell exactly on a scan point (l = 1, 3, 5, giving false mismatches) and it was found only after I changed to an odd number of steps; (e) the sign convention is only compared with the sign of the independent formula (both contain (−1)^m) and not with a textbook.
