At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 72, seed ^ salt)` picks the start; for each of the 8 maps (l, m) is found from the index (1 harmonic for l = 0, 3 for l = 1, …) and 181 colatitudes are scanned for the largest |P_l^|m||, used as the normalisation of that map; the Legendre function uses the recurrence P_m^m = (−1)^m (2m − 1)!! sin^m θ (by the product), P_{m+1}^m = x (2m + 1) P_m^m (the recurrence at l = m + 1, as P_{m−1}^m = 0) and P_l^m = ((2l − 1) x P_{l−1}^m − (l + m − 1) P_{l−2}^m) / (l − m). There is no large cache, only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain and the 8 normalisation factors. At sampling time (per pixel): the cell (column, row) and the position in it are found, the signed distance to the map rectangle (negative inside) gives the frame and the fade; inside the map the position is turned into (φ, θ) and Y = P_l^|m|(cos θ)·(cos mφ or sin |m|φ) is computed, the tone being (0.5 + 0.5·Y / the largest value)·fade; ink = clamp(0.9·tone + 0.5·frame²), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (a recurrence of O(l) steps per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one start (the 6 starts chosen 5, 9, 6, 11, 4 and 5 times; seeds 8, 2, 0, 3, 4 and 9 for the starts 0, 4, 9, 16, 25 and 36); the C1 sweep covers the 6 starts with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 26.02%/26.00%/25.86%, color is 0.025524–0.026109 to 0.79659–0.79838 with a mean of 0.35903–0.36016, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.77686–0.78071 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 26.06%–26.18%, color is 0.025155–0.025398 to 0.79938–0.80157 with a mean of 0.36049–0.36162, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.78271–0.78776 relief; between seeds 0 and 3 31.34% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (71.26, 103.70, 67.86), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0125 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 starts). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('sphericalharmonics', { size: 512, seed: 2, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`wallpapergroups` adds wallpaper groups, bringing the current catalog from 1094 to 1095 kinds (1096 gallery choices including plain). The tile is divided into 2 × 2 unit cells and in each a small motif with **no symmetry of its own** (a 'hook' of two line segments and a dot) is repeated under a **plane symmetry group (a wallpaper group)**: the picture is the union of the images of the motif under every operation of the group (translations modulo the lattice, rotations, reflections and glide reflections); there are the 12 groups that a square lattice allows: p1, p2, pm, pg, cm, pmm, pmg, pgg, cmm, p4, p4m and p4g (with 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 4, 8, 4, 8 and 8 operations per unit cell in that order); the seed picks one group; golden lines and dots on a dark blue-black. As the motif itself is not symmetric, the symmetry group of the picture is exactly the chosen group and not a larger one; each unit cell holds as many motifs as the order of the group. The tile has a whole number of unit cells, so it is a periodic pattern. The 5 groups of a hexagonal lattice (p3, p3m1, p31m, p6 and p6m) are not included, because a square tile cannot join a hexagonal lattice. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real (for example actual wallpaper). (The way the operations of each group are written and their names are from my memory and I did not check the International Tables; the tests check with generators and group orders, as explained below.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the shape and position of the motif (the anchor (0.25, 0.395), which I found by a search that maximises the least distance between the images over the groups, giving 0.205), the line half width 0.02, the dot radius 0.034 (in unit-cell units), the 12 groups, the gold-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of all 12 groups once each (seeds 12, 9, 1, 11, 14, 13, 3, 15, 0, 10, 25 and 5, in the order of the groups above). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is implemented: (1) **generators and the orders of the groups**: composing the generators written in the test for each group (for example p4g from a quarter turn and the glide reflection (½ − x, ½ + y)) until nothing new appears gives 1, 2, 2, 2, 2, 4, 4, 4, 8, 4, 8 and 8 elements, and the same set as the operation list of the preset (so the list is closed under composition); (2) **exactly these symmetries**: for the 32 candidate operations (the 8 linear parts of the square × translations of 0 or ½) 3000 points are taken and the colour at each point is compared with that at its image; for an operation of the group the number of points where the colours differ by more than 0.1 is **exactly 0** (only the grain differs, by under 0.03) and for the other operations that fraction is above 0.005 (0.0100 at the least in the probe), so among these 32 candidates the symmetry of the picture is **exactly** the chosen group; (3) **the number of repeats**: the number of 4-connected components of the pixels of the 512 by 512 reading with a colour above 0.5 is exactly 2 × the order of the group × 4 unit cells (each image has two components, the hook and the dot; all 12 groups match in the probe: 8, 16, …, 64), and the lit fraction divided by the order is 0.0054 to 0.0056 (about 0.0055 in the probe). Mutation check (done once): with the last operation of each group's list dropped, 4 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (tones and ranges, exactly these symmetries, the number of repeats and the maps) while the operation list, seed difference and C1 ones still pass; it has been restored. **Limitations**: (a) the group for each seed was found with a probe (by the invariances) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 12 are covered; with 80 seeds the groups are chosen 4, 4, 12, 6, 9, 10, 6, 6, 5, 6, 5 and 7 times); (b) the tests only show that the picture's symmetry is exactly the group made by this set of operations, and I did not separately verify that this set is the crystallographic p4g, pmg and so on (the names rest on my memory); (c) only the 32 candidate operations are checked and not symmetries with other translation fractions, although the component count shows that each unit cell holds exactly as many images as the order of the group; (d) only the 12 groups of a square lattice, not all 17. **Record of adjustments (a mistake and discards)**: in the first version I wrote the operation list of p4g as (½ − x, y), (−y, ½ − x) and so on, to go with the quarter turn, and the probe showed that the picture of the corresponding seeds had only 4 symmetries (no rotation), because that list is not a group (not closed under composition); it matched after I changed it to the way the International Tables write it (all four images with a translation of (½, ½)), and this mistake is now guarded directly by the test that composes the generators; the first version's motif was small and sparse (a third of the tile per unit cell, the motif covering about 0.13 of the side) and the images of p4g crowded each other, so the tile is now 2 × 2 cells, the anchor was moved to the searched position and the lines were made thicker.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 71, seed ^ salt)` picks a group, which is a list of operations, each (a, b, c, d, tx, ty) taking (x, y) of the unit cell to (a·x + b·y + tx, c·x + d·y + ty) (the translation modulo 1); there is no large precomputation, only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): the position in the unit cell is (x, y) = (fract(2·fract(u)), fract(2·fract(v))); for each operation of the group the image (qx, qy) is found (its fractional part, so it stays inside the unit cell) and the kernels of the motif at that point are computed: for each of the two line segments `t = clamp(1 − d² / 0.02²)` from the squared distance to the segment, and for the dot `t = clamp(1 − r² / 0.034²)`, each combined over all operations as `1 − Π(1 − t²)`; ink = clamp(0.9·line + 1·dot), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. The motif stays at least 0.16 from the edge of the unit cell, so where taking the fractional part makes a jump the kernel is zero. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (at most 8 operations per pixel, each with 2 segments and a dot). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 79 every seed matches exactly one group (the groups chosen 4, 4, 12, 6, 9, 10, 6, 6, 5, 6, 5 and 7 times; seeds 12, 9, 1, 11, 14, 13, 3, 15, 0, 10, 25 and 5 for the 12 groups above); the C1 sweep covers all 12 seeds with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 4.514%/1.131%/1.132%, color is 0.025405–0.025678 to 0.86755–0.86867 with a mean of 0.049643–0.078511, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.86228–0.86528 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 1.09%–4.38%, color is 0.025136–0.025278 to 0.86775–0.86820 with a mean of 0.049550–0.078517, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.86553–0.86673 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 3.41% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (18.09, 21.56, 42.48), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0123 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 12 groups). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('wallpapergroups', { size: 512, seed: 25, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`mapattractors` adds planar map attractors, bringing the current catalog from 1093 to 1094 kinds (1095 gallery choices including plain). The middle of the tile shows the **density of the orbit** of a planar chaotic map: starting from (0.1, 0.1), 1000 steps are taken to settle and then the next 500 thousand points are spread bilinearly over a 384 by 384 grid of nodes, blurred once by [1 2 1] / 4 in each direction and turned into a tone by a logarithm (saturating at a quarter of the highest density), so that both the fine lines and the sparse clouds can be seen; rose pink on dark purple-black; the seed picks one of 6 variants [map, a, b, c, d, window centre x, window centre y, window half side]: the Clifford map x′ = sin(a y) + c·cos(a x), y′ = sin(b x) + d·cos(b y) with parameters (−1.4, 1.6, 1, 0.7), (1.5, −1.8, 1.6, 0.9) and (−1.8, −2, −0.5, −0.9); the de Jong map x′ = sin(a y) − cos(b x), y′ = sin(c x) − cos(d y) with parameters (−2, −2, −1.2, 2), (1.4, −2.3, 2.4, −2.1) and (−2.24, 0.43, −0.65, −2.43). The plot is in the middle of the tile with 0.04 left all round, so it is not a periodic pattern. Unlike `lorenzattractor` (one trajectory line of a continuous three-dimensional flow, drawn as a thin line) this is a discrete two-dimensional map and what is drawn is the density of the orbit in the plane and not a line; and it differs from `logisticbifurcation` (the bifurcation diagram of a one-dimensional map). It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The formulas and parameters of these maps are from my memory and from picking by eye; I did not check the literature; that the first set is the same as a common Clifford example on the web is my impression and I did not verify it, and the others I picked by looking at images from an exploration script.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin of the plot 0.04, the 384 nodes, the 500 thousand points, the 1000 settling steps, the logarithmic gain 60, the saturation 0.25, the 6 variants (windows included), the rose-pink-on-dark-purple-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of all 6 variants (the montage of seeds 0 to 5 showed variants 5, 5, 0, 2, 5 and 0, so variants 0, 2 and 5 were seen, and seeds 9, 6 and 13 were rendered separately for variants 1, 3 and 4), but **the previews were rendered with Bun (JavaScriptCore)**, and the sin and cos of Bun and Node (V8) differ, so the chaotic orbit differs and the density noise of the picture and the statistics below are not the same (I measured the lit fraction of seed 0 to be 3.86% with Bun and 3.68% with Node); the statistics and tests are from Node (vitest) and the pictures differ only in noise, the shape of the attractor being the same. **Limitation (across engines)**: the pixels of this material are not guaranteed to be bit-for-bit the same across JavaScript engines, because the precision of Math.sin and Math.cos is up to the engine and a chaotic orbit amplifies the difference; I did not verify whether Chrome (V8) and Node give the same result. The tests **read only the sampler output back**: (1) with an **independent orbit** (start (−0.7, 0.3), 2000 settling steps and 1.5 million points, against the sampler's (0.1, 0.1), 1000 steps and 500 thousand points) counted in 48 by 48 cells of the tile, the Pearson correlation between the square root of the count of each cell and the mean colour of that cell in a 192 by 192 reading is above 0.94 for the variant of the seed (0.957 to 0.969 in the probe) and below 0.55 for each other variant (0.469 at most in the probe); (2) in the cells with no point of the independent orbit in them or in the eight cells around them (682 to 1367 cells per variant) the mean colour is under 0.06 (0.0493 at most in the probe, the level of the background); (3) no pixel with a colour above 0.5 in the 256 by 256 reading (1129 to 7929 of them per variant) is more than 0.01 of the tile outside the box that the independent orbit reaches (0.0032 at most in the probe). Mutation check (done once): with the cos term of the Clifford map multiplied by 1.03, 4 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the density correlation, the dark cells, the extent box and the seed difference) while the tones, C1 and maps ones still pass; it has been restored (this check touched only the 3 Clifford variants). **Limitations**: (a) the variant for each seed was found with a probe (by the correlation) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 are covered); (b) the map formulas in the test are the same definition as in the design, so they only show that the sampler draws the density of this map; (c) the correlation only checks the rough density per cell (48 by 48) and not the exact position of the fine lines; (d) the sampler uses only 500 thousand points, so sparse regions are noisy (visible in the images too).

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 70, seed ^ salt)` picks a variant; from (0.1, 0.1) 1000 steps settle the orbit and then 500 thousand steps follow, each adding the position (turned into grid coordinates in the window [centre − half side, centre + half side]²) with bilinear weights to 4 nodes, points outside the window being skipped; the grid is then blurred once by [1 2 1] / 4 in both directions and the tone is min(1, log(1 + 60·density / (0.25·highest density)) / log(61)); the retained cache is a `Float32Array(384²)` of 589,824 B (the tones) and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain, and the temporary arrays of start-up (2 × `Float64Array(384²)`) are dropped after use. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into grid coordinates (the plot is the tile less 0.04 all round); outside the window the tone is 0, inside it the 4 nodes are interpolated **bilinearly with smoothstep weights** (so the picture is C1 across the nodes); ink = clamp(0.9·tone), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Timing (measured with Bun, not Node)**: building a sampler took about 125 to 195 ms (the first, 195 ms, including warm-up) and a 256 by 256 reading then about 3 to 7 ms; these are single measurements, not a benchmark. Measured (tool-run, vitest/Node): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one variant (the 6 variants chosen 6, 5, 9, 5, 4 and 11 times; seeds 2, 9, 3, 6, 13 and 0 for the variants 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 variants with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 3.682%/3.673%/12.07%, color is 0.025374–0.025701 to 0.79564–0.80066 with a mean of 0.084713–0.187225, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.77553–0.78524 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 3.69%–12.12%, color is 0.025137–0.025305 to 0.80060–0.80180 with a mean of 0.084671–0.187227, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.78512–0.78815 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 12.62% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (38.10, 15.47, 33.30), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0244 and the minimum z component is 253. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('mapattractors', { size: 512, seed: 2, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`htree` adds the H-tree, bringing the current catalog from 1092 to 1093 kinds (1094 gallery choices including plain). One H-tree fractal sits in the middle of the tile: an H (a horizontal bar of length L with an upright bar of length L at each end, filling the square of side L); the next generation is 4 H of size r·L, turned a quarter turn, centred on the 4 ends of the previous H (the corners of the square); n generations are drawn, and each of the 4 ends of the last generation gets a small round dot; the squares of all the generations reach 0.46 from the centre (so L = 0.92 / (1 + r + r² + …)); r = 0.5 is the classic H-tree (each bar being 1 / √2 of the one before, which I remember and have not checked against the literature). Fine ice-blue lines and dots on a dark blue-black; the seed picks one of 6 variants [generations n, ratio r, turned]: [5, 0.5, no], [5, 0.45, yes], [5, 0.4, no], [4, 0.5, yes], [4, 0.38, yes], [4, 0.44, no] ('turned' means the main bar of the first H is upright and not horizontal). There is one figure in the middle of the tile with a margin all round, so it is not a periodic pattern. Unlike `pythagorastree` (a Pythagoras tree of glazed square tiles) these are thin-line H shapes with no tile faces. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real (for example a clock tree of a chip).

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the extent 0.46, the line half width 0.004, the end dot radius 0.008, the 6 variants, the ice-blue-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of the final version for all 6 variants (seeds 0, 8, 6, 13, 1 and 4, variants 0 to 5 by the probe's table; the first montage of seeds 0 to 5 showed variants 0, 4 and 5 and seeds 8, 6 and 13 were rendered separately for variants 1, 2 and 3). The tests **read only the sampler output back**: (1) with an **explicit construction by generations** (not the sampler's recursion; each generation is expanded from the ends of the previous one with no pruning) every segment of the variant of the seed is listed (1023 for 5 generations, 255 for 4) and 7 points per segment (ends included) all have a colour above 0.5 (all of them in the probe), while for each other variant fewer than 45% of its points do (0.351 at most in the probe); (2) every pixel of the 512 by 512 reading with a colour above 0.5 is closer than 0.85 of the half width of the line to the nearest segment or closer than 0.85 of the radius of the dot to the nearest end dot (0.744 at worst in the probe; 16295 to 52138 such pixels per variant); (3) each end of the last generation (256 or 1024 of them) has a colour above 0.8 (0.845 at the lowest in the probe). Mutation check (done once): with the first child generation not turned, 5 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (tones and ranges, the segments, the distance of bright pixels, the seed difference and the maps) while the dot and C1 ones still pass; it has been restored. **Limitations**: (a) the variant for each seed was found with a probe (by the separately written segments) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 are covered, but the 6 variants are chosen 7, 2, 6, 3, 8 and 14 times in the table of 40 seeds, variant 1 by only 2 seeds); (b) the H-tree construction of the test is the same definition as the design (the turn, the ratio and the ends), so it only shows that the sampler agrees with this definition and not that it is the classic H-tree; (c) the density distribution is not checked, only the segments and the distances. **Record of mistakes and discards**: my first version shrank each **H** by 1 / √2 (taking the ratio of each bar for the ratio of each H), which made the squares of the generations overlap and the picture a dense grid, and it was discarded; the second version had ratios 0.44 to 0.58, 5 to 7 generations and a line half width of 0.0025, and 5 of its 6 previews were still too dense (above a ratio of 0.5 the subtrees interleave and an H of a deeper generation becomes as small as the line width), so the final version has ratios 0.38 to 0.5, 4 or 5 generations and a line half width of 0.004, with the images looked at again.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 69, seed ^ salt)` picks a variant [generations n, ratio r, turned]; the reach below each generation reach(g) = (1 + r + … + r^(n−g−1)) / 2 (in units of the side L of an H of that generation) is computed; the side of the first H is L = 0.92 / (1 + r + … + r^(n−1)); there is no large precomputation, only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): the H of each generation is visited recursively: it is skipped entirely when the pixel is too far from the bounding square of its subtree (the centre with L·reach plus the half width of the line); otherwise the 3 bars (the main bar and the 2 cross bars) each give the squared distance to the segment, the kernel `t = clamp(1 − d² / 0.004²)` is combined over all segments as `1 − t²` (so there is no crease from a minimum), and the 4 ends are visited: unless it is the last generation an H of size r·L, turned a quarter turn, is visited there, and on the last generation a dot kernel `clamp(1 − r² / 0.008²)` is added there; ink = clamp(0.9·line + 1·dot), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not formally measure the sampling time**; the statistics probe (four 512² and three 256² readings, including start-up of the program) took about 0.53 s in total, which is not a benchmark. Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one variant (the 6 variants chosen 7, 2, 6, 3, 8 and 14 times; seeds 0, 8, 6, 13, 1 and 4 for the variants 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 variants with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 19.88%/6.69%/8.97%, color is 0.025334–0.025665 to 0.87352–0.87415 with a mean of 0.091917–0.203379, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.87606–0.87774 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 6.22%–19.89%, color is 0.025131–0.025265 to 0.87394–0.87456 with a mean of 0.091580–0.203639, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.87717–0.87883 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 22.88% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (22.19% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (27.73, 32.10, 44.15), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0517 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the previews (all 6 variants of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('htree', { size: 512, seed: 0, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`cornuspirals` adds Cornu spirals, bringing the current catalog from 1091 to 1092 kinds (1093 gallery choices including plain). The tile is divided into n × n cells and each cell draws a Cornu spiral (the Euler spiral, the clothoid) (C(t), S(t)) = ∫₀ᵗ (cos(π s² / 2), sin(π s² / 2)) ds with t from −T to T: a curve of unit speed whose curvature π t is proportional to the arc length t, with an inflection point in the middle (marked by a bright dot at the centre of the cell) and a tightening little scroll at each end (tending to ±(0.5, 0.5)), making an overall S shape; fine amber lines and dots on a dark purple-black; the seed picks one of 6 variants [cells n, T, turn, mirror]: [2, 2.6, no, no], [3, 2.2, yes, no], [2, 2, no, yes], [4, 2.4, yes, yes], [3, 2.6, no, yes], [4, 1.9, no, no]; in a cell whose column + row is odd, the mirror flips the curve upside down and the turn then turns it a quarter turn (even cells are unchanged, as on a checkerboard). The tile has a whole number of cells, so it is a periodic pattern; the curve is drawn in the middle of the cell with a margin from the cell edges. Unlike the existing `harmonograph` (one large figure of two damped pendulums, loops winding in to nested spirals), this is a curve repeated in cells whose curvature grows linearly with arc length, with no damped motion; and it also differs from `conformalspiral` (a conformal spiral checkerboard) and `sacksspiral` (a dot lattice of integers). It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The Fresnel integrals, the curvature proportional to arc length and the ends tending to (0.5, 0.5) are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below check with another way of computing them, the power series.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the extent of the curve in the cell 0.44, the line half width 0.007 (in cell units), the radius of the dot at the centre 0.025, the 6 variants, the amber-on-dark-purple-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of the final version for all 6 variants (seeds 4, 0, 1, 2, 20 and 10, variants 0 to 5 by the probe's table; variants 0 to 3 were seen in the first montage and variants 4 and 5 were rendered separately). The tests **read only the sampler output back**: (1) with the **power series** of the Fresnel integrals (the Maclaurin series, not the sampler's Simpson table) the 3001 points per cell of the curve of the variant of the seed are computed (turned into tile positions by the 'mirror, turn' convention), and **all** of them have a colour above 0.5 (all of 12004 to 48016 points in the probe), while for each other variant at most 65% of its points do (0.546 at most in the probe); (2) away from the dot at the centre of the cell (0.045 of a cell), every pixel of the 512 by 512 reading with a colour above 0.5 is closer than 0.6 of the half width of the line to a point of the series curve (0.52 of it at worst in the probe; 3532 to 5143 pixels per variant); (3) each cell repeats the first under the turn and mirror: 2000 points per other cell are taken and whether the colour is above 0.5 agrees with that at the corresponding point of the first cell for at least 99.5% (0.9993 at worst in the probe, the differences coming from the grain pushing a colour across 0.5); (4) the colour at the centre of every cell is above 0.8 (0.845 at the lowest in the probe). The arc length of the series curve equals 2T in the probe (to 4 decimals), and C(3), S(3) come out as 0.605721 and 0.496313, matching the 0.6057 and 0.4963 I remember (from memory, not looked up in a table). Mutation check (done once): with the phase π t² / 2 multiplied by 1.05 (the curvature growing 5% faster), 2 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the curve points and the distance to the line) while the others still pass; it has been restored. **Limitations**: (a) the 'mirror, turn' convention (an odd cell is mirrored first and then turned, and the direction of the transformation of the curve points) is written the same way in the test and in the design, so (3) only checks that the cells agree with each other and does not independently prove the convention; (b) the variant for each seed was found with a probe (using the series curve) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 are covered; variant 4 is chosen by only 2 of 40 seeds); (c) the distance is not checked within 0.045 of a cell from the centre of each cell, where the dot is; (d) T is at most 2.6 so that neighbouring turns do not merge: I estimated this analytically (the radius of curvature about 1 / (π t)) and did not measure it, only checking by eye in the images that they do not merge. The distance is to **the curve itself** (3 Newton steps from the nearest point on the polyline), not to the polyline: I reasoned that the corners of a polyline would leave creases in the kernel (I did not try a polyline-only version), so the curve is used directly; the C1 sweep has 0 violations for all 6 variants.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 68, seed ^ salt)` picks a variant [cells n, T, turn, mirror]; a table is built: Simpson's rule with 4 sub-intervals on each of 160 segments accumulates (C, S) from t = 0 (t < 0 by odd symmetry), the table being two `Float64Array(161)`; a 40 × 40 grid is then built in which each cell records the segments that its bounding box (widened by the half width of the line) meets, so background pixels look at no segment. At sampling time (per pixel): the cell (column, row) and the position in it (−0.5 to 0.5) are found; in an odd cell the mirror (upside down) and the turn are applied in that order; the position is divided by the curve scale 0.44 / 0.8; the segments in the grid cell are looked at and the nearest point on the polyline and its parameter are taken; if within the half width of the line, 3 Newton steps follow from that parameter (solving (P(t) − x)·P′(t) = 0, with P(t) from the node of the table plus a 2-point Gauss integral, t being limited to −T to T so that the ends are round); the line kernel is `t = clamp(1 − distance² / half width²)` combined as `1 − t²`, the dot kernel at the centre of the cell is `clamp(1 − r² / 0.025²)`; ink = clamp(0.9·line + 1·dot²), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the retained cache is the curve table (2 × 161 doubles), the lists of the grid and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not formally measure the sampling time**; the statistics probe (four 512² and three 256² readings, including start-up of the program) took about 0.33 s in total, which is not a benchmark. Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one variant (the 6 variants chosen 5, 8, 7, 11, 2 and 7 times; seeds 4, 0, 1, 2, 20 and 10 for the variants 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 variants with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 1.714%/1.535%/1.724%, color is 0.025448–0.025659 to 0.86431–0.87255 with a mean of 0.053533–0.054867, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.85366–0.87347 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 1.57%–2.01%, color is 0.025199–0.025269 to 0.86688–0.87390 with a mean of 0.053487–0.057318, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.85834–0.87707 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 3.21% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (3.29% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (29.70, 17.12, 33.56), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0399 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the previews (all 6 variants of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('cornuspirals', { size: 512, seed: 4, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`catenaryfestoons` adds catenary festoons, bringing the current catalog from 1090 to 1091 kinds (1092 gallery choices including plain). The tile holds rows of hanging chains: in each row, chains drop between equally spaced pegs (small round dots) as catenaries y = a·(cosh(c) − cosh(s / a)) (s is the distance along the row from the middle of a span, c is the half span in units of a, a = span / (2c), the sag at the middle is a·(cosh(c) − 1) and zero at the pegs), fine teal lines and bright pegs on a dark blue-black; the seed picks one of 6 variants [spans, rows, c, staggered]: [4, 6, 1, yes], [6, 7, 1.6, no], [3, 4, 0.7, yes], [5, 6, 1.8, no], [8, 10, 1.3, yes], [4, 6, 1.5, no]; staggered means odd rows are shifted by half a span (the number of rows is then even, so the tile joins at the seams). The tile has a whole number of spans along u and a whole number of rows along v, so it is a periodic pattern. Unlike the existing `scallopedslate`, `fishscaletiles` and `fishscaleshingles` (overlapping shingle surfaces with semicircular lower edges), these are thin lines on a flat ground, the curves being catenaries and not semicircles, with no overlap and no shadows. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of any real chain. (The formula of the catenary with cosh is from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below check with another way of writing it and with a brute-force polyline.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the line half width 0.0045, the peg radius 0.026, the 6 variants, the teal-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of the final version for all 6 variants (seeds 3, 2, 1, 9, 0 and 5, variants 0 to 5 by the probe's table). The tests **read only the sampler output back**: (1) the peg positions of each variant (computed by separate code: row k at v = k / rows, the odd rows shifted for a staggered variant): **every** peg of the variant of the seed has a colour above 0.7 (1.000 in the probe), while for each other variant at most 60% of its pegs do (0.500 at most in the probe, as variants 0 and 5 share the pegs of the even rows); (2) at the middle of each span, at the height of the pegs, there is no chain (it hangs below), so the colour is below 0.1 (0.055 at most in the probe); (3) the **middle line of the chain is on the catenary**: in the columns at the middle of a span and at 0.15 and 0.3 of a span either side of it, for rows 1 to rows − 2, within 0.3 of a row pitch around the catenary the 512 by 512 reading has exactly one run of pixels with a colour above 0.5 and the middle of that run is within 0.75 of a pixel of the catenary (0.476 at worst in the probe; 30 to 320 columns per variant, none with a number of runs other than one); the catenary is written with a cosh made of exp and not the sampler's `Math.cosh` call; a parabola with the same depth at the middle would be off by 1.88, 3.32 and 2.29 pixels at worst for variants 1, 3 and 5, so for those the test can tell the two apart, while for variants 0, 2 and 4 (smaller c, off by 0.64, 0.29 and 0.73 pixels in the probe) it **cannot**; (4) the **brute-force polyline**: 0.03 or more from the pegs, every pixel of the 512 by 512 reading with a colour above 0.5 is within 0.0045 (the half width of the line) of some point of the polyline of all the catenaries (201 points per span; 0.00258 at worst in the probe, with 4254 to 9752 such pixels per variant), and every point of that polyline also 0.03 or more from the pegs has a colour above 0.5 (all of 3420 to 14300 points in the probe). Mutation check (done once): with the catenary replaced by a parabola of the same depth at the middle, 2 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the middle line of the chain and the brute-force polyline) while the others still pass; it has been restored. **Limitations**: (a) the variant for each seed was found with a probe (by separately written peg positions) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 are covered); (b) the chain is not checked within 0.03 of a peg; (c) the distance to the line is a first-order approximation (the vertical offset times the cosine of the slope angle), accurate only for pixels very near the curve and not the true distance to the curve. **Record of adjustments**: the first version had a peg radius of 0.018 and let the chain fade in between 0.009 and 0.018 from the peg, and the C1 sweep had violations at u = 0 (rows with a peg on the seam; 0, 43, 0, 93, 0 and 12 for seeds 3, 2, 1, 9, 0 and 5): I first suspected floating-point noise from the wrap of fract, but looking at the values from u = ±1e-10 to ±2e-3 showed a real cusp in the picture at u = 0 above the pegs (the slope of the height is about ±7.6×10⁻⁴ on the two sides, symmetric): the first-order distance still makes the chain kernel nonzero directly above a peg (the sign of the slope flips at the seam, giving a cusp of the |u| type); it is now a peg radius of 0.026 with the chain fading in only between 0.016 and 0.022 from the peg (the kernel reaches at most 0.0045·cosh(c) from the peg, at most about 0.014, so the cusp no longer shows), and the C1 sweep has 0 violations for all 6 variants. (The staggered variants had no violations in the first sweep; I guess the grid did not come near those pegs, **which I did not verify**.)

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 67, seed ^ salt)` picks a variant [spans n, rows m, c, staggered]; the span width is 1 / n, the row pitch is 1 / m and a = span / (2c). At sampling time (per pixel): for the 3 rows k nearest to the pixel (floor(v·m) − 1 to +1): odd rows are shifted by half a span when staggered; s = (fract((u − shift) / span) − 0.5)·span (a peg is at fract = 0, that is s = ±span/2); the vertical offset of the chain is v − k/m − a·(cosh(c) − cosh(s / a)), the slope is sinh(s / a), and the square of the distance to the chain is about offset² / (1 + slope²) (first order); the distance to the peg is hypot(span/2 − |s|, v − k/m); the chain kernel is t = clamp(1 − distance² / 0.0045²)·fade-in with fade-in = smooth(clamp((peg distance − 0.016) / 0.006)); the peg kernel is t = clamp(1 − peg distance² / 0.026²); each is combined as `1 − Π(1 − t²)`; ink = clamp(0.9·chain + 1·peg), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.35, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the only retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (a cosh, a sinh and a hypot for each of 3 rows per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one variant (the 6 variants chosen 11, 7, 6, 3, 8 and 5 times); the C1 sweep covers all 6 variants (seeds 3, 2, 1, 9, 0, 5) with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 9.46%/2.49%/2.50%, color is 0.025449–0.025566 to 0.85463–0.86388 with a mean of 0.06210–0.12842, roughness is always 0.35, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8410–0.8624 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 2.48%–9.45%, color is 0.025116–0.025256 to 0.86544–0.87100 with a mean of 0.06223–0.12839, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8603–0.8733 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 11.36% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (11.38% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (14.54, 30.42, 33.40), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0297 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the previews (all 6 variants of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('catenaryfestoons', { size: 512, seed: 3, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`logisticbifurcation` adds the bifurcation diagram of the logistic map, bringing the current catalog from 1089 to 1090 kinds (1091 gallery choices including plain). The bifurcation diagram of the logistic map x → r·x·(1 − x): the horizontal axis is the parameter r, and for each column the orbit of x = 0.5 is iterated 300 times to settle and then the next 120 values are drawn, the vertical axis being x (larger x is up); so for small r there is one curve, the stable fixed point x = 1 − 1 / r, at r = 3 it splits into the 2-cycle (x = ((r + 1) ± √((r − 3)(r + 1))) / 2r), then successive period-doublings (4, 8, 16, …) lead into the chaotic bands, interrupted by stable windows of periodic orbits (the most visible being the period-3 window at r about 3.83); the whole orbit lies between f(f(1/2)) = r²(4 − r) / 16 and f(1/2) = r / 4, which are the upper and lower edges of the chaotic bands; fine cream dots on dark brown-black with a rectangular frame around; the seed picks one of 6 ranges (r start, r end, x low, x high): (2.4, 4, 0, 1) (the whole diagram), (3.4, 4, 0, 1), (3.7, 3.9, 0.05, 1), (3.5, 3.6, 0.3, 0.92), (2.9, 3.6, 0.3, 0.95) and (3.82, 3.87, 0.3, 0.96) (the period-3 window enlarged). The plot is in the middle of the tile with 0.07 left all round; it is not a periodic pattern (the edges of the tile do not join). Unlike the other kinds that draw trajectories of dynamical systems (the path of `lorenzattractor`, the damped pendulums of `harmonograph`), this is a bifurcation diagram of a parameter sweep. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The fixed point, the 2-cycle, the bounds on the orbit and the order of the bifurcations of the logistic map are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below check with an independent iteration and with closed forms.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin of the plot 0.07, the transient of 300 iterations, 120 plotted points, the dot half width 0.0025 (in tile units), the frame half width 0.004, the fade 0.01, the 2048 column steps, the 6 ranges, the cream-on-dark-brown colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of the final version for seeds 1, 8, 7, 13, 2 and 0 (sets 0 to 5 by the probe's table), so all 6 ranges have been seen. The tests **read only the sampler output back**: (1) with an **independent iteration** (written as r·x − r·x² and not as the sampler's r·x·(1 − x), with the preset's 300 steps of transient, requiring the point set after them to equal that after 20000 steps, the Lyapunov exponent to be below −0.05 and at most 40 points, so that only columns whose orbit has really settled are taken) the points of the stable cycles of each range are found, and those of the range of each seed (487, 438, 216, 1136, 743 and 196 for the ranges, at least 0.015 inside the edge of the plot) all have a colour above 0.5 (1.000 in the probe), while for each other range fewer than 30% of its points do (at most 0.131 in the probe, 0.226 with the columns the test lists); (2) in such columns (with all the points at least 8 rows from the edge of the counting window and the points either within 1.5 rows of each other or more than 6 apart) the number of runs of bright pixels equals the number of groups of points (5 to 49 columns per range in the probe, 0 mismatches), that is, there are no extra bright dots; (3) the **bounds** (closed forms): no pixel inside the plot (0.02 off the edge) with a colour above 0.6 has an x above r / 4 or below r²(4 − r) / 16 by more than 1% of the range of x (0.0023 at worst in the probe, with 1.9 to 35 thousand bright pixels per range); (4) the **closed forms of the fixed point and the 2-cycle**: for r from 2.45 to 2.95 the only stable point is x = 1 − 1 / r and for r from 3.12 to 3.38 they are ((r + 1) ± √((r − 3)(r + 1))) / (2r) (covered by ranges 0 and 4), and such a column has exactly one bright run (two for the 2-cycle) whose middle is within 1.5 rows of the closed form. Mutation check (done once): with the map multiplied by 0.99, 6 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (ranges and tones, stable cycle points, run counts, bounds, closed forms and the difference between ranges) while the C1 and maps ones still pass; it has been restored. **Limitations**: (a) only **stable** columns and the bounds are checked, **the chaotic bands are checked only by the bounds (the upper and lower edges), not by the density distribution in them or the positions of the bifurcation points** (a chaotic orbit is sensitive to the last bit, so there is no point-by-point comparison); (b) the number of column steps 2048 and the transient of the preset are shared by both sides; (c) the range for each seed (seeds 1, 8, 7, 13, 2, 0 for the ranges 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 are covered). **On continuity (important)**: in the chaotic bands the orbit is extremely sensitive to r (when I first took r for the column of each pixel directly, the C1 sweep had thousands of violations with second differences as large as about 1.5×10¹⁰, because a change of 1e-10 in r makes all the points of the column different), so **r is taken at the middle of one of 2048 column steps, the picture is constant along u within a column step and jumps at the boundaries of the steps (2047 of them), the jumps being large in the chaotic bands**; the C1 sweep therefore avoids the boundaries of the steps (including u = 0.5, which is exactly the boundary of steps 1023 and 1024), and after the repeated points of a cycle are removed the jump of the second derivative at the edge of the kernel is not amplified by identical points; **continuity along u is not claimed**. The maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0444, unlike the 0.0543 and others of earlier kinds, which I did not look into further. The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid; as the chaotic bands vary a lot with how the grid meets them, the ranges of the lit area and the mean are wide.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 66, seed ^ salt)` picks a range (r start, r end, x low, x high); the plot is in the middle of the tile with 0.07 left all round, its width being span = 0.86. At sampling time (per pixel): the signed distance to the rectangle of the plot gives the frame (half width 0.004, tone 0.45) and the fade `smooth(clamp(−distance / 0.01))`; inside the plot u is turned into the position c ∈ [0, 1] along the columns, the column step is k = floor(c·2048) and r = r start + ((k + 0.5) / 2048)·(r end − r start); for that step (computed when first needed and remembered) the orbit of x = 0.5 under x → r·x·(1 − x) is iterated 300 times and the next 120 values are taken, those within 1e-9 of an earlier one being kept once (a point on a cycle is drawn once); v is turned into the value of x = x high − (row position)·(x high − x low); for each point the vertical (x direction) distance to it (in tile units) gives `t = clamp(1 − (distance / 0.0025)²)` and the coverage of the dots is `1 − Π(1 − t²)`; ink is `clamp(0.9·fade·coverage + 0.45·frame²)`; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the retained cache is the points of each column step (at most 2048 steps, each with at most 120 doubles, about 2 MB, built only for the steps that are used) and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (one iteration per column step, and up to 120 kernels per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one range (the 6 ranges chosen 9, 7, 7, 6, 6 and 5 times); the C1 sweep covers all 6 ranges (seeds 1, 8, 7, 13, 2, 0) with 0 violations (avoiding the boundaries of the column steps; see above); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 4.80%–16.37%, color is 0.02565–0.02570 to 0.80107–0.80178 with a mean of 0.08480–0.17591, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.7866–0.7881 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 4.70%–16.25%, color is 0.02515–0.02525 to 0.80179–0.80274 with a mean of 0.08348–0.17474, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.7881–0.7907 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 10.1% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (9.95% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (56.1, 49.3, 33.0), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0444 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('logisticbifurcation', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`zordercurve` adds the Z-order (Morton) curve, bringing the current catalog from 1088 to 1089 kinds (1090 gallery choices including plain). The 2^b × 2^b cells of a grid (4×4, 8×8, 16×16) are put in a row in the Z order (Morton order): the index of the cell (column, row) is the number made by interleaving the bits of the row and the column (at each level the bit of the row and then that of the column; the other way round for the transposed N order); cells with consecutive indices are joined by a straight segment between their centres, so the curve repeats a "Z" at every scale and has big jumps (it is not a continuous space-filling curve, unlike the Hilbert curve); the nodes (the cell centres) are small dots whose tone rises along the curve from dark (0.3) to bright (0.95), the lines having a fixed tone 0.7; magenta on dark purple; the seed picks one of 6 pairs (b, transposed): (2, Z), (3, Z), (4, Z), (2, N), (3, N) and (4, N); the whole curve fills the tile and no line crosses the seam (half a cell is left at each end). Unlike `hilbertcurve`, `peanocurve` and `moorecurve` (continuous space-filling curves, the Hilbert one closing across the tile seam and the Peano one shifted around the torus by the seed), the Z-order curve has big jumps between neighbouring cells and keeps the structure of the interleaved bits. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on the Morton order and the interleaving of bits are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below build the order independently from binary strings.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the line half width 0.08 cell, the node radius 0.2 cell, the line tone 0.7, the node tones 0.3 to 0.95, the 6 pairs (b, transposed), the magenta-on-dark-purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5 (the lines are a little blurred after the scaling of the preview), which by the probe's table cover sets 1, 4, 0 and 5; **set 2 (16×16 Z order) and set 3 (4×4 N order) have not been seen**. The tests **read only the sampler output back**: (1) the **Morton order is built from binary strings** (not with the shifts of the sampler): the index of a cell is read from the string that puts, from the most significant bit down, the bit of the row and then that of the column at each level (or the other way round for the transposed order), the cells are sorted by index to give the nodes, and on the segment between each pair of consecutive nodes the check points at 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7 (off the node discs and on the lines; 45, 189 and 765 for the sets) are taken; at most 2 of the check points of the variant of each seed may read lower than 0.5, and each of the other 5 sets has at least 10 check points reading lower (at least 18 in the probe); (2) at the points of a low-discrepancy sequence that are more than 0.3 cell from every segment and more than 0.35 cell from every node (brute-force distances; about 4 to 6 thousand per seed in the probe, and the test takes 8,000 points and requires more than 1,500 of them to qualify) the colour is below 0.1 (0.055 at most in the probe); (3) the colour at the centre of node number i of n equals 0.14 + 0.72 × (nodeLow + (nodeHigh − nodeLow)·i / (n − 1)) to within 0.03 (0.0172 at most in the probe, the grain being ±0.015), so it rises from dark to light along the curve. Mutation check (done once): with the interleaving of the bits replaced by a row-major order, all the dedicated tests except the C1 one fail; it has been restored. **Limitations**: nodeLow, nodeHigh and the line width of the preset are shared by both sides; (1) checks only the middles of the segments, not the ends near the nodes or the shape of the node discs, and (2) checks only the dark places, **not the line width**; the variant for each seed (seeds 5, 0, 9, 7, 2, 4 for the sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered); seeds 0 and 1 give the same variant, so the seed-difference test uses seeds 0 and 2. **On C1**: the distance of the lines is the minimum over the segments, so where two segments meet at a node, outside the node disc and near the bisector of the angle between them, the minimum has a crease that may lie inside the line band (the line half width is 0.08 and the node disc radius 0.2; for an angle of 45 degrees the point on the bisector at 0.08 from both segments is about 0.21 cell from the node, just outside the node disc); the C1 sweep (random samples) did not meet a violation, but **I did not look at those places, so C1 near the nodes is not claimed**. The maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0020, far below other kinds (thin lines and little difference in tone; I did not look into it). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid; the extreme brightness and the highest height vary with how the grid meets the lines, so the ranges are wider.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 65, seed ^ salt)` picks a pair (b, transposed), the side being s = 2^b and the number of nodes n = s²; the index of each cell (column, row) is found: over the b bit levels the k-th bit of the column (of the row when transposed) is put at bit 2k of the index and the k-th bit of the row (of the column when transposed) at bit 2k + 1; the centre of the cell with that index is stored as the node. At sampling time (per pixel) the tile coordinates are multiplied by s, the distance of the point to each of the n − 1 segments between consecutive nodes is found (the projection parameter clamped to 0 to 1) and the least is taken, and the node disc of the cell the point is in is found; the coverage of the lines is `t = clamp(1 − distance² / 0.08²)`, that of the node is `clamp(1 − (distance to the cell centre)² / 0.2²)`, and ink is `0.7·t²·(1 − node²) + node tone·node²` (node tone = 0.3 + 0.65·index / (n − 1)); color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the retained cache is the table of nodes (at most 256 × 2 doubles) and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (every pixel scans all the segments, 255 for 16×16, with no spatial index, and I did not measure the cost of this on a large map). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one variant (the 6 sets chosen 7, 9, 4, 7, 7 and 6 times); the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 5, 0, 9, 7, 2, 4) with 0 violations (at the first try); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 9.935%–9.967%, color is 0.02540–0.02592 to 0.8152–0.8300 with a mean of 0.13039–0.13055, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.7976–0.8191 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 8.30%–9.38%, color is 0.02509–0.02526 to 0.8194–0.8363 with a mean of 0.11993–0.13031, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8062–0.8299 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 (8×8 Z order and 16×16 N order) 12.7% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (seeds 0 and 1 are the same variant and differ by only 0.10%, from the grain); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (57.0, 26.2, 52.2), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0020 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('zordercurve', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`polygonoffsets` adds the offset curves of a polygon, bringing the current catalog from 1087 to 1088 kinds (1089 gallery choices including plain). A polygon stands in the middle of the disc (6 of them: a five-pointed star, a six-pointed star, an L, a triangle, a cross and an arrow), and a line is drawn at every fixed step (0.045 disc radii) of the signed distance to the polygon (negative inside, positive outside), that is the offset curves of the polygon: outside, the corners of the curves are circular arcs (the equidistant lines from the corners), and inside they are sharp corners (the folds on the medial axis); the bands between the lines are coloured with four tones by inside or outside and the parity of the band number (0.08 and 0.2 outside, 0.32 and 0.48 inside), as thin green lines on dark green; the disc radius is 0.46 of the tile (diameter 0.92), the outside fades out between 0.94 and 0.96 with a ring added, and all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam; the seed picks one of the 6 polygons. Unlike `topographicmap` (contours of a sinusoidal terrain, every fifth line heavy) and `kaleidoscope` (iso-bands of an averaged noise), the distance field here is the geometric distance to a polygon and the lines are exact offset curves. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on offset curves, signed distance and the medial axis are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below compute the distance by brute force and check independently.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the step 0.045, the line half width 0.009, the ring half width 0.004, the fade range 0.94 to 0.96, the vertices of the 6 polygons (the five-pointed star with the outer radius 0.55 and the inner radius 0.23, the six-pointed star with 0.55 and 0.30, the L, the triangle, the cross and the arrow), the four band tones, the green-on-dark-green colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5, which by the table cover all 6 polygons. The tests **read only the sampler output back** and compute the distance **by brute force and not with the formula of the sampler**: the least distance to 401 points taken along each side of the polygon, and the inside by the winding number (the sum of the angles the sides subtend at the point, 2π inside and 0 outside); (1) a **forward construction**: from the middle of each side, along its normal, the signed distances ±(k + f) steps (k = 1 to 30, f = 0 on a line and f = 0.5 in the middle of a band) are walked, keeping only the points whose brute-force distance equals the distance walked to within 0.001 (that is, where that side is the nearest part) and that are within 0.85 of the middle; all the check points on the lines of the polygon of each seed (70, 72, 61, 54, 88 and 72 for the shapes) read bright with at most 2 lower than 0.7, each of the other 5 shapes has at least 20 check points reading lower (at least 43 in the probe), and the check points in the middle of a band all read below 0.6 (at most 0.5 in the probe); (2) the **offset property**: for every pixel of the 256 by 256 reading within 0.85 of the middle with a colour above 0.78, the brute-force signed distance is within 0.006 of a whole multiple of the step (0.0032 at worst in the probe, with 3,064 to 3,479 pixels per seed); (3) the colours in the middle of a band: outside even below 0.18 (0.098 to 0.125 in the probe), outside odd from 0.19 to 0.30 (0.231 to 0.259), inside even from 0.30 to 0.42 (0.356 to 0.380; the star shapes have none, their inside bands being too narrow to have a band midpoint where a side is the nearest part) and inside odd from 0.43 to 0.56 (0.472 to 0.498). Mutation check (done once): with the position of the lines multiplied by a factor 1.02, these two tests and the range test fail; it has been restored. **Limitations**: the vertex data of the polygons come from the preset, shared by both sides; the band midpoints cover only the places where a side is the nearest part, so the arc regions near the corners and the bands near the medial axis are covered only by the property (2) of the bright line pixels; the polygon for each seed (seeds 0, 1, 5, 2, 4, 3 for the shapes 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 are covered). **Important limitation on C1**: the offset curves have **folds on the medial axis inside and on the cut locus outside (for the concave shapes), which are not C1**; in the first C1 sweep, with random and grid samples, some grid points fell exactly on the axes of symmetry (u = 0.5 and so on), giving 348 and 622 violations with second differences up to about 563, which I judge to be real folds on the medial axis (they lie on the axes of symmetry) — **I did not check the other violation records (one per point, axis and channel) one by one**; the later sweep, with the grid made of odd divisions (13, 129, 509) and y values off the axes of symmetry, has 0 violations for all 6 polygons, so the test covers only points that avoid the medial axis and the cut locus and **does not claim that the whole picture is C1**. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning; the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0543, the same as for several earlier kinds. The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 64, seed ^ salt)` picks a polygon (its vertices being preset data). At sampling time (per pixel) the disc coordinates `(u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46` are taken and for each side the distance of the point to the segment (the projection parameter clamped to 0 to 1) is found; the least is the distance, the parity of the number of ray crossings gives inside or outside, and that gives the signed distance s (negative inside); the distance to the nearest line is |s − step·round(s / step)|, `t = clamp(1 − (distance / 0.009)²)` and the coverage of the lines is t²; the band number is floor(|s| / step), and the fill by inside or outside and the parity of the band number is 0.08 or 0.2 outside and 0.32 or 0.48 inside; the content of the disc is multiplied by the fade outside `smooth(clamp((0.94 − r) / 0.02))` and a thin ring (radius 1) is added: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`, ink = `fill·(1 − line) + line`), height is `0.8·(lines + ring)·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the only retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (one projection for each of at most 12 sides per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one polygon (the 6 polygons chosen 7, 7, 9, 7, 7 and 3 times); the C1 sweep (with the grid avoiding the axes of symmetry) covers all 6 polygons with 0 violations (the first sweep, which included grid points on the axes of symmetry, had violations, see above); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 14.83%–15.01%, color is 0.02563–0.02586 to 0.87257–0.87422 with a mean of 0.22502–0.22988, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8735–0.8779 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 14.72%–14.98%, color is 0.02519–0.02535 to 0.87394–0.87450 with a mean of 0.22486–0.22971, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8773–0.8788 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 20.8% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (20.9% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (53.3, 78.2, 41.2), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0543 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('polygonoffsets', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`powerdiagram` adds the power diagram (Laguerre–Voronoi diagram), bringing the current catalog from 1086 to 1087 kinds (1088 gallery choices including plain). The tile is divided into c × c cells (c = 5, 6, 7) with one disc in each (its centre jittered inside the cell and its radius 0.19 ± 0.09·spread cell widths, the discs not touching each other), and the whole tile is divided into polygonal cells by the power: the power of a point p about a circle (c, r) is |p − c|² − r², each point belongs to the circle of least power, the edges between cells lie on the radical axes (the lines of equal power) of two circles and so are straight; with equal radii it is the ordinary Voronoi diagram and with different radii the edges move towards the smaller circle; thin coral lines (the cell edges and the outlines of the discs) on dark wine, the inside of a disc in two tones (0.5 and 0.65, chosen at random by the hash) and the rest of the cell dark (0.12); the seed picks one of 6 pairs (c, spread): (5, 0), (6, 0.5), (7, 1), (5, 1), (6, 1) and (7, 0.5); the figure is periodic with the tile, the discs are all inside their own cells, and the edges of the cells may cross the seam. Unlike `voronoicells` (one jittered site per cell, split into colour plates by the nearest site, with soft weights to keep C1), the cells here are decided by the power of discs with radii, the edges are radical axes and the discs themselves are drawn. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on the power, radical axes and the power diagram are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below read the picture back only, find the discs in it and then check the edges independently.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the line half width 0.035 cell, the disc radii 0.19 ± 0.09·spread cells, the range of the centres (0.35 to 0.65 of the cell width), the 6 pairs (c, spread), the three fills (0.12, 0.5, 0.65), the coral-on-wine colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. **The first preview looked too much like an ordinary Voronoi diagram** (radii 0.2 ± 0.06·spread, centres from 0.3 to 0.7, a variant with c = 8) and the edges moved too little from the midlines; after seeing it I changed to the present radii and range of centres and replaced the variants with c = 8 by c = 5 and 7; I looked at the final preview for seeds 0 to 5, which by the table found from the picture cover sets 0, 3, 1, 4 and 5; **set 2 ((7, 1)) has not been seen**. The tests **read only the sampler output back**, find the discs in the picture and then check the edges independently: (1) the 4-connected regions of at least 60 pixels in the 512 by 512 reading with a colour from 0.42 to 0.70 and a roundness (2πI / area²) within 0.03 of 1 are taken as discs (the bands of the lines are not round and are excluded), the radius of the outline of a disc being the colour-weighted mean distance from the centroid of the bright pixels (colour above 0.7) within 7 pixels outside its region; the number of discs is c², each has a roundness within 0.01 of 1 (0.002 at worst in the probe), the centres are at 0.35 to 0.65 of the width of the cell (within 1.5 pixels), and the difference between the largest and the smallest radius over 2 × 0.09 × the cell width equals the spread of the variant to within 0.1 (0.03, 0.49 and 0.94 for the spreads 0, 0.5 and 1 in the probe); (2) the **radical axis property**: for every bright line pixel (colour above 0.78, more than 5 pixels from every outline), using the centres and outline radii found in the picture (plus copies in the eight neighbouring tiles), the two circles of least power are found and the distance of the point from the line of equal power of the two, (power_b − power_a) / (2|c_a − c_b|), has a median below 0.6 pixel, a 99th percentile below 1.1 pixels and a maximum below 1.8 pixels (0.30 to 0.46, 0.69 to 0.95 and 0.81 to 1.40 in the probe; a pixel is 1), and in the variants whose radii differ (all but the first) the same distance with the radii ignored (the ordinary Voronoi bisector) has a 99th percentile above 1.3 (1.5 to 3.8 in the probe), so the edges are those of the power diagram and not of the Voronoi diagram. Mutation check (done once): changing the power to the plain squared distance makes both tests, the range test, the seed-difference test and the maps test fail; it has been restored. **Limitations**: (a) the positions and outline radii of the discs are estimated from the picture, so the residuals include pixel quantisation (the tolerances are in pixels); (b) only the bright line pixels are checked, not the line width or the tones (the distribution of the two tones of the discs is not checked); (c) the discs not touching is guaranteed by the design, so the tests do not cover a power diagram of intersecting discs; (d) the cell width and the range of the jitter come from the preset data, shared by both sides; (e) near the vertices of the cells the lines take the minimum of the distances to the nearest radical axes, so **there is a short stretch (within the line half width) inside a cell near each vertex where the distance function has a crease and is not C1**; the C1 sweep (random samples) did not meet it, so C1 near the vertices cannot be claimed. The variant for each seed (seeds 0, 2, 15, 1, 3, 5 for the sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, but each variant is also checked against the number of discs and the range of the radii read from the picture. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning; the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0260, unlike the 0.0543, 0.0378, 0.0197 and 0.0075 of earlier kinds, which I did not look into further. The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid; as every pixel belongs to some cell there is no ground colour, and color is at least about 0.139 and AO at least about 0.709 (unlike 0.0255 and 0.6 for other kinds).

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 63, seed ^ salt)` picks a pair (c, spread); for the (c + 4) × (c + 4) cells covering the tile and two cells beyond on each side the centre of a cell is (column + 0.35 + 0.3·h₁, row + 0.35 + 0.3·h₂) (h being hashes of the wrapped cell numbers), the radius is 0.19 + spread·0.09·(2h₃ − 1) and the tone choice is h₄ < 0.5; they are stored in a `Float64Array`. At sampling time (per pixel) the tile coordinates are multiplied by c and made periodic, and among the 5 × 5 sites about the cell the power |p − c|² − r² of each is found, the one of least power giving the circle the point belongs to; the distance to a cell edge is the least over the other sites of (power_j − power_i) / (2|c_j − c_i|) (for a convex cell this is the distance to its boundary); the distance to the outline of the disc is `| |p − c| − r |`; each gives `t = clamp(1 − (distance / 0.035)²)` and the coverage of the lines is `1 − (1 − t₁²)(1 − t₂²)`; the fill is 0.5 or 0.65 inside a disc (power below 0) and 0.12 elsewhere; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`, ink = `fill·(1 − line) + line`), height is `0.8·line·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark (0.709 at the least in this kind, whose whole tile is filled) and metallic is 0; the retained cache is the table of sites ((c + 4)² × 4 doubles, about 3.9 KB for c = 7) and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (25 sites scanned twice per pixel). Measured (tool-run): the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 0, 2, 15, 1, 3, 5) with 0 violations (at the first try, but see the limitation about the creases at the vertices above); in the analysis of seeds 0 to 39 from the picture every seed finds exactly one matching (c, spread), the 6 sets being chosen 5, 10, 6, 5, 8 and 6 times (none unmatched); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 19.70%–20.53%, color is 0.13894–0.13929 to 0.87277–0.87311 with a mean of 0.27557–0.28191, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.709 and height is at most 0.8740–0.8755 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 19.52%–20.53%, color is 0.13873–0.13879 to 0.87416–0.87429 with a mean of 0.27456–0.28192, AO is at least 0.709 and height is at most 0.8778–0.8784 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 27.5% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (27.6% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (91.8, 48.4, 47.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0260 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('powerdiagram', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`reuleauxfield` adds the Reuleaux polygon field, bringing the current catalog from 1085 to 1086 kinds (1087 gallery choices including plain). The tile is divided into c × c square cells (c = 3, 4 or 5), and in the middle of each cell stands a Reuleaux polygon — a curve of constant width: for an odd number n of corners (3, 5, 7) a regular n-gon, a circle drawn about each corner with the distance between opposite corners as the radius, and the intersection of those n discs; its width is the same in every direction (Barbier's theorem; the Reuleaux triangle is the best known example), and the larger n is the closer it is to a circle; the width of every polygon is 0.8 of the cell, each is turned by a random angle in [0, 2π / n), so every shape is inside its own cell and does not cross the seam; thin teal lines on dark teal-black, the inside of a polygon filled with two alternating tones (0.3 and 0.5) by the parity of the sum of the cell's column and row; the seed picks one of 6 pairs (n, c): (3, 4), (3, 5), (5, 4), (5, 3), (7, 3) and (7, 4). Unlike the other materials that arrange shapes in cells, what is drawn here is a curve of constant width, the positions of the corners and arcs being fixed by n. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on Reuleaux polygons and Barbier's theorem and the area formula are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below read the picture back only and check it with geometric properties that do not use the construction.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the line half width 0.035 cell, the shape width 0.8 cell, the 6 pairs (n, c), the two fills (0.3 and 0.5), the teal-on-dark-teal colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5 (each preview crops only the top-left 512 pixels of one tile), which by the table cover sets 3, 2, 4 and 0; **set 1 ((3, 5)) and set 5 ((7, 4)) have not been seen**.
