At start-up (per sampler) the Grundy values are stored in an `Int32Array(4096)`; for `y = 0…63` and `x = 0…63` in turn the values of the reachable positions `G(x − k, y)` (`k = 1…x`), `G(x, y − k)` (`k = 1…y`) and `G(x − k, y − k)` (`k = 1…min(x, y)`) are collected and the smallest whole number that does not occur is taken; the tone is `0.7·min(G, 7) / 7`, stored in a `Float64Array(4096)`; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 28, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 28, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 64): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is an `Int32Array(4096)` of 16,384 B, a `Float64Array(4096)` of 32,768 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 180,224 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction (4,096 cells, each with at most 189 reachable positions) or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): the largest value of `G` is 95; there are 49 cells with `G = 0`, and all 4,096 cells agree with the `⌊k·φ⌋` formula; the numbers of cells with the values 0 to 6 are 49/51/49/49/49/49/47 and 3,753 have 7 or more; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a unique fitting shift, (14, 42), (30, 26), (29, 14) and (40, 45), with maximum fit errors of 0.014990–0.014999; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is always 71.37%, color is 0.06113–0.06133 to 0.85423–0.85451 with a mean of 0.67902–0.67912, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.7344 and height is at most 0.8485–0.8496 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is always 65.05%, color is 0.02512–0.02523 to 0.85459–0.85488 with a mean of 0.58354–0.58367, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8501–0.8509 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 15.5% of the cell centres differ in colour by more than 0.05 (6.6% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (97.5, 144.2, 163.8), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0399 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles, the `min(G, 7)` version): ice-blue rounded squares everywhere, with the dark small-value cells in two lines opening outwards and a small cluster. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('wythoffnim', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`golombruns` adds Golomb runs, bringing the current catalog from 1049 to 1050 kinds (1051 gallery choices including plain). A 64×64 table of rounded square tiles in which row `i` and column `j` hold term `64i + j + 1`, `a(n)`, of Golomb's sequence (`a(1) = 1` and `a(n) = 1 + a(n − a(a(n − 1)))`, the only non-decreasing sequence in which every `n` occurs exactly `a(n)` times: 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 6, …); the tone is the remainder of `a(n)` on division by 7 (0 to 6), so every run of equal terms is a plateau of one tone and the plateaus grow longer (`a(n)` is about `1.2·n^0.618`); a tweed-like pattern with horizontal bands, deep teal to sand gold; the seed moves the whole table around the torus. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 64×64 size, the tone mapping by the remainder on division by 7, the deep teal and sand gold tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The sampler builds the sequence with the recurrence; the tests rebuild the whole table in **another, independent way** — directly from the definition 'the value `k` is repeated `a(k)` times', building the sequence from itself (starting from 1, 2, 2) — and I first confirmed with a probe that the two constructions are identical on all 4,096 terms; the tests check the first 15 terms, the largest term 205 up to 4,096, that the remainders 0 to 6 occur 590, 595, 597, 574, 577, 579 and 584 times, and compare the colour at every cell centre against all 4096 possible shifts, which gives **exactly one** fitting shift for every seed (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03). This shows that the sampler's sequence table agrees with the independent construction; it does **not** prove that the defining property holds for all terms, nor that `a(n) ≈ 1.2·n^0.618` (that is standard theory, not verified here). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0377). The lit-area share, the lowest colour and the AO differ between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the cell width (4 and 8 pixels) and the position of the sample points inside the cells differ; the tests use the 256² values.

At start-up (per sampler) an `Int32Array(4097)` holds `a(1) = 1` and `a(n) = 1 + a(n − a(a(n − 1)))` (`n = 2…4096`), and the tone is `0.7·(a(n) mod 7) / 6`, stored in a `Float64Array(4096)`; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 27, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 27, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 64): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is an `Int32Array(4097)` of 16,388 B, a `Float64Array(4096)` of 32,768 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 180,228 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): the two constructions are identical on all 4,096 terms; the largest term is 205; the remainders 0 to 6 occur 590/595/597/574/577/579/584 times; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a unique fitting shift, (24, 38), (7, 41), (39, 62) and (50, 30), with maximum fit errors of 0.014984–0.014999; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 32.36%–32.43%, color is 0.05918–0.06055 to 0.85413–0.85448 with a mean of 0.41360–0.41367, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.7344 and height is at most 0.8462–0.8490 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 26.08%–26.13%, color is 0.02508–0.02539 to 0.85437–0.85475 with a mean of 0.35778–0.35786, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8495–0.8505 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 81.3% of the cell centres differ in colour by more than 0.05 (24.6% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (91.0, 90.6, 68.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0377 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles): small rounded squares in deep teal and sand gold in horizontal bands, each band a plateau of one tone of varying length, like tweed. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('golombruns', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`diamondsquare` adds Diamond-square, bringing the current catalog from 1048 to 1049 kinds (1050 gallery choices including plain). A plasma-like heightfield from the diamond-square midpoint displacement on a 64×64 vertex torus: the corner vertex (0, 0) starts at 0 and the step width is halved from 64, 32, … down to 2 (six levels); at every level the square step sets the middle of every square to the mean of its four corners and then the diamond step sets the middle of every edge to the mean of its four neighbours, each plus a random amount from the hash in the range `±0.55^level`; heights wrap round the torus, the mean is taken off, and `1/2 + height / 2.2` is the tone; between the vertices a smoothstep blends the four surrounding heights in both directions (so the field is C1); a cloud-like picture of amber highs and deep purple lows; the seed changes all the random amounts. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 64×64 size, the decay 0.55, the tone scale 2.2, the amber and deep purple tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the smaller grain (tone 0.005 and height 0.02, so that the noise in reading the heights back is far smaller than the random amounts of the finest level), the relief 0.004 (larger than the 0.0008 of most new materials, because the undulations are gentle and the normal map would be almost flat otherwise) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. I changed the parameters and looked at the previews several times (see ACCEPTANCE): with scale 4 in the first version the contrast was too low; with scale 2.2, the probe showed that the random coarsest levels push the mean height of the whole picture up or down, so that for seed 1 a third of the vertices had their tone pinned to the lower bound (the clamp to 0 and 1 cuts them off, and the heights read back are distorted), so I added 'take off the mean height', after which no vertex of any of the four seeds is clamped. The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**, deriving the structure of diamond-square independently from the vertex coordinates: the heights of the 4,096 vertices are read back from `(x / 64, y / 64)` (`tone = (colour − floor) / span`, height = `(tone − 1/2)·scale`, with the tone required to lie between 0.01 and 0.99, i.e. not clamped); for every vertex except the origin the level and parents follow from the number of trailing zeros of the smaller coordinate (both coordinates odd multiples of half a step means a square-step vertex with its four diagonal neighbours as parents, otherwise a diamond-step vertex with its four axis neighbours, wrapped round the torus), and the tests confirm that the numbers of vertices on the levels are 3, 12, 48, 192, 768 and 3072 (4,095 in all), that every vertex differs from the mean of its parents by at most `0.55^level` (with 0.03 of allowance for the grain in the read-back) and that on the three levels with 192 or more vertices the mean ratio of the difference to the allowed amount is between 0.45 and 0.56, which agrees with amounts spread evenly over `±0.55^level` (the mean would be a half); in addition at 3,000 points between the vertices the tone is recomputed from the read-back heights with a smoothstep blend formula written separately in the test and agrees with the sampler within 0.02 (measured largest 0.0043–0.0046). This shows that the sampler's heights really are built by the diamond-square rule (a mean plus a bounded random amount), by the relation of levels and parents, and by the smoothstep blend between vertices; it does **not** prove that the random amounts really are evenly distributed (only the mean ratio was tested), nor that the heightfield has the `1/f` 'fractal' spectrum, nor the quality of the seed selection (the tests only check that the vertex tones of seeds 0 and 1 differ by more than 0.05 at 50% to 70% of the vertices).

At start-up (per sampler) the vertex heights are stored in a `Float64Array(4096)`; starting from `height(0, 0) = 0`, for the step width `step = 64, 32, …, 2` (levels `0…5`) the square step sets `(x + step/2, y + step/2)` to the mean of the four corners `(x, y)`, `(x + step, y)`, `(x, y + step)` and `(x + step, y + step)`, the diamond step sets `(x + step/2, y)` and `(x, y + step/2)` to the mean of their four axis neighbours (`step/2` away, coordinates wrapping round the torus), and every value gets `(2·hash(x, y, seed ^ (salt + level)) − 1)·0.55^level` added; the mean height is then taken off; at sampling time the four surrounding vertices are found from `fract(u)·64` and `fract(v)·64` and blended with `smooth` (smoothstep) in both directions, `level = clamp(0.5 + blended height / 2.2)`: color is `toneFloor + 0.7·level + 0.005·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·level + 0.02·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops with the low parts to `1 − 0.4·(1 − level)` and metallic is 0; because the blend between vertices is a smoothstep, the slope is zero at the vertices and the field is C1; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(4096)` of 32,768 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 163,840 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction (4,095 vertices, one hash each) or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): the numbers of vertices on the levels are 3/12/48/192/768/3072; the largest `|difference| / 0.55^level` is 0.75–0.90 on the coarsest level and then up to 1.014 (levels 1 and 2), 1.044 (level 3), 1.100 (level 4) and 1.224 (level 5, where the allowed amount is only 0.050 and the grain noise is a sizeable part of it), the mean ratio on levels 3 to 5 is 0.487–0.520; the vertex tones range from 0.1897 to 0.7709, with no vertex clamped; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 37.78%–51.50%, color is 0.2088–0.3088 to 0.6999–0.7702 with a mean of 0.48998–0.49001, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6387–0.6973 and height is at most 0.6513–0.7338 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 37.74%–51.46%, color is 0.1903–0.3063 to 0.6763–0.7709 with a mean of 0.48998–0.49001, AO is at least 0.6289–0.6962 and height is at most 0.6244–0.7352 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 60.2% of the vertices differ in tone by more than 0.05 (42.0% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (131.1, 104.5, 83.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.00126 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles, the final version): amber cloud-like highs with deep purple dark patches and no obvious grid lines. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('diamondsquare', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`moirefringes` adds Moire fringes, bringing the current catalog from 1047 to 1048 kinds (1049 gallery choices including plain). Moiré fringes from two soft-edged line gratings multiplied: the first has `base` periods across the tile with its lines along `u`, the second has the whole-number wave vector `(beatU, base + beatV)`, and light passes only where both are open (the product of the two grating values); where the bars of the two gratings coincide a bright fringe appears and where they interleave a dark one, and the fringes repeat with the difference of the two wave vectors, `(beatU, beatV)` per tile (all wave vectors are whole numbers, so the tile repeats seamlessly); light blue on a deep blue-black ground; the seed picks `base` (16/20/24/28), one of 8 difference vectors (`(1,0)`, `(2,0)`, `(3,0)`, `(0,1)`, `(0,2)`, `(1,1)`, `(2,1)`, `(1,2)`) and two phases. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of any real grating.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the list of base frequencies, the list of difference vectors, the softness 0.6, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the light blue and deep blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at two seeds' previews). The tests check the frequency content **only through values read back from the sampler**: the colour at the centres of a 128×128 grid is analysed with a discrete Fourier transform written separately in the test (`m` from −8 to 8 and `n` from 0 to 40, half plane only), and the tests confirm that the two strongest high-frequency peaks (`n ≥ 10`, `|m| ≤ 4`) both have an amplitude between 0.115 and 0.125 and are the wave vectors of the two gratings, one of them being `(0, base)` with `base` in the list; that the strongest low-frequency peak (`n ≤ 8`, amplitude 0.075 to 0.085) is exactly the difference of the two wave vectors (turned into the half plane) and one of the listed difference vectors, and that the next low-frequency peak is below 0.02; that the four seeds give different grating pairs; and that repeated reads with one seed are identical. This shows that the fringe frequency the sampler draws really equals the difference of the two grating wave vectors; it does **not** prove the shape of the fringes or of the soft edges, nor the quality of the seed selection (the tests only check that the four seeds give different grating pairs). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0286). The lit-area share differs slightly between 256² and 512² sampling; the tests use the 256² values of seeds 0/1/0xffffffff.

At sampling time `base = frequencies[floor(hash(0, 25, seed ^ salt)·4)]`, `(beatU, beatV) = beats[floor(hash(1, 25, seed ^ salt)·8)]` and the phases are `hash(2, 25, …)` and `hash(3, 25, …)`; `one = cos(2π(base·fract(v) + phase 1))`, `two = cos(2π(beatU·fract(u) + (base + beatV)·fract(v) + phase 2))` and `open = smooth(clamp(one / 0.6 + 0.5))·smooth(clamp(two / 0.6 + 0.5))`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.7·open − gapTone)·open + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·open·(0.45 + 0.55·open) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; every function is smooth (a smooth step composed with a cosine), so the field is C1; the retained cache is only a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (there is no table), lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time** (no table is built; sampling includes two `cos`). Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): the wave vectors of the two gratings are (0, 28) and (2, 28), (0, 20) and (1, 20), (0, 28) and (3, 28), (0, 20) and (1, 21), i.e. base 28/20/28/20 and difference vectors (2, 0)/(1, 0)/(3, 0)/(1, 1); the grating peaks have an amplitude of 0.1206–0.1207, the low-frequency difference-vector peak 0.0795–0.0796 and the next low-frequency peak 0.0057–0.0127; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 21.81%–21.88%, color is 0.02559–0.02581 to 0.85430–0.85456 with a mean of 0.22320–0.22321, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8781–0.8788 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 21.72%–21.86%, color is 0.02512–0.02528 to 0.85446–0.85481 with a mean of 0.22315–0.22321, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8786–0.8795 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 34.5% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (52.0, 59.5, 74.0), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0286 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seeds 7 and 0): long thin light-blue horizontal lines on deep blue-black with sharp lens-shaped ends, the fringes in a gently slanting arrangement for seed 7 and a vertical one for seed 0. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('moirefringes', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`stringart` adds String art, bringing the current catalog from 1046 to 1047 kinds (1048 gallery choices including plain). The thread picture of the times-table circle: 96 points are spread evenly round a circle and numbered 0 to 95, and every point `i` is joined by a straight thread to the point `(m·i + c) mod 96`, so the threads envelop a curve (the multiplier `m = 2` gives a cardioid, 3 a nephroid, 4 a curve with three cusps and 5 one with four; these are the usual names and I did not verify them here); the seed picks the multiplier `m` (2 to 5) and the offset `c` (0 to 95); thin pink lines on a deep purple-black ground, one disc per 0.5 m tile. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 96 points, the radius 0.47, the line radius 0.003 and edge softness 0.002, the ranges of the multiplier and offset, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the pink and deep purple-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at three previews: the first had no offset `c`, and I found that seeds 0 and 1 picked the same multiplier and gave almost identical pictures (the mask difference between them was only 0.07%), so I added the offset `c` and looked at the preview again). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: for every multiplier 2 to 5 and offset 0 to 95 they first check whether the midpoints of all 96 threads are lit in the sampler, then compare the candidates that pass at 3000 points against a point-to-segment distance written separately in the test (lit within 0.001 of a thread, dark from 0.0045 on), take the candidate with the fewest disagreements as the reading, and require 0 disagreements, more than 2,000 clear points and more than 100 disagreements for the next best candidate — **this last requirement was added after a correction**: I found that with midpoints alone, false candidates differing from the real one by a small turn also pass (two candidates for seed 0, three for 0xffffffff and two for 1 had all midpoints lit), so only the point-by-point comparison determines the parameters uniquely. This shows that the lines the sampler draws really are the threads of the multiplier and offset read, and that the parameters are determined uniquely; it does **not** prove that the envelope of the lines is really a cardioid, a nephroid and so on, nor the quality of the seed selection (the tests only check that the (multiplier, offset) pairs of the four seeds are different and that 3 different multipliers occur). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0543, larger than for most materials because the lines are thin). The lit-area share differs slightly between 256² and 512² sampling (thin lines); the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff).

At start-up (per sampler) `multiplier = 2 + floor(hash(0, 24, seed ^ salt)·4)` and `offset = floor(hash(1, 24, seed ^ salt)·96)` decide the parameters, the 96 points are `0.5 + 0.47·(cos, sin)(2π·i / 96)`, and for every `i` `j = (multiplier·i + offset) mod 96` (skipped when `j = i`) gives the segment `(point i, point j)`; at sampling time only points within `radius + line radius` of the tile centre are evaluated, the distance from the point to every segment is computed, a thread is `smooth(clamp((0.003 − distance) / 0.002))` and the threads are combined as `1 − Π(1 − thread)` (smooth; a thread is a plateau for distances below 0.001, so the field is C1): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.7·mask − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·mask·(0.45 + 0.55·mask) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 outside the threads and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus a small array of at most 96 segments of 4 numbers each (not counted), lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time** (every sample inside the disc computes distances to at most 96 segments). Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): the (multiplier, offset) pairs read are (4, 61), (4, 65), (5, 26) and (3, 63); the numbers of candidates with all thread midpoints lit are 2/2/3/1 per seed, of which the correct one disagrees with the independent distance at 0 points (about 2,206–2,281 clear points) and the others at 378–406 points (seed 7 has only one candidate); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 16.55%–16.83%, color is 0.02521–0.02569 to 0.85370–0.85426 with a mean of 0.17865–0.18097, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8765–0.8781 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 16.33%–16.85%, color is 0.02509–0.02523 to 0.85449–0.85479 with a mean of 0.17684–0.18109, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8786–0.8794 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 21.9% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (53.3, 31.3, 49.6), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0543 and the minimum z component is 251. I viewed the preview: a disc of thin pink lines on deep purple-black, the envelope of the lines forming cusps inside the circle (three visible with multiplier 4, two with multiplier 3) and dense line ends along the rim; after adding the offset I looked at the seed-7 preview (multiplier 3) again, and the positions of the cusps are no longer left-right symmetric. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('stringart', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`happynumbers` adds Happy numbers, bringing the current catalog from 1045 to 1046 kinds (1047 gallery choices including plain). A 64×64 table of rounded square tiles in which row `i` and column `j` hold the number `n = 64i + j + 1` (1 to 4096); a number is replaced again and again by the sum of the squares of its decimal digits, and if it ends at 1 the number is a happy number, otherwise it falls into the cycle 4, 16, 37, 58, 89, 145, 42, 20, 4; an unhappy number is dark, a happy number glows, the brighter the fewer replacements it needs (the number 1 needs none and is brightest); 614 of the 4,096 numbers are happy; lime-green stars on a deep green ground; the seed moves the whole table around the torus. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 64×64 size, the tone mapping of happy numbers (0 to 6 replacements, tone `0.7·(0.35 + 0.65·(1 − count / 6))`), the deep green and lime-green tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at two previews: in the first the palette was still that of the previous material, dark brown and orange, because my generator did not replace it, which I noticed only when I looked at the picture; I changed it to deep green and lime-green with the same table). The sampler decides whether a number is happy by stopping at 1 or 4; the tests recompute the whole table in **another, independent way** — with the digits of the decimal string and a set that detects when a number repeats (without relying on the fact that the cycle always passes through 4) — and check that 614 of the 4,096 numbers are happy and that the numbers of numbers needing 0 to 6 replacements are 1, 3, 42, 157, 150, 173 and 88, and compare the colour at every cell centre against all 4096 possible shifts, which gives **exactly one** fitting shift for every seed (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03). This shows that the sampler's happy-number table agrees with the independent computation (including that every unhappy number up to 4096 falls into the cycle through 4, since the two methods agree on all 4,096 numbers); it does **not** prove that fact in general. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0377). The lit-area share differs between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the cell width (4 and 8 pixels) and the position of the sample points inside the cells differ; the tests use the 256² values.

At start-up (per sampler) for every number `n = 1…4096` the loop `while (n ≠ 1 and n ≠ 4) { n = sum of the squares of the digits; count++ }` runs, and the tone is `0.7·(0.35 + 0.65·(1 − count / 6))` when it ends at `n = 1` and 0 otherwise, stored in a `Float64Array(4096)`; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 23, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 23, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 64): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(4096)` of 32,768 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 163,840 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): 614 happy numbers, with 0 to 6 replacements numbering 1/3/42/157/150/173/88; each of the four seeds has a unique fitting shift, (23, 39), (48, 6), (45, 31) and (0, 21), with maximum fit errors of 0.014984–0.014999; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is always 6.46%, color is 0.05919–0.05949 to 0.84451–0.84637 with a mean of 0.17149–0.17164, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.7344 and height is at most 0.8280–0.8348 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is always 4.86%, color is 0.02518–0.02539 to 0.84269–0.84878 with a mean of 0.15184–0.15199, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8326–0.8400 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 26.3% of the cell centres differ in colour by more than 0.05 (8.6% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (34.3, 55.7, 33.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0377 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7, the deep green and lime-green version): scattered lime-green points of varying brightness on deep green, like a starry sky. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('happynumbers', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`euclidsteps` adds Euclid steps, bringing the current catalog from 1044 to 1045 kinds (1046 gallery choices including plain). A 64×64 table of rounded square tiles: the tile in row `i` and column `j` is the number of division steps `(a, b) → (b, a mod b)` that Euclid's algorithm needs to bring the pair `(i + 1, j + 1)` to a zero remainder, with a tone that rises with the step count (1 step darkest, the longest, 9 steps, brightest); a pair where `b` divides `a` takes only 1 step (darkest), so the darkest are the whole column `b = 1` and the lines where `b` divides `a`, and the longest are pairs near the golden ratio, giving fan-shaped dark lines of rational numbers radiating from the origin; dark violet to gold tones; the seed moves the whole table around the torus. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 64×64 size, the tone normalised by the longest step count, the dark violet and gold tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at two previews: the first used dark brown to orange, which had low contrast and dirty colours, so I changed it to dark violet to gold, with the same table). The sampler computes the step counts with a loop; the tests recompute the whole table in **another, independent way** — the recursion `steps(a, b) = b = 0 ? 0 : 1 + steps(b, a mod b)` — and check that the longest run is 9 steps and that the numbers of cells with 1 to 9 steps are 280, 671, 1006, 1005, 699, 327, 94, 13 and 1, and compare the colour at every cell centre against all 4096 possible shifts, which gives **exactly one** fitting shift for every seed (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03). This shows that the sampler's step table agrees with the independent recursion; it does **not** prove any theorem of number theory about Euclid's algorithm (these are only measured counts). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0377). The lit-area share, the highest colour and the AO differ between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the cell width (4 and 8 pixels) and the position of the sample points inside the cells differ, and because only one cell has the brightest 9 steps, so the highest colour reached depends on the sampling grid; the tests use the 256² values.

At start-up (per sampler) for every cell `(row, col)` starting from `(a, b) = (row + 1, col + 1)` the loop `while (b ≠ 0) { (a, b) = (b, a mod b); steps++ }` runs, the step count is stored in an `Int32Array(4096)` and the longest count `longest` (9) is noted, and the tone is `0.7·(steps − 1) / (longest − 1)`, stored in a `Float64Array(4096)`; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 22, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 22, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 64): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is an `Int32Array(4096)` of 16,384 B, a `Float64Array(4096)` of 32,768 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 180,224 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time** (construction is 4096 loops of at most 9 steps). Measured (tool-run): the numbers of cells with 1 to 9 steps are 280/671/1006/1005/699/327/94/13/1; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a unique fitting shift, (38, 62), (47, 26), (35, 15) and (43, 31), with maximum fit errors of 0.014989–0.014999; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 8.52%–8.62%, color is 0.06021–0.06042 to 0.84833–0.85052 with a mean of 0.31565–0.31568, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.7344 and height is at most 0.8270–0.8390 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 6.41%–6.47%, color is 0.02517–0.02538 to 0.84374–0.85155 with a mean of 0.27447–0.27450, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8331–0.8420 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 82.1% of the cell centres differ in colour by more than 0.05 (11.9% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (80.2, 63.1, 61.8), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0377 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7, the final dark violet to gold version): small rounded squares in dark violet and gold, with one darker whole column and one darker whole row, and dark fan-shaped lines radiating from the origin. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('euclidsteps', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`phasevortices` adds Phase vortices, bringing the current catalog from 1043 to 1044 kinds (1045 gallery choices including plain). The phase picture of the complex field `F = cos(2π(2x + a)) + i·cos(2π(2y + b))`: `F` vanishes where both cosines vanish, giving 4×4 = 16 isolated zeros per tile (vortices, 1/4 apart), and the phase turns once round every vortex; the colour draws lines of the phase — where `cos(6·phase)` is above a threshold it is bright — so exactly 6 bright spokes meet around every vortex and the spokes of neighbouring vortices join into lens shapes; the height adds rings of constant `|F|`; light lilac on a deep purple-black ground; the seed decides the shift `(a, b)`, that is the position of the whole vortex lattice. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 2 periods per axis, the 6 spokes, the vortex core size 0.05, the threshold 0.35, the 4 height rings, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the lilac and deep purple-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The tests check the topological property of the vortices **only through values read back from the sampler**: going once round a circle of radius 0.02 (96 sample points) they count how many times the colour crosses the middle of the tone range (twice the number of bright arcs); a cell of 1/4 × 1/4 is scanned in steps of 0.005, the points whose circle crosses 12 times (6 spokes) enclose a vortex and form one small blob (measured 37–39 scan points), and the circular mean of that blob (period 1/4, so that a vortex at the edge of the cell is not split in two) is the vortex position modulo 1/4; the tests then confirm that the circle at all 16 lattice positions crosses exactly 12 times and that the circle at the 16 points exactly half way between the vortices (1/8 off in both directions) crosses 0 times, i.e. has no winding. This shows that the sampler draws 16 vortices with exactly 6 spokes each, as a topological property read from the colour; it does **not** prove the direction of the phase turn (clockwise or anticlockwise; bright and dark lines do not show it), nor the shape of the height rings, nor the quality of the seed selection (the tests only check that the four seeds have different vortex lattice positions). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0090). The lit-area share differs slightly between 256² and 512² sampling; the tests use the 256² values of seeds 0/1/0xffffffff.

At sampling time `real = cos(2π(2·fract(u) + a))` and `imaginary = cos(2π(2·fract(v) + b))` with `a = hash(0, 21, seed ^ salt)` and `b = hash(1, 21, seed ^ salt)`; `magnitude = hypot(real, imaginary)`, and the unit vector of the phase `(real, imaginary) / magnitude` is raised to the 6th power by repeated products, whose real part is `powerX = cos(6·phase)`; `fade = smooth(clamp(magnitude / 0.05))` (the spokes fade out inside the vortex core, which keeps the field smooth at the vortex), `spoke = smooth(clamp((fade·powerX − 0.35) / 0.3))` and `ring = 0.5 + 0.5·cos(2π·4·magnitude)`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.7·spoke − gapTone)·spoke + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·(0.45 + 0.55·(0.6·spoke + 0.4·ring)) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 outside the spokes and metallic is 0; the retained cache is only a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (there is no table), lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time** (no table is built; sampling includes two `cos`, one `hypot` and 6 complex multiplications). Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): the scan points whose circle crosses 12 times are 39/37/39/39, and the vortex positions modulo 1/4 are (0.0489, 0.1670), (0.1113, 0.1263), (0.1783, 0.0075) and (0.2261, 0.0380); the circle at all 16 vortex positions crosses exactly 12 times (16 of 16 for every seed), and the circle at the 16 points half way between the vortices crosses 0 times (16 of 16 for every seed); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 27.96%–28.45%, color is 0.02537–0.02567 to 0.85410–0.85439 with a mean of 0.26940–0.27032, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8749–0.8772 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 28.08%–28.17%, color is 0.02511–0.02520 to 0.85459–0.85484 with a mean of 0.26949–0.26977, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8782–0.8789 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 46.8% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (62.7, 53.2, 90.7), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0090 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles, 8×8 vortices): light lilac spokes meeting in stars at the lattice points on a deep purple-black ground, the spokes between neighbouring vortices enclosing lens shapes. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('phasevortices', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`recamanarcs` adds Recaman arcs, bringing the current catalog from 1042 to 1043 kinds (1044 gallery choices including plain). The arc diagram of Recamán's sequence: `a(0) = 0` and `a(n)` is `a(n − 1) − n` when that is positive and has not appeared before, otherwise `a(n − 1) + n`; the first 60 steps are used (the sequence begins 0, 1, 3, 6, 2, 7, 13, 20, 12, 21, …, 61 positions with 57 distinct values and a maximum of 114), and every step is drawn as a half circle on a number line from `a(n − 1)` to `a(n)` (diameter `n`), the odd steps on one side of the line and the even steps on the other, so neighbouring large half circles join into nested, almost circular loops; every tile has two bands one above the other (the sides of the second swapped), thin teal lines on a deep teal-black ground; the seed shifts the whole picture sideways by up to 5.5 units (the tile is 128 units wide) and may swap the sides. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 60 steps, the width of 128 units, the side margin 7, the line radius 0.3 and edge softness 0.2, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the teal and deep teal-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at two previews: in the first the line radius was 0.9, and since the radii of neighbouring large half circles differ by only 1 they merged into thick rings in which no line could be told apart, so I changed it to 0.3). The sampler records the visited numbers in a `Set`; the tests rebuild the 61 positions from **another, independently written Recamán sequence** (also with a set, but written in the test) and then check **only through values read back from the sampler**: taking the number line (the middle line of the first band) as the reference, they look in steps of 0.02 for every shift at which the line is lit at all 61 positions and dark in all 263 gaps at least 0.6 from any position; the shifts that are kept form one block (10 to 25 steps, measured 17, about 0.32 units wide) and the middle of the block is taken as the shift; the tests then confirm that the apexes of all 60 half circles are lit on one side (on the other side at most a few, measured 4, by chance), that the shift is inside the allowed range, and, with a separately written polyline distance to the arcs (240 segments per half circle), that at 4000 points everything within 0.1 of an arc is lit and everything beyond 0.4 is dark (about 3,260 points are that clear; measured disagreements: 0). This shows that the half circles the sampler draws really correspond to Recamán's sequence with odd and even steps on opposite sides; it does **not** prove the shape of the soft edge (distance 0.1 to 0.4), nor the quality of the seed selection (the tests only check that the four seeds have different shifts and that both side swaps occur). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0543, larger than for most materials because the lines are thin). The 256² sampling undersamples the thin lines, so its lit-area share differs from the 512² one (see below); the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff).

At start-up (per sampler) the positions of the first 60 steps are computed with a `Set`, and `hash(0, 20, seed ^ salt)` gives the shift (±5.5 units) and `hash(1, 20, seed ^ salt) < 0.5` whether the sides are swapped; every half circle records its centre (`(a(n−1) + a(n)) / 2 + 7 + shift`), its radius (`n / 2`) and its side. At sampling time `(u, v)` is turned into units (`x = fract(u)·128`, `y = fract(v)·128`), the band is chosen by whether `y` is in the upper or lower half (the middle lines of the bands are at `y = 32` and `96`, and the sides of the second band are swapped) and `dy` is the offset from the band's middle line; for every half circle (skipped when the horizontal distance exceeds `radius + 0.3`): on the half circle's own side the distance is `|hypot(along, dy) − radius|`, otherwise it is the distance to the two end points of the diameter; every half circle is a line `smooth(clamp((0.3 − distance) / 0.2))` and the lines are combined as `1 − Π(1 − line)` (smooth, and a line is a plateau for distances below 0.1, so the field is C1): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.7·mask − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·mask·(0.45 + 0.55·mask) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 outside the lines and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus small arrays of 61 positions and 60 half circles (not counted), lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction (60 steps) or the sampling time** (every sample computes distances to at most 60 half circles, skipping those that are too far sideways). Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): the kept shifts form a contiguous block of 17 steps for every seed, with block middles 2.44/3.64/11.14/7.88; the apexes of all 60 half circles are lit on one side and 4/4/4/4 on the other (the lit side is one way for seeds 0 and 7 and the other way for seeds 1 and 0xffffffff); of 4000 points about 3,260 are clear enough (about 275–308 lit and 2,977–2,983 dark) and disagree with the independent polyline distance in 0 cases; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 10.58%–11.04%, color is 0.02520–0.02568 to 0.85385–0.85434 with a mean of 0.13175–0.13343, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8769–0.8782 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 11.31%–11.38%, color is 0.02508–0.02528 to 0.85435–0.85480 with a mean of 0.13574–0.13656, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8783–0.8795 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 13.5% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (24.2, 50.9, 55.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0543 and the minimum z component is 251. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles, the final thin-line version): thin teal lines on deep teal-black, the large half circles joining into nested, almost circular loops, a few small loops at the left end, and one band above another in every tile. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('recamanarcs', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`kaleidoscope` adds Kaleidoscope, bringing the current catalog from 1041 to 1042 kinds (1043 gallery choices including plain). A kaleidoscope or mandala pattern: a smooth value-noise field is averaged over the 8-fold dihedral group of the tile centre (a rotation by every 45°, with and without a mirror image, 16 elements), so the picture has exactly 8-fold rotation plus mirror symmetry and no crease along the mirror lines; the contour bands of the average (13 bands) are the pattern, as a copper-orange disc on a deep purple ground with fine concentric rings in the middle and rings of symmetric ornament outwards; one disc per 0.5 m tile; the seed decides the noise field and so the whole ornament. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of any real kaleidoscope.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 8-fold symmetry, the 10×10 noise cells, the 13 bands, the sharpness 0.7, the radius 0.47, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the copper-orange and deep purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at three previews: with 7 bands the disc was almost one flat bright area, with 18 bands the fine rings at the centre were too dense with a risk of aliasing, and I settled on 13). The tests of this material are **geometric property checks** that do not depend on any formula of the sampler: at 3000 points (a golden-ratio sequence) within radius 0.44 the colour of every point is compared with that of its image under the group — a rotation by 45°, the mirror image about the horizontal axis and the mirror image about the line at 22.5° — and the colour differences are within the grain (up to 0.03 in all, and not symmetric; measured largest 0.0289), whereas for a rotation by 22.5° or 72° (not among the 16 elements) the mean colour difference is 0.1 or more (measured 0.18–0.30). This shows that the sampler's output really has the symmetry of this group and not a higher one; it does **not** prove that this is the 'right' kaleidoscope, nor the quality of the noise field itself, nor the quality of the seed selection (the tests only check that seeds 0 and 1 differ in colour by more than 0.2 at more than 15% of the points and that repeated sampling with one seed is identical). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0163). The lit-area share differs slightly between 256² and 512² sampling; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff), where the lit share differs a lot between seeds: 28.8%–35.4%.

At sampling time `dx = fract(u) − 0.5`, `dy = fract(v) − 0.5` is the offset from the tile centre; for `k = 0…7` `(dx, dy)` is rotated by `k·45°` to `(rx, ry)` and the noise field is taken at `(0.5 + rx, 0.5 + ry)` and at `(0.5 + rx, 0.5 − ry)` (the mirror image), and the 16 values are averaged to `average`; `wave = cos(2π·13·average)`, `value = smooth(clamp(wave / 0.7 / 2 + 0.5))` and the disc mask is `mask = smooth(clamp((0.47 − r) / 0.01))`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.7·value − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·mask·(0.45 + 0.55·value) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 outside the disc and metallic is 0; because the field is averaged over the group instead of folded into a fundamental region there is no crease along the mirror lines, and the field is C1; the disc lies inside the tile (radius 0.47, and rotations preserve the radius), so every rotated point is inside the tile. The retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus the 10×10 noise field of 100 doubles, 800 B, 131,872 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time** (every sample has 16 noise lookups and 8 rotations). Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): the largest colour difference under a rotation by 45° is 0.02688/0.02813/0.02687/0.02804, under the mirror image about the horizontal axis 0.02792/0.02768/0.02887/0.02797, under the mirror image about the 22.5° line 0.02686/0.02819/0.02698/0.02758; the mean colour difference under a rotation by 22.5° is 0.2263/0.2973/0.2826/0.1775 and by 72° 0.2484/0.2694/0.2904/0.1923; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 28.77%–35.37%, color is 0.02572–0.02605 to 0.85398–0.85416 with a mean of 0.31689–0.35844, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8773–0.8778 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 28.97%–44.78%, color is 0.02517–0.02536 to 0.85468–0.85475 with a mean of 0.31714–0.41332, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8790–0.8793 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 31.1% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (120.6, 77.3, 75.4), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0163 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles, the final 13-band version): four copper-orange discs on deep purple with fine concentric rings in the middle, then a dark ring and rings of symmetric petal-like dark spots. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('kaleidoscope', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`zoneplate` adds Zone plate, bringing the current catalog from 1040 to 1041 kinds (1042 gallery choices including plain). A Fresnel zone plate: concentric bright and dark rings around a centre whose `n`-th transition between bright and dark lies at the radius `0.47·√((n + ½) / 14)`, so the rings get narrower towards the outside (14 zones, radius 0.47), with a smooth step between bright and dark; pale yellow-green rings on a deep blue-black ground, one disc per 0.5 m tile; the seed moves the centre by up to 0.03 around the middle of the tile and may swap bright and dark. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of any real zone plate. (Different from the existing `fresnel`, a Fresnel lens with equally spaced saw-tooth rings.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 14 zones, the radius 0.47, the drift 0.03, the transition width, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the pale yellow-green and deep blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: the centre is taken as the mean position of the lit pixels (color>0.5) of a 256² grid (a set of rings is symmetric about its centre, so the mean position is the centre), 8 rays are followed outwards from it in steps of 0.0005 and the radii where the colour crosses the middle of the tone range are interpolated linearly, and the tests confirm that on every ray the first 13 transitions between a bright and a dark zone are within 0.002 of `radius·√((n + ½) / zones)` — the `√` formula appears only in the test; that the number of transitions on a ray is 14 plus the rim of the plate (when the outermost zone is bright, which happens exactly when the centre zone is bright, since the number of zones is even); that the centre is within 0.03 of the middle of the tile; and that the four seeds give four different centres, with both a swapped and an unswapped bright/dark case among them. This shows that the zone radii the sampler draws follow the √n law of a zone plate; it does **not** prove the shape of the smooth step at the transitions, nor the quality of the seed selection. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0225). The lit-area share differs slightly between 256² and 512² sampling (and the bright/dark swap of seed 7 changes it too); the tests use the 256² values of seeds 0/1/0xffffffff.

At sampling time `dx`, `dy` are `fract(u)`, `fract(v)` minus the centre, which is `0.5 + (hash(0 / 1, 19, seed ^ salt) − 0.5)·2·0.03`, and the bright/dark swap is `hash(2, 19, seed ^ salt) < 0.5`; the wave is `wave = 0.5 + 0.5·cos(π·14·(dx² + dy²) / 0.47²)`, the brightness `lit = smooth(clamp((wave − 0.5) / 0.3 + 0.5))` (`1 − lit` when swapped) and the disc mask `mask = smooth(clamp((0.47 − r) / 0.01))`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.7·value − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·mask·(0.45 + 0.55·value) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 outside the disc and metallic is 0; every function is a smooth function of `r²` (a smooth step composed with a cosine), so the field is C1; the retained cache is only a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (there is no table), lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time** (no table is built; sampling includes one `cos` and one `sqrt`). Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): the centres estimated from the mean position of lit pixels are (0.5216, 0.4885), (0.4858, 0.4706), (0.5263, 0.4879) and (0.4844, 0.5264); the largest error of the first 13 transitions against the `√` formula is 0.00063/0.00064/0.00019/0.00020 (ray step in the probe 0.00047); the number of transitions per ray is 15 for seeds 0/1/0xffffffff (centre zone bright) and 14 for seed 7 (centre zone dark, i.e. swapped); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 32.89%–32.99%, color is 0.02542–0.02567 to 0.85387–0.85419 with a mean of 0.34066–0.34070, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8770–0.8778 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 32.91%–32.93% (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) and 34.55% (seed 7), color is 0.02515–0.02525 to 0.85456–0.85478 with a mean of 0.34066–0.35077, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8788–0.8794 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 35.3% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (84.6, 90.7, 83.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0225 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles): four pale yellow-green concentric-ring discs on deep blue-black, a dark circle in the middle and rings that get narrower and denser outwards, with a fine bright ring at the rim. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('zoneplate', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`graycode` adds Gray code, bringing the current catalog from 1039 to 1040 kinds (1041 gallery choices including plain). A rotary-encoder disc: the circle is split into 128 sectors and 7 concentric rings, and sector `n` carries on the rings, in order, the bits of the reflected binary Gray code of the number `n` (`n xor (n >> 1)`) — the innermost ring is the highest bit and the outermost the lowest — with bit 1 a lit silver-white arc and bit 0 a dark arc, so neighbouring sectors (also the last and the first) differ in exactly one ring; thin dark grooves separate the rings, there is one disc per 0.5 m tile, and the ground outside the disc is deep blue-black; the seed turns the disc by a whole number of sectors. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of any real encoder.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 128 sectors, the 7 rings, the inner and outer radii 0.10 and 0.46, the groove width, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the silver-white and deep blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The sampler gets the Gray code from `n xor (n >> 1)`; the tests rebuild the whole table of 128 entries in **another, independent way** — by reflection: the code for `k + 1` bits is the code for `k` bits followed by the same list in reverse order with the new top bit set — and then read the bits back from the sampler (the tone in the middle of every ring in the middle of every sector, decided lit or dark at the midpoint of the tone range, with every read-back at least 0.1 from the midpoint, so no ambiguous case). The tests check that the read-back bits fit the independent table with exactly **one** whole-sector turn (unique for each of the four seeds, out of 128 possible turns); that every pair of neighbouring sectors (including the last and the first) differs in exactly one ring — the definition of a Gray code, independent of how the table is written; and that exactly half (448) of the 896 bits are lit. This shows that the sampler's bit layout agrees with the independently reflected Gray code; it does **not** prove the shape of the blend zone at ring and sector edges (the last 35% of a sector blends with a smooth step towards the next sector's bit), which is covered only by the C1 checks. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0241, larger than for most materials because the height steps at ring and sector edges are steep). The lit-area share differs slightly between 256² and 512² sampling; the tests use the 256² values.

At sampling time the offset from the tile centre is `fract(u) − 0.5`, `fract(v) − 0.5`; the radius `r` decides the ring (`ring = floor((r − 0.10) / ((0.46 − 0.10) / 7))`, with arcs only for 0 to 6), the `atan2` angle is turned into 'sector units' `around = angle / 2π · 128`, and the sector is `n = (floor(around) + turn) mod 128` with `turn = floor(hash(0, 18, seed ^ salt) · 128)`; the bit on the ring is `((n xor (n >> 1)) >> (6 − ring)) & 1`, and over the last 35% of the sector it moves to that of the next sector by a smoothstep (zero slope at both ends, so the value is continuous and C1 across sector edges); the ring mask is `smooth(clamp(min(r − start, end − r) / 0.006))` (the ring is inset by 0.004 on both sides, forming the groove): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.7·value − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·mask·(0.45 + 0.55·value) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the grooves and outside the disc, and metallic is 0; the retained cache is only a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (there is no table), lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time** (no table is built; sampling includes one `atan2` and one `hypot`). Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): the unique whole-sector turn that fits the independent reflected table is 10/71/101/125; all 128 pairs of neighbouring sectors differ in exactly one ring; 448 of the 896 bits are lit; no read-back is ambiguous; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 22.57%–22.67%, color is 0.02551–0.02600 to 0.85383–0.85454 with a mean of 0.24738–0.24749, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8769–0.8788 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 22.58%–22.60%, color is 0.02521–0.02532 to 0.85467–0.85493 with a mean of 0.24738–0.24750, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8791–0.8798 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 23.0% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (62.8, 69.2, 82.7), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0241 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (2×2 tiles): four silver-white encoder discs on deep blue-black, the inner arcs longest and ever more broken towards the outside, the outermost ring fine short arcs, with dark thin grooves between the rings. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('graycode', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`poissondisk` adds Poisson disk, bringing the current catalog from 1038 to 1039 kinds (1040 gallery choices including plain). Dart throwing on the torus picks random points that are at least 0.085 apart (the shortest way around the torus), a Poisson-disk sample; every point gets a disc of radius 0.034 (less than half of the minimum distance, so the discs never touch), giving evenly spread mint discs on a deep teal-black ground; the seed decides the position and the number of all points (I measured 92/90/88/86 discs for seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7). It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the minimum distance 0.085, the disc radius 0.034, the 6000 candidates, the 12×12 buckets, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the mint and deep teal-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: the lit pixels (color>0.5) of a 256² grid are split into 4-connected discs on the torus with a flood fill written in the test, the centre of each disc is its circular mean (right for discs that cross the tile edge), and the tests confirm that there are 80 to 100 discs, each of 170 to 190 pixels, that every pair of disc centres is more than 0.083 apart on the torus (the minimum distance is 0.085 and the read-back centres are good to about one pixel, 1/256), and that no point of a 64×64 grid is 0.095 or more from the nearest disc centre (no gap is left where another point would have fitted, i.e. the dart throwing saturated). This shows that the discs the sampler draws really do not touch, keep the minimum distance and leave no large holes; it does **not** prove that such a point set is statistically a uniform Poisson-disk distribution (I did not separately verify the properties of dart throwing itself), nor the quality of the seed selection (the tests only check that, of the disc centres for seed 0, less than 15% have a counterpart within 0.01 among the centres for seed 1). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0016). The lit-area share differs slightly between 256² and 512² sampling; the tests use the 256² values.

At start-up (per sampler) the k-th candidate point is `hash(k, 0, seed ^ salt)`, `hash(k, 1, seed ^ salt)` (k from 0 to 5999) and is accepted when its shortest torus distance to every accepted point is at least 0.085; accepted points are filed into 12×12 buckets (bucket width 1/12, wider than a disc radius, so a lookup only needs the 3×3 buckets around it); at sampling time the nearest point in those 3×3 buckets is found, `t = clamp(1 − d²/0.034²)`, `mask = smooth(clamp(t/0.35))`, `dome = t²` and the tone is `0.7·(0.7 + 0.3·dome)`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 outside the discs and metallic is 0; a disc is only a function of the squared distance to its point, exactly zero at its rim, and discs never overlap, so the field is C1. The retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus small arrays of the coordinates of about 90 points and the buckets (not counted), all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction time (about 90 points, 6000 candidates times the number of accepted points in distance comparisons) or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): 92/90/88/86 discs (the same on 256² and 512² grids); the smallest distance between disc centres is 0.08470/0.08445/0.08440 on a 256² grid (0.08483 for seed 7) and 0.08490–0.08520 on a 512² grid; disc sizes are 177–185 pixels on 256² and 718–731 pixels on 512²; the largest distance from a point of the 64×64 grid to the nearest disc centre is 0.0871–0.0898; of the 92 disc centres for seed 0 only 1 has a seed-1 disc centre within 0.01; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 24.31%–25.38%, color is 0.02535–0.02559 to 0.85011–0.85301 with a mean of 0.21783–0.22576, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8363–0.8454 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 23.77%–25.39%, color is 0.02509–0.02527 to 0.85148–0.85324 with a mean of 0.21369–0.22578, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8396–0.8461 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 38.4% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (44.2, 74.9, 69.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0016 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed the preview: equal-sized mint discs on a deep teal-black ground, evenly spaced, not overlapping and with no obvious regular arrangement. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('poissondisk', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`wangtiles` adds Wang tiles, bringing the current catalog from 1037 to 1038 kinds (1039 gallery choices including plain). A random Wang tiling on a 16×16 table of rounded square tiles: every edge between two neighbouring tiles has one of two colours (dark or light) chosen at random, and every tile is drawn with the colours of its own four edges (top, bottom, left, right) — so two tiles that share an edge always agree on its colour, the matching rule of Wang tiles; inside a tile the tone is a smooth average of the four edge colours weighted by the distance to the middle of each edge, so the patch of an edge forms a blurred diamond across the two tiles. Amber on a deep purple ground; the seed decides all the edge colours. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 16×16 size, the two edge colours, the weights `(1 − d²/reach²)²` (reach 0.9), the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the amber and deep purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The sampler first picks the colour of every horizontal and vertical edge on the torus with `hash`, and the two tiles at an edge share the same datum, so the matching rule is true by construction; the tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: the colours of the four edges of every tile are read 0.4 of a cell from the tile centre towards each edge (the read-back value is at least 0.1 away from the midpoint, so there is no ambiguous case), every shared edge is confirmed to read back with the same colour from both sides (including the wrap-around of the torus), all 16 kinds of tile (the combinations of four edge colours) occur, and at about 2,500 points inside the tiles the tone is recomputed with a weighting formula written separately in the test (taking the read-back edge colours as input) and compared with the sampler within the grain (0.015). This shows that the sampler's edge colours agree and its tone formula matches the independent formula; it does not prove statistical properties of the random distribution, nor the quality of the seed selection (the tests only check that the share of top edges differing between seeds 0 and 1 lies between 35% and 65%). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0068).

At start-up (per sampler) for every cell `(i, j)` `hash(i, j, seed ^ salt)` decides the colour of the 'horizontal edge above the tile' (< 0.5 dark = 0, otherwise light = 1) and `hash(i, j, seed ^ (salt + 1))` the colour of the 'vertical edge left of the tile', each stored in a `Uint8Array(256)`; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1); the top, bottom, left and right edges of a tile come from this cell and the cells below and to the right (modulo 16), the weight of each edge is `max(0, 1 − d²/0.9²)²` (`d` being the distance to the edge's midpoint in cell widths), the tone is `0.7·Σ weight·edge colour / Σ weight`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is two `Uint8Array(256)` of 512 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 131,584 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): the number of shared edges that read back with different colours from their two sides is 0, all 16 kinds of tile occur and no read-back is ambiguous; recomputing 2,541 points with the independent formula from the read-back edge colours gives a maximum difference of 0.01445–0.01485; of the 512 top and left edges in all, 243–249 are light (1); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 32.56%–32.89%, color is 0.02570–0.02586 to 0.85340–0.85405 with a mean of 0.35701–0.35805, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8422–0.8461 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 31.69%–32.56%, color is 0.02520–0.02542 to 0.85425–0.85473 with a mean of 0.35193–0.35792, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8477–0.8491 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 30.0% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (102.7, 75.9, 57.6), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0068 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed the preview: amber rounded square tiles on deep purple, each with a smooth light-to-dark gradient inside, the patches of the edges forming blurred diamonds across two tiles. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('wangtiles', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`bayerdither` adds Bayer dither, bringing the current catalog from 1036 to 1037 kinds (1038 gallery choices including plain). An ordered-dither grey ramp on a 64×64 table of rounded square tiles: the 8×8 Bayer threshold matrix (built from `M(1) = [0]` by the doubling recursion `M(2s) = [[4M, 4M + 2], [4M + 3, 4M + 1]]`, with the values 0 to 63 spread as evenly as possible) is repeated over the table, and a cell glows when its threshold is below the 'brightness level' of its column; the level rises by 2 for every column from 2 at the left and right edges of the table to 64 in the middle (every cell lit) and falls symmetrically back, so the glowing share grows smoothly from about 3% to 100% and back, the way a halftone printer renders a grey ramp. Silver-white tiles lie on a deep blue ground; 2,112 of the 4,096 cells glow; the seed moves the whole table around the torus. It is a schematic halftone picture, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 64×64 size, the 8×8 Bayer matrix, the triangular ramp whose level rises by 2 per column, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the silver-white and deep blue colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The sampler builds the Bayer matrix with the doubling recursion; the tests recompute it in **another, independent way** — the closed form in which every bit `j` of the coordinates contributes `4^(2 − j)·(2·(x_j xor y_j) + y_j)` — and I first confirmed with a probe that this closed form is identical to the recursion on all 64 cells of the 8×8 matrix; the tests check that the matrix holds each of 0 to 63 once and that 2,112 cells glow, and compare the colour at every cell centre against all 4,096 possible shifts. **The shift is not unique for this material**: because the dither matrix repeats every 8 rows, shifting vertically by 8 cells changes nothing, so every seed has exactly **8** fitting shifts (the same horizontal shift and vertical shifts that differ by multiples of 8), which the tests check explicitly instead of expecting a unique solution (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03). This shows that the sampler's Bayer matrix, level ramp and glow rule agree with the independent formula. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0378). The lit-area share, the lowest colour and the AO differ between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the cell width (4 and 8 pixels) and the position of the sample points inside the cells differ, not because of different seeds; the tests use the 256² values.
