`hestain` adds H&E-stained tissue, bringing the current catalog from 952 to 953 kinds (954 gallery choices including plain). A schematic of a microscope slide of hematoxylin-and-eosin stained tissue: a pale pink-violet cytoplasm with mottle and fibre streaks along v, scattered with dark purple oval nuclei whose positions and shapes come from the spot regime of periodic Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion (a high threshold leaves only the cores), each with a very faint pale halo. It is not real histology: there are no cell membranes, no chromatin structure inside nuclei, no cell-type differences, vessels or tissue layers, the nuclei are more evenly spread than in real tissue, and because of the single dark-to-light gradient the cytoplasm is lavender rather than eosin pink.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source, histology atlas or measurement cited and no photograph compared; the reaction-diffusion parameters equal `cheetahfur`'s (feed 0.04, kill 0.065, 6000 steps, a 96×96 grid), the nucleus threshold of 0.6 (higher than cheetahfur's 0.5, so the nuclei are smaller), the sharpness, the halo, the purple and pink tones and the 0.05 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real tissue. In the first preview the cytoplasm was a dark lavender (0.72); I raised the base to 0.8 and lowered the halo to 0.04 (also so that the sum of tones stays inside [0, 1]), and it is still lavender rather than pink, which is a limit of a single gradient.

It reuses `latticeField` and `grayScott`. A dedicated sampler takes the smooth nucleus mask `nucleus = 0.5 + 0.5·tanh(12·(pattern − level))` (level = 0.6 ± 0.1 moving with a slow 5×5 noise); the halo is a thin band around a lower iso-level, `exp(−((pattern − level + 0.14)/0.1)²)·(1 − nucleus)` (C-infinity); color is `0.8 + 0.14·(14×14 noise − 0.5) + 0.1·(110×26 fibre noise − 0.5) − 0.62·nucleus + 0.04·halo + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`; height is `0.6·nucleus + 0.4·grain`; roughness rises by 0.1 on nuclei; the cache totals 96² + 7² + 5² + 14² + 110×26 + 128² = 28,730 Float64 values / 229,840 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM; building also uses about 294,912 B of scratch arrays, of which only v is kept). Defaults are a 0.05 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Simulation cost: on this machine under bun a sampler build took about 190–296 ms and 512² maps about 281 ms (single measurements, not a benchmark).

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('hestain', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`; the first build for each seed spends about 0.2 s more on the simulation.

`petricolonies` adds petri dish colonies, bringing the current catalog from 951 to 952 kinds (953 gallery choices including plain). Cream round colonies scattered over a flat amber agar surface; colony positions and shapes come from the spot regime of periodic Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion and their sizes vary; each colony has a slightly darker thin rim and a slightly raised centre (height and roughness follow the colony), over a fine agar grain. It is not a real dish's circular border, the mucoid gloss of colonies, concentric structure inside colonies, bubbles or translucency, and the preview has only one amber-to-cream gradient.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source, microbiology photograph or measurement cited and no photograph compared; the reaction-diffusion parameters equal `cheetahfur`'s (feed 0.04, kill 0.065, 6000 steps, a 96×96 grid), and the threshold, sharpness, rim width, amber and cream tones, roughness and the 0.12 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real species. In the first preview the rim was almost invisible, so I widened it from 0.07 to 0.12, deepened its tone from 0.2 to 0.4 and raised the colony size variation from 0.3 to 0.5; these adjustments are my subjective reading of the preview.

It reuses `latticeField` and `grayScott`. A dedicated sampler takes the smooth colony mask `fill = 0.5 + 0.5·tanh(9·(pattern − level))` (level = 0.5 ± 0.25 moving with a slow 5×5 noise, so colony sizes differ); the rim is a thin band around the same iso-level, `exp(−((pattern − level)/0.12)²)·(1 − fill)` (C-infinity, only outside the colony); color is `0.42 + 0.42·fill − 0.4·rim + 0.04·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`; height is `0.8·fill·pattern + 0.2·grain`, so colony centres (large pattern) are higher; roughness rises by 0.4 on colonies; the cache totals 96² + 7² + 5² + 128² = 25,674 Float64 values / 205,392 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM; building also uses about 294,912 B of scratch arrays, of which only v is kept). Defaults are a 0.12 m nominal tile and 0.0015 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement; at 0.003 in the first version the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps was 0.117, and 0.0015 gave about 0.0314). Simulation cost: on this machine under bun a sampler build took about 190–309 ms and 512² maps about 270–304 ms (single measurements, not a benchmark).

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('petricolonies', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`; the first build for each seed spends about 0.2 s more on the simulation.

`turingmaze` adds a Turing maze, bringing the current catalog from 950 to 951 kinds (952 gallery choices including plain). A dark ink labyrinth on white paper: curved, branching, partly closed thick stripes produced by periodic Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion in its labyrinth regime, whose width and density vary slightly with slow noise, over a fine paper grain. On the tested seeds the ink forms one connected network. This is a reaction-diffusion stripe pattern and **not a fingerprint** (fingerprint ridges are much finer and have whorls and bifurcations), nor real printing or ink; the preview has a single ink-to-paper gradient.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source cited and no photograph compared; the reaction-diffusion parameters (feed 0.03, kill 0.057, 6000 steps, a 96×96 grid), the threshold and sharpness, the warp amount, the ink and paper tones and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real object. I first named it fingerprint, but after viewing the preview the stripe spacing was roughly five to ten times too coarse and there were no whorls, so it was renamed `turingmaze`.

It reuses the shared helpers `latticeField` and `grayScott` added for `cheetahfur`. A dedicated sampler looks the same periodic pattern up after a light noise warp (±0.025 UV) and takes a smooth stripe mask `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(9·(pattern − level))` (level = 0.5 ± 0.12 moving with a slow 7×7 noise); ink density is stripe × (0.82 + 0.18·7×7 noise) and color is `0.94 − 0.86·ink + 0.05·(160² fine grain − 0.5)`; the cache totals 96² + 5² + 7² + 7² + 160² = 34,939 Float64 values / 279,512 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM; building also uses about 294,912 B of scratch arrays, of which only v is kept). Height is about 0.7 × stripes plus 0.3 × grain; roughness drops by up to 0.15 on ink. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). The labyrinth parameters were stable on the 12 seeds I scanned (raw peak v of 0.32–0.35 and a consistent edge density), which does not guarantee stability for every seed. Simulation cost: on this machine under bun a sampler build took about 192–252 ms and 512² maps about 293 ms (single measurements, not a benchmark).

`cheetahfur` adds cheetah fur, bringing the current catalog from 949 to 950 kinds (951 gallery choices including plain). Black oval spots on short tawny fur, where the spot positions, sizes and shapes come from a periodic Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion simulation, so they are irregular but similarly spaced like natural spots rather than random dots or a fixed grid; the fur carries fine fibres along v and the spots are slightly rougher. It is not a real cheetah's coat gradient, the pale halo around spots, white belly fur or fur direction, and the preview has only one tawny-to-black gradient.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of cheetah markings. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the reaction-diffusion parameters (feed 0.04, kill 0.065, 6000 steps, a 96×96 grid), the spot threshold and sharpness, the warp amount, the fur and spot tones and the 0.25 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real cheetah. It is the first material in this engine that runs a simulation while its sampler is built; every other material is still a pure noise function.

A dedicated sampler plus two shared helpers: `latticeField(values, nx, ny)` is a periodic lattice sampler (the same smoothstep blend as the existing `cachedNoise`, C1; `cachedNoise` now calls it), and `grayScott(size, seedCells, feed, kill, steps, seed)` runs Gray-Scott on a periodic size×size grid (Du 0.2097, Dv 0.105, dt 1; only additions, subtractions and multiplications are used, with no transcendental functions, so the bits do not depend on the engine). The initial perturbation is one 3×3 block per jittered `seedCells×seedCells` cell so that no seed can start as a long band, and the inhibitor concentration is normalised to [0, 1]. Sampling looks the pattern up after a light `warpField` distortion (±0.015 UV) and takes a smooth spot mask `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(7·(pattern − level))` (level = 0.5 ± 0.1 moving with a 5×5 slow noise, so spot sizes differ slightly); fur color is `0.86·(1 − spot) + 0.05·spot` plus a 200×28 fibre noise stretched along v and a 128² fine grain; the cache totals 96² + 6² + 5² + 200×28 + 128² = 31,261 Float64 values / 250,088 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM; building also uses four 96² scratch arrays u, v, nextU and nextV, about 294,912 B, of which only v is kept). Simulation cost: on this machine under bun a sampler build took about 169–176 ms and 512² maps about 271 ms (single measurements, not a benchmark). Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile and 0.0015 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement).

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('cheetahfur', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`. Note the first build for each seed spends about 0.2 s more on the simulation.

`jade` adds jade, bringing the current catalog from 948 to 949 kinds (950 gallery choices including plain). A polished green nephrite surface: a mid-green cloudy tone (a broad plus a fine cloud), crossed by pale green veins (following iso-contours of a noise field, so they form closed or winding curves) and finer hairline veins; the surface is smooth (low roughness) and slightly rougher on the veins. It is not a real jade's translucency, subsurface scattering, cotton-like inclusions, orange rind or real vein distribution, and the preview reads more like marbling drawn along iso-contours.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of polished nephrite jade. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts of the noise fields, the cloud weights, the iso-contour positions and widths of the veins, the dark and light green tones, roughness and the 0.15 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real jade.

A dedicated sampler takes the cloud as `0.7·cloud(5×5) + 0.3·fine(18×18)` periodic noise; the veins are thin bands around an iso-contour of a noise field, `exp(−((n − c)/w)²)` (C-infinity; a ridge `|n − c|` would not be C1), with `n` a 7×7 noise field, `c = 0.5` and `w = 0.045`, plus hairline veins from a 13×13 noise field with `c = 0.45` and `w = 0.03`, joined by the union `1 − Π(1 − x)`; a 128² fine grain is added; the cache totals 25 + 324 + 49 + 169 + 16,384 = 16,951 Float64 values / 135,608 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height is about 0.5 relief × cloud plus 0.2 × veins plus 0.3 × grain; roughness rises by 0.06 on veins; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.15 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: pale veins (color>0.6) cover 2.3–4.9% (varying a lot with the seed), color is 0.201–0.768 with a mean of 0.376–0.399, roughness is 0.20–0.26 and height is at most 0.859–0.902 relief; the vein masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 8.5% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (77, 115, 87) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0057. I viewed the preview: pale green iso-contour veins over a mid-green cloudy ground that read as a marbled green stone, but the vein paths (closed loops and sharp turns) are more regular and unnatural than a real jade's, and there is no translucency at all. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('jade', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`spectrogram` adds spectrogram, bringing the current catalog from 947 to 948 kinds (949 gallery choices including plain). A spectrogram-style surface on a deep blue ground: 12 horizontal yellow harmonic lines bent into waves by vibrato, 5 vertical broadband burst bands and scattered speckle, with a time-frequency energy field deciding where it shows (patches fade). It is not a real audio spectrum, real harmonic ratios, time/frequency scales, a colour-scale legend or text; every harmonic has the same vibrato depth (real higher harmonics wobble more), and colour is a single linear dark-blue-to-bright-yellow gradient rather than the multi-colour scales common on real spectrograms.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a spectrogram. No specific source document, photograph, audio data or measurement is cited and no real spectrogram was compared; the harmonic count (12), vibrato depth and cycles, drift amount, energy-field resolution and threshold, burst count and weight, the deep blue and bright yellow tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices.

A dedicated sampler draws the harmonic lines as an integer number (12) of `exp(−sin²(π·12·(v − shift))/w²)` (C-infinity, wrapping with the tile) with shift = `(0.2·sin(2π·6·u) + 0.18·(drift(u) − 0.5))/12` (vibrato plus a slow drift from an 8×2 periodic noise field); the bursts are an integer number (5) of vertical `exp(−sin²(π·5·u)/w²)`; the speckle is a 96×96 periodic noise field; all three are multiplied by a smooth gate from a 20×14 energy field, `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(5·(noise − 0.35))`, and joined by the union `1 − Π(1 − x)` so intensity stays in [0, 1]; the cache totals 16 + 280 + 9,216 + 16,384 = 25,896 Float64 values / 207,168 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Colour is pigment mapped from intensity (0.04 + 0.9 × intensity), height is about 0.6 relief × intensity plus 0.4 relief of paper grain; roughness is always 0.4; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: bright lines (color>0.5) cover 6.31–6.76%, color is 0.0400–0.939 with a mean of 0.155–0.161 and height is at most 0.971–0.982 relief; the harmonic line position follows the vibrato (about +0.2 of a spacing at a positive vibrato peak and about −0.2 at a negative one, verified by the tests for each seed, with a tolerance including the drift's upper bound of 0.09); the bright-area masks (color>0.2) of seeds 0 and 1 differ on more than 5% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (50, 41, 67), r>128 covers 7.0% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.092. I viewed the preview: neat yellow wavy lines and vertical bright bands on a deep blue ground that read as a stylised spectrogram, but too regular (all harmonics bend in phase and are equally spaced). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('spectrogram', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`barchart` adds bar chart paper, bringing the current catalog from 946 to 947 kinds (948 gallery choices including plain). This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a bar chart. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the chart and bar counts (2 charts × 12 bars), bar width, height range, grid line count and width, plot-area bounds, navy and paper tones, roughness and the 0.25 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real chart.

A dedicated sampler draws each bar as a smooth box — a width term `smooth(clamp((0.34 − |dx|)/0.03))` plus one top term and one baseline term, each `smooth(clamp(…/0.03))` — kept entirely inside its own column (half-width 0.34 < 0.5); the grid lines are `exp(−sin²(π·steps)/w²)` inside the plot area (C-infinity, limited by a plot-area mask) and the baseline is `exp(−d²/w²)`; bar heights come from a per-column hash; everything is a convex mix; the cache totals 24 + 16,384 = 16,408 Float64 values / 131,264 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, bar and baseline height is about 0.6 relief plus 0.4 relief of paper grain and roughness drops 0.08 on bars; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. `ecgpaper` adds ECG paper, bringing the current catalog from 945 to 946 kinds (947 gallery choices including plain). A pale pink medical chart paper: a 40×40-per-tile fine grid (a heavier major line every 5 cells, so 8×8 large squares), three horizontal recording strips each repeating six heartbeat waveforms (P, Q, R, S and T waves, with ±18% amplitude variation from beat to beat) drawn in a thin dark maroon line on the strip baseline. It is not a real ECG's lead labels, calibration pulse, time scale, pathological waveforms or printed text; the waveform is a simplified schematic curve (its T wave has a flat top).

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of ECG chart paper. No specific source document, photograph, medical standard or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the grid (40×40 per tile, major every 5), the strip and beat counts (3 strips × 6 beats), the wave positions and heights, line width, pink paper and maroon ink tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real ECG paper or to be usable for medical purposes.

A dedicated sampler draws the minor and major grids as one integer-count family per direction of `exp(−sin²(π·n·s)/w²)` (C-infinity, wrapping with the tile), joined by the union `1 − Π(1 − x)`; each strip's heartbeat is five compact bumps for the P, Q, R, S and T waves — `a·smooth(1 − ((x − c)/s)²)` is exactly zero for `|x − c| ≥ s` and C1, so each beat is exactly zero at its own ends and the per-beat amplitudes leave no step between beats (I first used Gaussians, whose tails are not exactly zero and left a jump of about 10⁻¹² at beat boundaries, which the C1 test magnified to about 0.038 and failed on); the trace is `exp(−d²/w²)` of width 0.0035 with `d = dy / √(1 + slope²)` the first-order distance to the curve so steep strokes keep a similar thickness, limited by two C1 windows to the vertical range the curve can reach and to its own strip; the grid and paper grain are combined and the ink is mixed in by a convex mix; the cache totals 18 + 16,384 = 16,402 Float64 values / 131,216 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, trace height is about 0.6 relief plus 0.4 relief of paper grain and roughness drops 0.1 on ink; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: ink (color<0.3) covers 3.23–3.27% (3.13% at seed 7), paper (color>0.85) covers 73.8–73.9%, color is 0.05–0.955 with a mean of 0.859–0.860, roughness is 0.60–0.70 and height is at most 0.983–0.992 relief; the baseline of every strip and the top of every R wave are ink (the test verifies each beat, 3 strips × 6 beats); the ink masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on only 0.75% of pixels (only the per-beat amplitudes and the paper grain change with the seed); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (228, 206, 206), r<110 covers 2.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.061. I viewed the preview: three repeating heartbeat traces on pink grid paper that read as ECG paper overall, though the R waves are short and the T wave is flat-topped, unlike a real waveform. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('ecgpaper', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`. Use at least size 512 so the fine grid (about 13 pixels per cell) and the trace (about 2 pixels wide) are legible.

`redalder` adds red alder, bringing the current catalog from 944 to 945 kinds (946 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished longitudinal Alnus rubra face: an even light yellowish-tan to slightly reddish ground, a fine uniform texture, two very faint darker bands, longitudinal fibre grain and very few (about 0.15%) fine dark short marks (standing in for the occasional aggregate rays). It is not a heartwood/sapwood distinction, the wide streaks of aggregate rays, knots, wavy grain or a finish.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database Red Alder](https://www.wood-database.com/red-alder/) (Color/Appearance: light tan to reddish brown, darkening and reddening with age, no visible heartwood/sapwood distinction, occasional small streaks from aggregate rays; Grain/Texture: generally straight with a moderately fine, uniform texture; Endgrain: diffuse-porous with small to medium, numerous pores) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/alnus-rubra.jpg) (an even light tan face, very faint lengthwise color change and scattered tiny dark short marks). These are color and grain-form references only: the wide streaks of aggregate rays, knots and wavy grain are **not** reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or real dimensions are not derived from the photograph; the numerous small pores are too small to show here, and a few dark marks stand in for the occasionally visible rays.

It reuses the existing Padauk/Bloodwood-family long elliptical vessel sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `blackwalnut`, `teak`, `honduranmahogany`, `shagbarkhickory`, `eastindianrosewood`, `bubinga`, `jarrah` and `merbau`); only the constructor selects the preset: a 36×12 vessel-site table (13,824 B), two undulating (bandWarp 0.8), very low-contrast (bandContrast 0.1) dark bands, a 220×9 longitudinal fibre field, 128² fine grain and the fixed 3×4 warp table, totalling 20,104 Float64 values / 160,832 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0; the dark marks are real height depressions while color streaks are pigment. The default 0.18 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. Because the shared sampler keeps the body color at about 0.25–0.46 of the palette, I chose a lighter warm-brown palette (dark (178, 124, 80) / light (246, 204, 150)) so the body color approaches the photograph's light tan. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid: dark marks (AO<0.9) cover 0.12–0.15%, undented body covers 99.8%, body color is 0.254–0.459, the across/along color-difference ratio is 9.98–10.64, roughness 0.50–0.602, height 0.45–0.503 relief and minimum AO 0.75; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (204, 155, 107), AO<230 covers 0.147% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0008. I viewed the preview: an even light tan face with very faint bands and scattered fine dark marks, similar to the photograph in overall tone and evenness; the photograph is finer and more orange-yellow (my by-eye estimate is about (215, 170, 120), not a measurement). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('redalder', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of sherpa fleece. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts, probabilities, sizes and aspect ratios of the two lump layers, the edge noise, the tones, roughness and the 0.15 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real fabric.

Color is pigment, dome height is about 0.85 relief plus 0.15 relief of grain; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.15 m nominal tile and 0.012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I tuned this preset twice: the first version (22×22 grid, smaller lumps) looked like coarse sand or crumbs, and the second, with larger lumps, read more like fluffy tufts and was adopted; the first version's tones also let colour reach 1.01 (outside [0, 1]), and lowering the large/small lump tones to 0.52/0.58 and the dome to 0.2 brought the maximum back to 0.93. This material is an authored schematic of the general look of tilled soil. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts, probabilities, sizes and aspect ratios of the clod and pebble layers, the edge noise, the layer tones, roughness and the 0.4 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real soil.

It reuses the existing two-layer rotated-ellipse piece sampler of `granola` by fallthrough (the constructor only selects the preset; no new sampler): clods (8×8 grid, probability 1, semi-axes 0.34–0.62 cell × a 0.7–1.3 aspect) and pale pebbles (16×16 grid, probability 0.3, semi-axes 0.1–0.22 cell) are each jittered ±0.45 in their cell with a random rotation, and each pixel composites the pieces of its 5×5 cells in a fixed order (the largest piece, at maximum stretch and edge perturbation, can reach more than one cell past its own, so a 3×3 window would cut it) — `value = value·(1 − m) + piece·m` with the mask `m = smooth(clamp((1 − q)/0.4))`, `q` multiplied by an edge perturbation from a 48×48 periodic noise field — clods first, pebbles over them, so every term is C1; the part not covered by any piece has colour 0.14 and AO 0.45; the cache totals 448 + 1,792 + 2,304 + 16,384 = 20,928 Float64 values / 167,424 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, dome height is about 0.8 relief plus 0.2 relief of grain; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile and 0.012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). While writing this preset I first set the pebble tone to 0.78 and the probe showed colour up to 1.03 (outside [0, 1]); lowering it to 0.66 ± 0.08 fixed that. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: the gap ground between clods (AO<0.46) covers 35.9–41.8% (42.0% at seed 7), pale pebbles (color>0.5) cover 6.8–9.4%, color is 0.094–0.899 with a mean of 0.270–0.288, the gap ground averages 0.140, roughness is always 0.92, minimum AO is 0.45 and height is at most 0.994–0.997 relief; the cover masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 43.7% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (62, 47, 35), AO<200 covers 50.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.894. I viewed the preview: lighter brown clods and small pebbles over a dark brown gap ground that read as loose soil, but quite like a camouflage pattern and far flatter than real soil. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('tilledsoil', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

It is not a real heat sink's fin height and thickness, base plate, heat pipes, clips or machining burrs.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of an extruded aluminium heat sink. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the fin count (20 per tile), the fin-top to gap ratio and sharpness, the metal tones, extrusion-line and mottle strength, roughness and the 0.1 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real heat sink specification.

Color is the metal's reflectance colour, fin-top height is about 0.8 relief, extrusion lines 0.1 and grain 0.1; there is no mortar. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: fin tops (color>0.5) cover 47.1–47.3% and gaps (color<0.25) 43.4–43.7%, the region with AO<0.9 is always 56.25% (seed-independent), color is 0.099–0.777 with a mean of 0.416–0.421, roughness is 0.38–0.58, minimum AO is 0.50, metallic is always 1 and height is at most 0.988–0.992 relief; on a fin top the per-pixel colour difference along u (across fins) is about 4.9–5.3 times that along v (the extrusion lines); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (76, 79, 86), the metallic channel averages 255 and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.716. I viewed the four-panel preview: neat straight fins with deep gaps that read as an extruded-aluminium heat sink, but very simplified (no fin height, chamfers or base plate). A cream-white floret surface built from domed buds at three scales (10², 26² and 64² cells): large florets carry smaller buds that carry still smaller bumps; bud crowns are brighter, the gaps are grey-beige with AO occlusion (AO<0.7 covers about 15%), and the whole is rough (roughness a constant 0.78) with a fine grain. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; the cell counts, radius, amplitudes, tones, roughness and the 0.12 m nominal tile of the three scales are authored choices and do not claim to match any cauliflower cultivar, and it is not a true fractal (only three layers are added).

Each scale sums `smooth(1 − q/r²)` bud domes (r = 0.62 cell) over the 3×3 neighbour cells, the three layers add with amplitudes 1, 0.45 and 0.2, and `H/(1+0.12H)` saturates the height; color uses `H/(1+H)` so it stays within [0,1], AO is `1 − 0.55/(1+8H²)`, and everything is C1. This material is an authored schematic of the general look of metal-flake car paint. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; flake size, density, tones, metallic coverage, roughness and the 0.1 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real paint or color code.

A dedicated sampler stores five Float64 values per cell (jittered offset x, y, tilt x, y and tone; a missing flake has tone 0), 20,480 Float64 values for the 64² cells, plus a 128² clear-coat grain of 16,384 Float64 values, for 36,864 Float64 values / 294,912 B of lattice arithmetic in total (not total RAM). Flakes are summed rather than owned: each is a `smooth(1 − q/r²)` dome (radius 0.55 cell, zero value and slope at the rim) over the 3×3 neighbour cells (a flake reaches at most 0.9 cell from its cell centre, which the neighbourhood covers); height is the sum of each dome times `1 + 2·tilt·(tiltX·dx + tiltY·dy)`, so overlaps stay C1. The coverage `S/(1+S)` (S being the weighted sum times flakeGain 1.2) saturates smoothly into color, metallic, roughness and AO without hard clipping. This is why the kind is added to the metallic list in `procedural-material.ts` (metallic factor 1, controlled by the per-sample metallic channel) and to the generic 'non-metal' exception list in the tests. The default 0.1 m nominal tile and 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. My first render used 48 cells, radius 0.78 and presence 0.85, and after viewing it the face was almost entirely silver with no blue base visible, so I changed to 64 cells, radius 0.55, presence 0.5 and flakeGain 1.2. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: metallic>0.3 covers 21.5–22.3%, metallic peaks at 0.671–0.683, bottoms at 0 and averages 0.117–0.121, color is 0.165–0.748, height runs from 0.25 to 1.31–1.38 relief, roughness is 0.052–0.12, minimum AO is 0.932 and the color–metallic correlation is about 0.999; the flake masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 33.3% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/b is about (73, 113), the mean metallic channel is 30.3/255 with 21.9% above 76 and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.351. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('metalflakepaint', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 1 and the per-pixel metallic channel sets the flake metalness, and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`. Use at least size 512 so each flake spans several pixels.

`tapemeasure` adds a tape measure, bringing the current catalog from 911 to 912 kinds (913 gallery choices including plain). One tile is a 100 mm segment of yellow tape: 100 millimetre ticks (0.2 of the tile height long), a longer tick every 5 mm (0.3) and the longest, thicker tick every 10 mm (0.42), all near-black and hanging from 0.08 below the band edge; the cross-section is a cosine bow with raised rims and a concave centre, so the glossy coat has a lengthwise normal gradient. It has no numerals, imperial scale, end hook, case or wear.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a metric tape measure. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; tick lengths and widths, the yellow, the bow depth, roughness and the 0.1 m nominal tile (exactly one 100 mm segment) are authored choices and do not claim to match any real tape standard or accuracy class.

A dedicated sampler finds the nearest tick with `k = round(u·100)` and picks the length by the k 1/5/10 mm hierarchy; ink = `smooth(1 − d²/w²)` times 0.004 top and bottom ramps, zero beyond the tick width, so the nearest-tick ownership change at half a millimetre never jumps; the bow height is `0.1 + 0.55·(0.5+0.5cos 2πv)`, with zero slope at both rims, so it is C1 across tiles, and the rims carry AO (at most 0.25). The cache is only a 64² paper/coat grain (4,096 Float64 values / 32,768 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). Color is pigment, ink height is 0.04 relief; metallic is 0 (a painted tape) and there is no mortar. The default 0.1 m nominal tile and 0.03 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices; I first used 0.01, then saw the normals were too flat and raised it to 0.03. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: at v = tickTop + 0.1 all 100 ticks are dark (color 0.016–0.043) and color between ticks is at least 0.886; at lengths 0.25 / 0.35 there are 20 / 10 dark ticks and 0 beyond the longest; overall color is 0.016–0.915, height 0.100–0.653 relief, AO 0.75–1 and roughness 0.375–0.544; in the seed-7 512² maps the mean r/g/b is about (217, 185, 35), yellow pixels (r>180, g>150, b<70) cover 94.3%, r<100 covers 4.3% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.111. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('tapemeasure', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`. Use at least size 512 so millimetre ticks are about one pixel wide.

`ledmatrix` adds an LED dot-matrix panel, bringing the current catalog from 910 to 911 kinds (912 gallery choices including plain). A 48×48 grid of round LEDs split into 8×6 character cells (5×7 LEDs plus one blank column and row each); each cell lights 2–4 random short horizontal, vertical or diagonal strokes by seed (pseudo-glyphs, not a font); lit LEDs are bright red-orange, unlit ones dark red, the LED lenses are smooth and slightly domed and the black plate is rougher with AO. It is not a real font or readable text, scrolling animation, emission, color mixing or RGB sub-pixels.

This material is an authored schematic of the general structure of an LED dot-matrix display panel. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; the LED count, character-cell size, stroke generation rule, tones, roughness, AO and the 0.16 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real product.

A dedicated sampler draws strokes per character cell from `hash` by seed at construction into a 2,304-entry Uint8 lit table, plus 2,304 Float64 brightness jitters (2,304 B + 18,432 B = 20,736 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). At sample time each LED owns its square cell; the lens is `smooth(1 − q/r²)` with r = 0.46 < 0.5, zero (value and slope) at the cell boundary, so lit/unlit tone changes never jump at a seam, and the black plate shows between lenses. Color is pigment (there is no emission), lit LEDs add a 0.1 lens highlight tone; height only feeds the normal and AO; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. The default 0.16 m nominal tile and 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. I first set litTone to 0.88; probing showed lit LED color reaching 1.0199 (outside [0,1]), so I lowered it to 0.84, after which lit LED color is 0.900–0.980. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: lit fraction 12.9–14.1%, lit LED color 0.900–0.980, unlit LED 0.150–0.170, lens height 1.0 relief / plate 0, lens roughness 0.17 / plate 0.62, plate AO 0.55 / lens 1, plate color 0.02; the lit masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 21.5% of LEDs; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r is 48.0, r>160 covers 3.07%, AO<200 covers 67.6% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.413. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('ledmatrix', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`. Use at least size 512 so each LED is about 10 pixels.

`barcodelabel` adds a barcode label, bringing the current catalog from 909 to 910 kinds (911 gallery choices including plain). One tile is a full label width: 10-module quiet zones on both sides, a Code 128 Start B pattern (11 modules), nine data symbols (each six alternating bar/space widths of 1–4 modules summing to 11) and a 13-module stop pattern, 143 modules in total; the bars occupy only the v 0.1–0.9 label band with blank paper above and below. Near-black toner (slightly raised and smoother) is printed on bright rough paper with a fine paper-fibre grain. It is not a decodable Code 128: the data symbols are seed-chosen random widths with no check symbol and without the parity rule (bar widths summing to even, space widths to odd), and there is no human-readable text, other label elements or curvature.

The structure follows the actually read [Wikipedia “Code 128”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_128): each symbol is three black bars and three white spaces of 1–4 modules each summing to 11 modules and starting with a bar and ending with a space; the stop pattern is 13 modules including a final 2-module bar; the quiet zone is at least 10 modules on each side. The Start B bit pattern `11010010000` and the stop pattern `1100011101011` that I use come from my recollection of the standard's symbol table; the text extracted from that page did not include the tables, so those two bit strings are **not verified by the page**. The appearance (black bars on white paper, 0.14 m tile, toner height, roughness, paper color) is authored, with no specific label photograph or measurement cited.

A dedicated sampler, at construction, draws nine symbols from `hash` by seed (five widths of 1–4 each, the sixth derived from the sum of 11 and required to fall in 1–4, retried up to 4,096 times and falling back to the Start B widths on failure) into a 143-module bit array; at sample time x = fract(u)·143 finds the module and each bar edge blends over ±`edgeRamp/2` = 0.11 module with `smooth` (zero slope at both ends, hence C1), and the label band edges use a 0.012 `smooth` ramp. The cache is a 96² paper-fibre grain (9,216 Float64 values / 73,728 B) plus a 143-entry module-bit array. Color is pigment; toner has height 0.35 relief and paper grain at most 0.1; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. The default 0.14 m nominal tile and 0.0006 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: color<0.5 covers 30.1–34.8%, the lowest color is 0.0276, the highest 0.982, mean toner height is about 0.39 relief versus about 0.055 for paper and roughness spans 0.445–0.575; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r is 173.3, r<128 covers 31.1% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0036. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('barcodelabel', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`. Use at least size 512 so each module is about three pixels.

`topographicmap` adds topographic contour paper, bringing the current catalog from 908 to 909 kinds (910 gallery choices including plain). On warm off-white paper, constant-width brown contour lines are printed over a terrain made of seven integer-wavenumber sinusoids (16 contour levels, every fifth an index contour that is heavier and darker), with a very faint elevation tint and fine paper-fibre grain; the ink sits slightly above the paper. It is not real terrain data, elevation labels, rivers, roads, a grid or legend text.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a contour map. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; level count, index interval, line width, ink and paper colors and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real map specification or scale.

A dedicated sampler sums seven integer-wavenumber sinusoids (seed-chosen phases, ±20% amplitude jitter) into a periodic analytic (C∞) terrain; the contour distance `sin²(πd)/π² ÷ (levels·|∇|)²` converts level distance to squared UV distance (|∇| has a 0.4 floor so summits and saddles stay smooth), so line width does not widen on flat ground; line = `smooth(1 − distance²/width²)` and the index weight is `((1+cos(2πd/5))/2)^6`, so width and ink are C∞. The cache is a 128² paper-fibre grain plus 7 phases and 7 amplitudes, 16,398 Float64 values / 131,184 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment; ink has height 0.6 relief and paper grain at most 0.15; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. The default 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0015 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: color<0.7 (including edge falloff) covers 9.3–10.5%, color<0.45 covers 6.7–7.6%, the lowest color is 0.14 (index ink), the highest 0.925–0.930, the mean 0.839–0.846 and mean ink height is about 0.575 relief versus about 0.077 for paper; the ink masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 17.6% of pixels; the seed-7 512² mean base color is about (222, 206, 180), b<170 covers 10.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.111. I viewed the first render and confirmed the line width looks consistent on both flat and steep ground before settling. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('topographicmap', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`. Use at least size 512 so thin lines span one to two pixels.

`eastindianrosewood` adds East Indian rosewood, bringing the current catalog from 907 to 908 kinds (909 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished longitudinal Dalbergia latifolia face: a deep purplish-brown ground, five darker near-black undulating streaks, fine longitudinal fibre grain and scattered short open-vessel pits (about 1.2%). It is not a golden-brown pale face, white sapwood, a polished surface, interlocked/wavy figure or oily luster.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database East Indian Rosewood](https://www.wood-database.com/east-indian-rosewood/) (Color/Appearance: heartwood from golden brown to deep purplish brown with darker blackish streaks, darkening with age to a deep brown) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/dalbergia-latifolia-1-300x600.jpg) (a deep brown, purple-tinged longitudinal face with darker streaks and fine pores). These are color and grain-form references only: the golden-brown variation, pale sapwood and real vessel distribution are not reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or physical size is not inferred from the photograph.

It reuses the existing Padauk/Bloodwood-family long elliptical vessel sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `blackwalnut`, `teak`, `honduranmahogany` and `shagbarkhickory`); only the constructor selects the preset: a 40×14 vessel-site table (17,920 B), five strongly undulating (bandWarp 0.8), high-contrast (bandContrast 0.45) dark bands, a 220×9 longitudinal fibre field, 128² fine grain and the fixed 3×4 warp table, totalling 20,616 Float64 values / 164,928 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0; the vessel pits are real height depressions while color streaks are pigment. The default 0.18 m nominal tile and 0.0025 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid, vessels cover 1.18–1.22%, body color spans 0.255–0.908, the across/along color-difference ratio is 8.6–10.2, roughness is 0.460–0.564 and height is 0.42–0.503 relief; the seed-7 512² mean base color is about (97, 61, 49), vessels cover 1.18% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0052. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('eastindianrosewood', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`lenticularsheet` adds a lenticular print sheet, bringing the current catalog from 906 to 907 kinds (908 gallery choices including plain). 32 parallel cylindrical lenses per tile (long strips along v), glossy smooth bright crests and low rougher seams with AO (0.65) between lenses; the blue-silver base is a diagonal 'flip' stripe (2 cycles per lens, 3 cycles along v) combined with an 8×8 low-frequency printed image. It is not a real interlaced multi-frame image, view-dependent animation, lens refraction or a readable picture.

This material is an authored schematic of the general structure of a lenticular print sheet. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; lens count, tones, flip stripe, roughness, AO and the 0.1 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real product or optical specification.

A dedicated sampler uses f = fract(u·32) per lens; lens height = 0.5 − 0.5·cos(2πf) (zero slope at crest and seam, so it is C1 across lenses); the flip stripe is sin(2π(2f + 3v)) (integer cycles so it wraps with the tile), plus an 8×8 cachedNoise low-frequency image (64 Float64 values / 512 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). Color is pigment, height only feeds the normal and AO; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. The default 0.1 m nominal tile and 0.008 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid: crest height 1.0 relief, seam 0.1, crest roughness 0.1, seam 0.4, crest AO 1, seam 0.65; color spans about 0.094–0.902; the across/along color-difference ratio is about 21.0–21.1; the flip along a lens crest sweeps from 0.25–0.30 up to 0.87–0.90; the mean image color difference between seeds 0 and 1 is 0.070; in the seed-7 512² maps the mean blue channel is 179.1, AO<230 covers 37.5% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.323. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`europeanlarch` adds European larch, bringing the current catalog from 905 to 906 kinds (907 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished flatsawn Larix decidua face: a pale pink-brown / pale yellow-tan earlywood ground, 12 flowing reddish-brown latewood ring lines (moderately wide, about a quarter of the area, curving and undulating with arches) and fine longitudinal fibre grain. It is not resin pockets, knots, the narrow near-white sapwood/heartwood boundary, spiral grain or a finish.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database European Larch](https://www.wood-database.com/european-larch/) (Color/Appearance: heartwood from yellow to medium reddish brown, narrow nearly white sapwood clearly demarcated from heartwood, flatsawn sections showing interesting growth-ring patterns; Grain/Texture: generally straight or spiraled, medium to fine texture with a greasy feel) and the actually downloaded and viewed [flatsawn photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/european-larch-s-400x400.jpg) (pale pink-tan face with flowing reddish-brown ring lines and arches). These are color and grain-form references only: the sapwood/heartwood boundary, knots and greasy luster are not reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or physical size is not inferred from the photograph. During development I first set warp to 1.4, which rendered closed swirling loops unlike the photograph; after viewing it I lowered it to 0.55 with 12 rings and arch 2.2, which is still more regular than the photograph but closer to its flowing arches.

It reuses the `douglasfir` ring-index sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `longleafpine`, `westernredcedar` and `sitkaspruce`); only the constructor selects the preset (rings 12, arch 2.2, warp 0.55, latewood 0.45–0.9, lateTone 0.52, earlyTone 0.86); a 36-value warp table plus a 180×6 fibre field and 128² fine grain total 17,500 Float64 values / 140,000 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0, latewood is slightly higher and ring color is pigment. The default 0.2 m nominal tile and 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid, latewood-colored points (color<0.6) cover 25.7–26.5%, earlywood-colored points (>0.75) 62.6–63.6%, the color range is 0.316–0.907, roughness 0.531–0.610, height 0.498–0.662 relief and the across/along color-difference ratio 2.84–2.88; in the seed-7 512² maps g≥165 covers 69.9%, g<165 covers 30.1%, the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.028 and the mean base color is about (220, 176, 142). No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`monitorlizardskin` adds a monitor-lizard-style granular scaly skin, bringing the current catalog from 903 to 904 kinds (905 gallery choices including plain). A 14-column × 16-row hex-packed grid of round raised scales (odd rows shifted by half a column), each with its own tone (standard deviation about 0.09–0.10), slightly brighter and smoother, separated by narrow deep dark grooves (AO 0.4, color 0.04, roughness 0.7); four transverse light/dark bands undulate along v, in olive brown. It is not a specific species' scale shapes, size zones, spots or rings, and has no ventral scutes, dorsal crest or skin folds.

This material is an authored schematic of a generic coarse granular monitor-lizard skin. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; the introduction of [Wikipedia “Monitor lizard”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monitor_lizard) that I read describes genus, range and body size but not skin, so scale size, tones, bands, roughness, AO and the 0.14 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real species or specimen.

A dedicated sampler finds the nearest scale centre on a hex-packed grid (odd rows shifted by half a column, searching the row above, the row itself and the row below); scale = `smooth(1 − q/r²)` with r = 0.5, the hex Voronoi inradius, so a scale reaches zero before ownership changes (the per-scale tone lookup therefore creates no jump), with zero slope at the centre and rim. A 14×16 table (224 per-scale tone Float64 values) plus a 160² fine grain total 25,824 Float64 values / 206,592 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). An even row count makes the stagger parity and the four transverse bands wrap with the tile. Metallic is 0 and there is no mortar; the default is a 0.14 m nominal tile and 0.01 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement). I first tried radius 0.48 and a 0.9 vertical flattening, but flattening left non-zero jumps at the ownership boundary, so the final version is isotropic with radius 0.5. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: scale-crown height 0.780–0.795 relief, AO 1, color 0.336–0.701 and roughness 0.550–0.609; the groove halfway to the same-row neighbour has height 0.08, AO 0.4, color 0.04 and roughness 0.7; per-scale tone standard deviation is 0.090–0.099. In the seed-7 512² maps mean r is 67.9, AO<180 covers 55.3%, r<50 covers 39.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.17. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('monitorlizardskin', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`. Use at least size 256 so each scale has several pixels.

`honduranmahogany` adds Honduran mahogany, bringing the current catalog from 901 to 902 kinds (903 gallery choices including plain). `chesterfieldleather` adds Chesterfield diamond-tufted brown leather, bringing the current catalog from 889 to 890 kinds (891 gallery choices including plain). A 6×6-cell tile carries a small button at every other cell centre (18 per tile), joined by diagonal pleats around puffed diamond cushions; pleats are dark with low AO and cushion crowns are lighter and smoother, over fine brown leather grain and low-frequency creases. It is not real furniture scale or any specific product's geometry, and has no metal button faces, stitching, cracked leather or transparent holes.

This material is an authored schematic of generic diamond-tufted leather. No specific source document, product photograph or measurement is cited, so it does not claim to match any real furniture, button pitch, leather type or color; colors, roughness, AO, relief layers and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices.

A dedicated sampler uses two diagonal coordinates `a=u·N+v·N−1` and `b=u·N−v·N` and takes the signed distances `da`/`db` to the nearest even integers; `smooth(clamp(|d|/pillowSpan))` has zero slope on the fold lines, and the product forms the diamond cushions while staying C1. Buttons are smoothstep domes from the distance to the nearest even lattice point. N must be even for the tile to wrap. Constructor caches are a 128² grain and a 24² crease field, 16,960 Float64 values / 135,680 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0 and there is no mortar; the default is a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.012 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement). Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: cushion crowns are 0.688–0.717 relief high, fold lines about 0.08 and buttons about 0.30; fold AO is 0.5 and crown AO is 1; the seed-7 512² mean base color is about (108, 55, 33), 35.3% of pixels have AO<160 and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.040. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('chesterfieldleather', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`longleafpine` adds longleaf-pine growth-ring grain, bringing the current catalog from 888 to 889 kinds (890 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished Pinus palustris face: pale yellow-white earlywood with narrow high-contrast orange-brown latewood stripes in nearly parallel, gently undulating rings. It is not resin canals, knots, an all-reddish-brown heartwood face, a finish, or Douglas-fir-style large pointed arches.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database Longleaf Pine](https://www.wood-database.com/longleaf-pine/) (Color/Appearance: reddish-brown heartwood and yellowish-white sapwood; Grain/Texture: straight, fine to medium; Endgrain: large, numerous, evenly distributed resin canals, abrupt earlywood-to-latewood transition and high color contrast) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/longleaf-pine.jpg) (pale yellow-white ground with parallel orange-brown latewood stripes). These are color and stripe-shape references only: no source image is shipped and true color, roughness or physical size is not inferred from the photograph.

It reuses the `douglasfir` ring-index sampler by fallthrough; only the constructor selects the preset. More rings, a very small longitudinal arch and skew, a wider latewood darkening ramp and stronger latewood color difference produce nearly parallel stripes. The three constructor caches are a 5×5 warp, a 192×5 longitudinal fiber field and 128² grain (17,369 Float64 values / 138,952 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). Metallic is 0 and there is no mortar; latewood is slightly raised and smoother and earlywood has slightly lower AO. The default 0.12 m nominal tile and 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid, color<0.4 latewood covers 21.1–24.0% and color>0.75 earlywood 52.7–55.9%, with an across/along color-difference ratio of 12.0–12.9 and latewood about 0.19 relief above earlywood; the seed-7 512² mean base color is about (232, 186, 125) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.030. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('longleafpine', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`douglasfir` adds flatsawn Douglas-fir, bringing the current catalog from 887 to 888 kinds (889 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished flatsawn longitudinal Pseudotsuga menziesii face: light orange-tan earlywood, darker orange-brown latewood growth rings, with multiple pointed cathedral arches around larger concentric ovals. It is not a knot, resin pocket or canal, sapwood/heartwood boundary, finished surface, or quartersawn straight parallel rings.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database Douglas-Fir](https://www.wood-database.com/douglas-fir/) (Color/Appearance: light brown with a hint of red and/or yellow and darker growth rings, wild grain in flatsawn pieces; Grain/Texture: generally straight or slightly wavy, medium to coarse; Identification: small to medium, infrequent resin canals and an abrupt earlywood-to-latewood transition) and the actually downloaded and viewed [flatsawn specimen photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/pseudotsuga-menziesii.jpg) (nested arched rings and one small knot). These are color and ring-shape references only: no source image is shipped, the knot is not reproduced, and true color, roughness or physical size is not inferred from the photograph.

A dedicated sampler (not a fallthrough to the vessel sampler) builds a smooth periodic ring-index field from cosine terms — a transverse term, a longitudinal arch term, an oblique skew and a seeded low-frequency warp — and takes fract() through a smoothstep ring profile whose value and slope are zero at both ends (a wide earlywood-to-latewood darkening followed by an abrupt return to earlywood), so the tile stays periodic and C1. Latewood is slightly raised and smoother; earlywood has slightly lower AO; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. The three constructor caches are a 5×5 warp, a 160×5 longitudinal fiber field and 128² grain (17,209 Float64 values / 137,672 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). The default 0.2 m nominal tile and 0.0035 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid, color<0.4 latewood covers 15.2% and color>0.75 earlywood 70.5–70.9%, with an across/along color-difference ratio of 2.95–3.09; the seed-7 512² mean base color is about (214, 165, 107) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.049. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('douglasfir', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()`; the metallic factor is 0 and cleanup uses the existing `destroy()`.

`blackwalnut` adds a dark chocolate-brown black walnut flatsawn face, bringing the current catalog from 886 to 887 kinds (888 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished flatsawn longitudinal Juglans nigra heartwood face: medium-dark chocolate brown, darker long longitudinal streaks, straight to gently undulating grain and sparse short open-vessel pits. It is not purple/grey cast, sapwood, curl/burl/birdseye/crotch figure or a finished surface, and it has no semi-ring-porous earlywood-to-latewood vessel-size gradient: the pits are uniform stylized marks.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database Black Walnut](https://www.wood-database.com/black-walnut/) (Color/Appearance: pale to dark chocolate brown with darker streaks; Grain/Texture: usually straight but can be irregular, medium texture, moderate natural luster; Porosity: semi-ring-porous) and the actually downloaded and viewed [flatsawn full-board scan](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/juglans-nigra-full.jpg). They are color and grain-direction references only: no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or physical size is not inferred from the photograph.

It reuses the existing Padauk/Bloodwood-family long elliptical vessel sampler by fallthrough; only the constructor selects the preset: a 40×14 vessel-site table (four Float64 per site, 17,920 B), four warped bands, a 192×9 longitudinal fiber field and 128² fine grain. Metallic is 0 and AO drops only at vessels; the pits are real height depressions while longitudinal color streaks are pigment, not raised relief. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`to92packagefaces` adds four rotated/jittered 2×2 TO-92 front schematics, bringing the current catalog from 885 to 886 kinds (887 gallery choices including plain). Matte-black D-shaped bodies have straight sides, flat bottoms and upper elliptical domes; three equally spaced parallel straight neutral-metal leads have broad root shoulders and narrow tails, with roots masked by the body. No exposed tab, mounting hole or markings are drawn. Full leads have M1; body/backing have M0, with C1 boundary blends. Authored normalized heights are backing .02 < lead .44 < body .68.

The dimension reference is the actually downloaded and raster-viewed [onsemi P2N2222A/D, January 2013 Rev. 7, PDF page 6](https://www.onsemi.com/pdf/datasheet/p2n2222a-d.pdf#page=6): embedded drawing 98ASB42022B, TO-92 (TO-226), CASE 29-11, Issue AM, dated 09 MAR 2007, drawing page 1 of 2, STRAIGHT LEAD BULK PACK view. Its A 4.45–5.20 mm, B 4.32–5.33 mm, G 1.15–1.39 mm and K ≥12.70 mm are dimension references only, not measurements of the artwork. The upper half ellipse, proportions, shoulders, color, roughness, AO and heights are authored simplifications, not exact CAD. No chemistry, plating, optical or electrical properties are inferred; no source artwork is shipped.

Defaults are a 0.08 m nominal tile, 0.0042 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 1. Explicit `createMaterial({ metallic: 0 })` changes only the scalar factor, not the stored M mask. The TO-220 constructor-cached pose/grain and C1 role-replacement structure is reused, preserving periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership without new APIs or dependencies. Remove borrowed materials before destroying the texture-owning preset; manage caller-owned pools/caches separately. Prefer 512 for the three narrow tails; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim runtime/browser verification.

Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('to92packagefaces', { size: 512, seed: 7, heightMap: true })`, then `createMaterial()` for the default lead metal factor; explicit `createMaterial({ metallic: 0 })` retains the stored mask and existing texture cleanup.

`ftypefemalefaces` adds four 2×2 bare F-type female bulkhead front schematics, bringing the catalog from 883 to 884 kinds: six-flat nickel-plated metal hex bases, concentric raised round shoulders, CLOSED unkeyed raised circular lips, pale P.P. dielectric disks and tiny deeper dark opaque central female entries. Exterior hardware has M1; backing, P.P. and entries have M0. Authored normalized height order is backing .02 < entry .06 < nut .26 < shoulder .36 < P.P. .48 < lip .66. The entry is a height depression, not a painted dot; pale P.P. remains continuous around it. Unlike ST, there is no open keyway or bayonet stud, and no male pin or invented visible central metal contact ring.

The primary reference is the actually downloaded and raster-viewed historical [Amphenol Connex CAT-103 ©2001 catalog, PDF page 159 / printed page 158](https://docs.rs-online.com/1ab7/A700000006717073.pdf#page=159): the 222121 BULKHEAD ADAPTER JACK-TO-JACK photograph, drawing and model-specific Nickel / P.P. / 75Ω table. Generic Delrin/Teflon notes elsewhere do not override this model's P.P.; neither base-alloy chemistry nor exact contact material is inferred. The drawing's 11 HEX and 21.3 mm axial overall length are references, not measured front geometry; washer/nut side dimensions are not front height. The tiny actual entry cross-section is unresolved at source-photo resolution: its circular form here is a deliberate artist simplification, not exact CAD. Proportions, color, roughness, AO, layer heights, default 0.04 m tile and 0.0042 UV-relief factor are authored; .0042 is not metres or a calibrated depth. No thread helix/decorative thread turns, washer teeth, rear/cable/PCB, real holes, transparency or new mesh; no RF/75Ω, electrical, optical, mating or safety simulation/certification. Historical 75Ω identifies the part only. Source assets are not bundled; this extends the existing `pbr3d` gallery, not a new examples entry.

The independent 46-field preset (44 numeric fields and two palettes) uses ten C1 profiles: six smooth hex half-planes and four squared-radius circle profiles. Nested convex role replacement and 20 constructor-cached C/H/R/AO deltas avoid nonzero hard-min/max joins. Four four-column Float64 poses (128 B) plus 96² Float64 grain (73,728 B) retain 73,856 B typed-array payload, excluding JS object/closure overhead—not total RAM, FPS or a performance improvement claim. The rotation-independent owner bound, maxScale × nutInradius / (sqrt(3)/2) + jitter, is approximately .369958 < .5. Constructor-cached poses/grain leave no query allocation, loop, hash, trigonometry or square root; zero support and unused grain on full P.P./entry/backing are skipped. The second fractional wrap before owner indexing is retained for tiny negative UVs. Default metallic is 1; explicit `createMaterial({ metallic: 0 })` changes only the factor, not the stored hardware/nonmetal mask. Existing opaque four maps, optional height, tint/repeats and sync/Worker/cache APIs and ownership remain unchanged: remove borrowing materials before disposing the texture-owning preset, and manage caller-owned pools/caches separately. No new dependency or API. These are source/implementation descriptions, not full-suite, runtime, browser or built-distribution verification claims.

Starting at (16,16) facing up on an all-white unbounded plane, this offline trajectory ends at (8,8) facing down, with 122 black/226 visited cells. Its entire x=5–24, y=6–22 trajectory stays inside the 32-cell frame. Runtime stores only 32 row bitmaps and the final direction vector, not a simulator or copied image. Each sampler retains one 96² Float64 grain lattice (73,728 B typed storage, excluding JS data/output maps), with O(1) bitmap lookup, allocation-free sampling, no repeated hashes and generic detail bypassed. From the quadratic roots, the authored implementation derives b′ = 2Σ(other b) − b and (bz)′ = 2Σ(other bz) − bz, starting with a negative enclosing circle and three equal inner circles. `deltoidaltrihexagonaltiles` adds an authored deltoidal trihexagonal (V3.4.6.4) tiling: the hexagon of points nearest to each point of a triangular lattice is cut into six kites by six spokes to its side midpoints, and the kites around a point take burgundy, rose and ivory glaze in turn, so the three kites of every lattice triangle also differ; the kites sit in bevelled glaze over rougher gray grout, and every straight edge lies on one of six parallel line families 30° apart. `monkscloth` approximates a selected natural-cream coarse four-by-four Monk’s Cloth. `basswood` approximates a selected finely sanded unfinished longitudinal Tilia americana face: uniform pale cream/light tan color, low-contrast long straight grain and shallow micrograin, not every Tilia species, endgrain anatomy, coarse dark vessels, transverse curl, knots, coating or species identification. The Wood Database account and both raw/finished photographs were actually read/viewed; only the raw appearance is selected. Each point retains two cached lookups with no new allocation, hash, trigonometry, square root, kind branch or neighbor scan; no unused zero-curl Anigre fields, third cache or second synthesizer are added. `sphericalwashers` approximates selected silver form-C-style stainless spherical washers as complete circular annuli intentionally flipped convex seating-face up. The normally upward flat bearing face, mating D/G conical seats, outward-rising straight cup-washer walls and three-wave spring washers are different surfaces. The actually viewed Halder stainless product photograph and section identify the spherical face on the underside in normal assembly; this preset explicitly reverses its display orientation instead of mislabeling the flat top as convex. Twenty-five fixed-center owners cache only per-ring tones and 128² grain, totaling 16,409 Float64 values / 131,272 bytes of field-table arithmetic, not total RAM or texture-cache size. Following the existing annular squared-radius C1 shoulders, lower opaque dielectric backing and cachedNoise conventions, the true spherical profile uses sqrt(R²-q), not a paraboloid, inverted cup cone or torus. This genuinely different geometry keeps a short independent case rather than adding profile dispatch or another closure to the old cup hot path. Only nonempty metal faces require one necessary square root and one grain lookup; no point allocation, hashing, trigonometry or neighbor scan is added. R 0.54 exceeds outer radius 0.36, leaving a spherical radicand of at least 0.162 throughout support and 0.14 clearance to the 0.5 owner half-width. Grain affects pigment/roughness only, not carved concentric grooves. The continuous inward-high/outward-low metal face is M1, round bores/backing M0, with coherent C1 partial coverage and AO 0.3/0.95; actual default/createMaterial factor 1 preserves authored B. The authored 0.10 m nominal tile and 0.025 UV relief are not DIN dimensions or measured thickness. Four opaque default maps and optional height retain options, tint, Worker/cache, repeats and ownership. No mesh holes, knurled sidewalls, transparency, mating-part reconstruction, tilt compensation, clamping/contact mechanics, grade/corrosion/hardness/load/DIN certification or photograph bundle is added.

A maximum half-length of 0.32 stays within the 0.5 owner half-width with 0.18 clearance; foreground sampling retains two cached lookups and an early lower-opaque-backing return, with no new point allocation, hash, trigonometry, square root, kind branch or neighbor scan. `ramie` approximates a selected natural off-white Ramie plain-weave swatch: equally dense fine warp/weft yarns, alternating 1/1 crossing lifts, fine longitudinal fibers and lower dark opaque backing. `eudialyte` approximates interlocking angular dark-raspberry fragments, black matrix and fine dark intergrain contacts in a selected cabochon. A 0.12 m tile has 8×8 owners with two independent seeded sites each: 384 cached center-x/center-y/baked-pigment values plus 192² grain, totaling 37,248 Float64 values / 297,984 bytes. Existing compact weighted-crystal, Howlite squared-weight-overlap and cachedNoise conventions are reused: sites in 0.2–0.8 and radius-1.18 cap¹⁶ weights normalize over 3×3 owners / 18 sites. The worst own-site squared distance 1.28 is below support² 1.3924, so total weight and its square stay strictly positive without epsilon or a fake fallback; omitted sites cannot enter before distance 1.2, after support vanishes. sum(weight²)/sum(weight)² through a smooth 0.50–0.56 shoulder creates fine dark contacts without nearest-owner/max/min junction creases; fine noise multiplicatively varies pigment and supplies micrograin. A shared reciprocal normalizes pigment and overlap. Each point uses one grain lookup and a fixed local site search, without allocations, hashing, sqrt or trig. Pigment classes are selected once in the constructor, not by a UV hard threshold; shared detail is bypassed. No false parallel crystal ribs are added: fragments and matrix share one fine-micrograin polished plane with AO 1 / M0 / mortar 0 / factor 0, without carving intergrain contacts into cavities. Opaque maps, optional height, tint, workers, cache, repeats and ownership are unchanged. A 0.00012 UV relief is not metre-valued geometry displacement; no transparent refraction, complete mineral proportions, chemical/origin/identification, healing or radiation-safety certification is added.

`larvikite` approximates a polished dark-grey Larvikite face with sparse static blue-grey feldspar flashes and grain-local parallel tonal traces.
